In the Tangle of Life

[Serial novel — "In the Tangle of Life"; instalment 7.]
(A novel with dramatic events in Kraków, Zawiercie and New York) 7)
Years passed; there was a world war. During the war David made money in America. From the very first day he did not want to go to work, only to trade. At first he toiled, worked in a shop, then opened a shop himself and made good money.
Once, already after the war, in the year 1920, he was at a protest meeting about the attacks on Jews that were taking place at the time. To his great surprise he saw Bernard there. He went up to him, greeted him and asked whether he knew anything of Nechama and the child and where they were now.
"Right here in New York," Bernard answered him, "and your little daughter Emma you won't recognise — she is already a young lady of 16."
"And you married Nechama?" David asked with a pounding heart.
"What is the matter with you? You still haven't freed yourself of the old suspicion; Nechama was innocent."
And he told him how she had tried to commit suicide right after the divorce.
"But you did love each other, both of you," David said to him.
"A pity that Nechama is so proud and that you know her so little," Bernard answered, "though she was your [?] wife. It may be true that I had a certain feeling for her, but she allowed nothing at all; the rest she will tell you herself, if she wishes."
"You mean to say that you wanted to marry her and she refused you?"
"More than once."
"Why?"
"Because she told me that she loves you, although you were in such a hurry to divorce her."
"And how did they come here?"
"With me."
"With you?"
"Yes, I was going to America, so I didn't want to leave them there alone."
"And you simply supported them and paid their expenses, just like that?"
"Just like that! Even a little more than the expenses! Over there they didn't even have anything to eat; you, after all, did not care at all even about your daughter."
"Can I see them?"
"I will ask them first; give me your telephone, and I'll ring you tomorrow morning."
The next day Bernard rang him that he could come to the house.
When David came to the house, the reception was very cold, both from Nechama and from the daughter, but Bernard soon intervened.
"Nechama, you are too proud, and being too proud does no good. I'll let out a secret: Nechama was in seventh heaven with happiness today when I told her that I had found you. Nechama, stop playing theatre, don't put on a proud front, be sincere, the way you really are — and you too, Emma!"
And Bernard's words had their effect.
It did not take long before David and Nechama drew close again; they began to meet often, and David became a frequent guest at Nechama's and their daughter Emma's.
And once, when Bernard came in, Emma ran towards him.
"Bernard, I have important news for you! Father got married to Mother today!"
"Mazel tov!" said Bernard.
"For the third time under the wedding canopy with one's own wife — isn't that heroic?" David smiled.
Two years passed of a truly happy life together for David and Nechama. David also introduced his wife to Malkale, and both women became great friends.
But something began to happen to Nechama. She began to be ill, and it was noticed when it was already too late.
Nechama now knew that her days were numbered; nevertheless she did not put on any sad expression.
But it did not take long before she could no longer get up from bed; she called David over and said to him:
"Now, I believe, it is high time to tell you everything. Take out of my bag a black notebook — I always carry it with me — there you will find a whole set of accounts; it is a bookkeeping of kisses. You will learn that I kissed not only Bernard, but others too. But for every kiss I received, for the students' fund [?], a sum that came to 5 dollars. It actually began with Bernard: he once told me he wanted me to give him a kiss, and I said: I'll do it — first give me 20 francs for the students' fund. And so it went; often [?] I let others kiss me too and gave the money to the students' fund. You will find an exact account of everything there — I was never unfaithful to you!"
"Why didn't you tell me then?"
"Perhaps I should have done so, but my pride did not allow me."
At these words she groaned, and not long afterwards she breathed her last.
"Only now have I come to know you, Nechama!" David wept quietly at the deathbed.
The next day was the funeral; everyone was broken, everyone wept, but not David — it was a wonder, no one could understand it.
When the grave had been filled in and everyone had left, a shot was suddenly heard. David had shot himself on his wife's grave.
Next to him a note was found: "Lay me beside her, although I was not worthy of her."
(To be continued).
First the Father Vanished, Then the Mother — and They Left 4 Small Children Abandoned

[Będzin — Welfare.]
At Kołłątaja 45 there lived in a cellar room a certain Dawid Narengus[?], a tailor, with his wife and 4 small children, the youngest of whom is two and a half years old.
One fine morning the father vanished, leaving his family abandoned. Some time later the wife received word that her "intended" had once again said "harei at" [i.e. married another woman] in Częstochowa, and she went off, ostensibly to look for him — and she too never came back to her children, who as a result suffered terrible want.
Jews being, after all, compassionate sons of compassionate ones, they see to it that the children do not go hungry: they eat breakfast with the Grajcer family, lunch with the Grosman family and supper with the Szpigelman family.
The youngest child, however, forcibly quartered himself with the Własnik family, who clothed him and shod him; because of this the little boy is more attached to this couple than to his own parents. The child has only one request of Własnik: that he not drive him back into the damp cellar.
Własnik shows the child "fatherly" love and cuddles him like a real father. As he explained to us, the child will stay with him until his real parents come back.
Hooligan Attack During a Jewish Funeral

[Będzin — Czeladź; Antisemitism.]
On Sunday, on the road to Czeladź, several young hooligans together with a gentile girl came by[?] and threw stones at the people who were returning from Mrs. Gutman's funeral. A stone hit Mr. Icze Bernblat[?] on the head and he was injured.
Fainted from Hunger

[Będzin — Poverty.]
A young Jewish woman came into the office of the "Beys Lekhem" society and asked to be given a loaf of bread. As she uttered these words she fainted. A doctor had to be called to her, who revived the woman.
As it turned out, the woman is [doubtful word — probably: pregnant] and had fainted from hunger.
Jewish Teachers' Association Dissolved

[Zagłębie — Education; Authorities.]
The district court in Sosnowiec considered the motion of the local starostwo (county office) to dissolve the professional association of Jewish teachers in Zagłębie. The starostwo's motion is justified by the fact that communist activists were elected to the board of the teachers' association, [which] threatened public security and order.
The court agreed with the grounds and decided to dissolve the branch of the Jewish teachers' association in Będzin.

Poisoned by Goose Meat.
On Saturday the Salomon family (Plac 3 Maja) suddenly fell seriously ill. The doctor established that the family had been poisoned by eating goose.

Donations for the "Orphanage".
The staff of the firm of Jakub Gutman handed us 100 złoty for the "Orphanage" (Beys Yesoymim) to honour the memory of the late Mrs. Gitl Gutman.
— The firm of Jakubowicz in Będzin donated 25 hats.
— The school headmistress Mrs. Brojra[?] donated several baskets of vegetables from her garden.

Boycott Proclamations.
On the walls of Czeladź proclamations have appeared not to buy from any Jew. The proclamations say that "there is no need to beat, but boycott — yes".
Parnas Rynski Confirmed as President of the Kehilla Council

[Będzin — Kehilla.]
On Wednesday the kehilla board received a communication from the starosta that, on the basis of a rescript of the Ministry for Religious Affairs, Parnas Szlomo Icchak Rejnski [Ryński?] is confirmed as president of the kehilla council.
At the same time the hitherto president, Y. M. Kurland, is released from that office.
Did the Dąbrowa Kehilla President Demand a 500-złoty Bribe? On the Eve of a Sensational Trial in the Local Municipal Court

[Dąbrowa — Rabbinate; Courts.]
As we have already written at the time, the candidate for the Dąbrowa rabbinate, R' Baruch Epsztajn, accused before the starosta the kehilla president in Dąbrowa, Mr. L. Rechnic, of having wanted to demand 500 złoty from Epsztajn in return for helping him at the voivodeship office in the matter of the rabbinate question.
On the basis of the accusation Mr. Epsztajn was brought to court, and the trial took place before the local court.
During the court hearing R' Baruch Epsztajn declared that he would produce witnesses who would confirm the accusation he had made against Mr. Rechnic.
The trial was therefore adjourned, and the following were summoned as witnesses: Messrs. Ławnik[?], Gerszon Rechnic, Chaim Lejb Jungster of Dąbrowa, Mordechaj Lewi and Elimelech Lewi.
The sensational trial will take place on the 28th of this month. For[?] the prosecution, attorney Pawełek[?] will appear.
The Tefillin Thief Discovered

[Będzin — Crime.]
In the previous issue of our paper there was a report on the theft in the Radomsko shtibl in Będzin, where a visitor stole four pairs of tefillin from the students of the "Keter Torah" yeshiva.
Thanks to the report the theft was uncovered: the thief of the tefillin is a certain Almer, who lives on Wiejska Street in Sosnowiec.
Strike of the Ladies' Ready-to-Wear Tailors Still Continues

[Będzin — Labour.]
The strike of the ladies' ready-to-wear (shop) tailors, which broke out 2 weeks ago, still continues. The negotiations so far between the employers and the employees have not yet brought any positive result.
As we are informed, the fine weather is the main reason why the strike still continues, because the shop owners are in no hurry to stock up on autumn clothing.
Sosnowiec — The Election Fair Has Begun

14 lists. — The Chęciny Hasidim are to leave the bloc. — Statement of the Tailors' Guild.
The election fair has officially begun. It has already been established that for the 14 parnassim [kehilla board members] who were to be elected, 14 candidate lists are standing. The remaining lists turned out to be fictitious and were disqualified by the election commission.
In the previous issue of our paper we reported that the Koziegłowy[?] faction had formed a bloc with the Chęciny Hasidim. As we are informed, the Chęciny Hasidim are demanding that the bloc guarantee them a seat on the board for Mr. Grachowiga[?]; if no such guarantee is given, they threaten to leave the bloc.
— The young organization "Torah va-Avodah" is running separately with a list for the first time; the first candidate on the list is Mr. Moshe Windman[?].
— From the Tailors' Guild we have received a communiqué which states that "the guild originally wanted to go together with the general Artisans' Association. But since[?] the board of the Artisans' Association did not want to give the guild an 'honourable place', the Tailors' Guild — which is larger and stronger in numbers than all the Jewish artisans' guilds — decided to give its members a free hand".
A Month-Long Campaign Proclaimed for the Interest-Free Loan Fund

On Sunday evening the board of the Gemilut Hesed [interest-free loan] fund called a larger meeting in connection with the month-long campaign which the board of the fund has proclaimed.
The chairman, Mr. L. Negel[?], reporting on the matter, demonstrated with figures: 1) the enormous benefit of the institution to the broad strata of the Jewish population, and 2) the meagre interest of the members in general and of the guarantors in particular; and in order to improve the situation of the institution, which today is the lifeline for hundreds of Jewish families, Mr. Negel[?] put forward the following proposals: 1) to proceed with the strictest measures to collect the [outstanding?] debts; 2) to recruit new members in the month[-campaign?]; and 3) to carry out properly, in the coming Days of Awe, the traditional "nedarim" [pledges] campaign.
After the discussion, in which the board members Czechowski, Glajtman, Nachemia[?], Sicecki[?] and others took part, the above proposals were adopted.
At the same time an appeal is made to the Jewish public that everyone should take account of the usefulness of the Gemilut Hesed fund — which, incidentally, is one of the finest such funds in Poland — and enrol as a member.
Stolen Objects Found

During the search at the goldsmith Perer's, various gold and silver objects were confiscated, such as candlesticks, small gold watches, tableware and the like, which come from thefts.
The confiscated objects are in the custody of the local examining magistrate.
The Writer I. M. Weissenberg in Zagłębie

The well-known writer I. M. Weissenberg is staying in Zagłębie, conducting a campaign on behalf of his monthly journal "Kritik" and for his new work "In der tifer eybikeyt" ("In Deep Eternity").
The lovers of Yiddish literature in Zagłębie will no doubt help the guest in his campaign.

List 16 of the "Torah va-Avodah" movement is holding the following pre-election meetings: 1) Saturday at 4.30 p.m. in its own premises, Dekerta 13, and 2) Sunday at 11 a.m. in the Mizrachi synagogue.

A Drunkard's Bestial Deed

On Tuesday a certain Sułkowski came to the "Katarzyna" ironworks in a drunken state and made rows. A sharp exchange of words developed between him and a group of workers, which soon turned into blows. At a certain moment Sułkowski grabbed one of the workers by the head and bit off his nose. By decree the Ministry of Commerce has appointed director Laramski[?] as director of the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec.

Before the local district court the trial of Ajzyk[?] Bekermajster took place these days; he was accused of resisting a bailiff (sequestrator) when the latter wanted to take household goods for overdue tax debts.

In the apartment of a certain Ti-Deri [?], an unemployed man in Czeladź, the border guard found: 100 lighters, several kilos of [lighter] flints, razors [?] and other goods smuggled from Germany.

A conference was held at the local labour inspector on the question of raising the wages for public works. Because the workers are demanding an increase of 40 to 60 percent, which the representatives of the Zagłębie local self-governments could not decide on, a delegation was chosen which went to Kielce in order to intervene with the voivode and with the director of the Labour Fund.

The artists of the "Philharmonia" in Łódź are performing "The Dybbuk" today at the Municipal Theatre. The next performance — "The Romanian Wedding".

Experienced election-makers predict that the 14 mandates of the kehilla council will probably be divided among the following lists:
the Zionist-Mizrachist Bloc will get 3 mandates
Agudas Yisroel — 2 "

Artisans' Association — 2 "

Chęciny Hasidim — 2 "

Conference of the Zionist Organisations of the Kielce Voivodeship.

On Sunday, the 23rd of this month, at 12 noon, a conference of the Zionist organisations of the Kielce voivodeship will take place in Kielce, in the hall of the Zionist Club.
On behalf of the Central Committee, the following comrades will take part in the conference: the president [?] Dr. Yitzchok Schiper and the president [?] of the Main Board of "HeChalutz Ba'al Melacha" in Poland, Eng. [?] Landsztak.
The agenda of the conference is as follows:
1) opening, 2) the current situation in Eretz Yisroel (lectures by Dr. Schiper and Eng. [?] Landsztak), 3) our platform and tasks in the kehillas, 4) discussion, 5) resolutions and closing of the conference.
Some hundred delegates from nearly fifty towns and townlets of the Kielce voivodeship will take part in the conference.
In the Presence of the Bailiff He Slashed His Aunt.

Between the Kielce resident Yosl Goldszlager and his cousins, the brothers Rosenholz, a dispute has been going on for quite some time over a fairly large sum of money which the Rosenholzes owe Goldszlager.
This Tuesday Goldszlager, together with the komornik [bailiff], came to his cousins' apartment intending to carry out the auction of the household goods. On the stairs he ran into his aunt, Mrs. Chaja Rosenholz, with whom he began to argue heatedly. At a certain moment Goldszlager grabbed a knife and cut his aunt's throat in several places. There was great panic; the doctor who was called, Dr. Gushibovski [Grzybowski?], bandaged Mrs. Rosenholz's wounds and left her in her apartment.
This shameful scandal within a wealthy family, as well as the fact of someone going at an elderly woman with a knife, made a strong impression.

New Arrangements at the Kielce Cemetery.

As we are informed, work will begin in the coming days on new arrangements at the Kielce cemetery.
First, two large waiting rooms for women and men will be built, a beys-medresh, a tahara house [for washing the dead], etc. The building costs of these structures are being donated by the respected local citizen and well-known industrialist Mr. Shaftl Tojman[?], in memory of his wife Zlate Leah, may she rest in peace.

Major Political Lecture by Deputy Yitskhok Grünbaum in Kielce.

The Central Committee of the Zionist Organisation in Poland has sent word that if the Executive member, Deputy Yitskhok Grünbaum, remains in Poland for a few more days, he will certainly visit Kielce, where he will deliver a major political lecture on the present situation in Zionism and in Eretz Israel.
The news of Deputy Grünbaum's possible visit has aroused great interest in Kielce and its surroundings.
She Wanted to Increase Her Balance at the P.K.O.

Helena Skraba of Kielce, having no more than 1 zł. in her P.K.O. [Postal Savings Bank] passbook, came up with the following scheme: to the figure 1 she added a zero and another one, and hurried off to the post office, where out of the sum of 101 zł. she withdrew 56 zł.
Some time later she came again for the second instalment, but this time the swindle was discovered, and instead of going home she was led off to jail.

The pipeline construction will cost 150 thousand zł.

The Będzin Kehilla Protests Against Arab Terror

Yesterday at noon[?] a protest meeting took place in the premises of the Będzin kehilla in connection with the Arab murders in the Jewish Yishuv.
At the meeting, in which the kehilla board and council took part, a protest resolution was adopted according to the wording of the Coordination Commission.
The resolution was sent to the English government in London.
It is characteristic that even in convening[?] the session on so serious a matter, behind-the-scenes politics was played, and Comrade Landauer was not invited. Only under pressure from the supervisory authority was an invitation sent to Comrade Landauer, on which the words „członek rady“ [„council member“] had been crossed out...
A Theft in Broad Daylight

Yesterday in daytime thieves got into the apartment of Mechel[?] Recht on Kołłątaja Street in Będzin, where they tore out the drawers of the cupboards, from which they took various silver and gold objects.
District Conference of Betar in Sosnowiec

This coming Sunday a district conference of Betar will take place in Sosnowiec. Also taking part in the conference will be Dr. Bornstein, the creator of „Achdut Israel“, and A. Propes.
Dr. Bornstein will also speak at the election rally of the Revisionist list, which takes place tomorrow in the open air.
A Theft Through the Roof

In the night from Wednesday to Thursday thieves got through the roof into the stationery shop of Dawid Gutensztajn in Będzin, from which they stole various goods.
The theft amounts to about 1.500 zł.
Bronia Kalin of Zawiercie Among the Martyrs of the Land of Israel

During an excursion in the woods around Mount Carmel, when Arab murderers attacked a group of passengers and shot them dead, among the martyrs was also Miss Bronia Kalin of Zawiercie.
In the next issue of the „Zagl. Tsayt.“ a letter from the Land of Israel will be printed, from Matek Hampel, dedicated to the tragically perished young woman.

With today's issue our domestic postal subscribers receive enclosed settlement[?] (rozrachunkowe) forms, on which they must immediately transfer the subscription amount, without paying any postage. Those who do not pay will not receive the next issue.

[Notes of the Week — abroad and Palestine.] In Moscow 16 condemned[?] Trotskyists, headed by Zinoviev and Kamenev, have been shot.

From the Election Campaign in Sosnowiec

[Sosnowiec — kehilla; elections.] The election campaign has already come into full blaze. Last Saturday and Sunday a large number of meetings, of almost all the parties, took place in Sosnowiec.
On Saturday during the day the "Mizrachi" held a hall meeting, at which Messrs. Wszepkowicz[?] and Steinfeld described the state of the kehilla economy under the hitherto commissarial kehilla administration and the tasks of the elected parnasim in the new kehilla.
— The same day a large meeting of the Zionist list No. 18 took place in the "Palace". At this meeting there spoke Messrs. G. Stawski, Szenicki and the leader of the list, Dr. Moladista[?], who in his [?] speech set out the kehilla system in general and in Sosnowiec in particular, and pointed out the guidelines of the Zionist representatives regarding the kehilla economy.
— On Sunday morning a meeting of list 7 took place in the "Eden" cinema. The first speaker was Moshe Chaim Kaminer, who offhandedly dismissed all the Torah and wisdom to be found among their rabbis (he meant the Mizrachist ones), who receive their ordination in some Warsaw "Tachkemoni".
The second speaker, a certain Horowitz from Bielitz, declared to the assembled audience that "Rabbi Englard is a spiritual aristocrat, a noble man and a diamond, whom the Jews of Sosnowiec do not appreciate. And if Rabbi Englard — says the speaker — wants to be rabbi of Sosnowiec, he only aims to go on spinning the golden thread of the tzaddikim, holy and pure, from whom he descends."
The closing speech was given by Rabbi Englard, who fears that in Sosnowiec there will indeed be further rabbinical elections, because two weeks after the board and the council are constituted, rabbinical elections will soon take place.
Rabbi Englard relates that during the whole time of the dispute he has striven only for peace, but on all sides peace is pushed away. Even "the rabbi of Koziegłowy also does not want to hold a din Torah with him." At the end he appeals to vote for his list.
— The same day in the afternoon a hall meeting took place in the Mizrachi synagogue, chaired by Mr. Kupermintz, which drew a very large audience. Speeches were given by Messrs. Baruch Wszepkowicz, Yitzchak Steinfeld and others, who showed that the candidates of list 17 are those who carry on themselves the yoke of all Klal Israel. At the end it was unanimously resolved that all vote for list 17.
— In the evening a hall assembly took place in the premises of the League, at which Messrs. Szulklaper, Kramaszyk and Shalom Pilc spoke, calling on those present to vote for list 25, on which there stand people who will defend the working masses.
— On Tuesday the first election proclamation of the Artisans' Association appeared around the town. The proclamation is stuffed with party phraseology, such as "struggle against the clergy", "all the shtiblekh etc. must be driven out of the kehilla."
It is hard to believe that the candidates figuring on the artisans' list agreed to this content, for such a Jew as Yoel Dymant, or even Shmuel Nuta Nachemia[?], are not entering the kehilla "to drive out the clergy and the shtiblekh"; this is only a fantasy of a couple of boyish hotheads.
Będzin Tax Office Claims 115,000 Zł. from the Franco-Italian Company

[Będzin — taxes and courts.] In the Sosnowiec District Court the trial took place these days against the Franco-Italian Company in Dąbrowa, from which the Będzin tax office claims 115,000 zł. fine for not purchasing a separate trade licence (patent) in the years 1933 and 1934 for the "Kasztelan" coal mine.
The Będzin tax office bases its claim on the fact that "Kasztelan" belongs to the Będzin tax office and must hold a separate licence.
For formal reasons the trial was postponed.
From the Half-Colony for Jewish Schoolchildren

[Będzin — welfare and education.] As we have already written, on the initiative of the Będzin magistrate, half-colonies (day camps) for poor pupils of the public schools were organised this year for the first time; for the Jewish children 900 zł. was allocated.
In connection with this a committee of the school guardians (opiekunki) was organised at the Jewish kehilla, which within a very short time set up the half-colony properly.
Over 15 days 140 children received good, tasty meals 3 times a day, and they spent their free time in the school garden on Kościuszko Street.
The half-colony was run by Mr. Avraham Iche Hajcenberg with the assistance of the Froebelian kindergarten teacher Miss Sala Najman and the seminary teacher Miss Sala Szajnerman.
When a Woman Wants to Be a Man...

[Sosnowiec — courts; Będzin county.] A sensational petition has come in to the District Court in Sosnowiec from a woman, resident of Niesiec[?], Będzin county, who wants to be a man.
The patient is the 22-year-old Bronisława Bernarska, who asks the court to change her first name and surname as a woman to the name of a man, and that she be recognised as such.
Mrs. Bernarska supports her petition with the fact that in St. Lazarus Hospital in Kraków she was examined by Professor Albricht, who declared that she is... a man.
Because of this the court decided to request from the above-mentioned professor a confirmation of whether Mrs. Bernarska's statement agrees with reality.
Huge protest meeting against Arab terror.

Sharp speech by Rabbi Chameides.
On Monday evening the Katowice Zionist organisations (General Zionists, the "League" and "Mizrachi") held a protest meeting in the large kehilla hall against the continuing bloody terror in the Land of Israel.
Dr. Tarsan [?] opens the grand meeting, explains its purpose, calls on those present to honour the fallen martyrs, and gives the floor to Rabbi Chameides [Rabbi Dr. Kalman Chameides of Katowice] for his address.
The esteemed speaker begins in Hebrew and speaks about the aim pursued by our enemies, the fanaticised and wild Arabs, who have badly misread our not reacting with the same terror for terror, our heroically biting our lips and not letting ourselves be provoked, and have understood our slogan of "havlagah" [restraint] as cowardice.
The Jewish people in the Diaspora must show [?] its moral support for the Yishuv, which fights and bleeds for our right to be able to come to the land of our past and our future.
Rabbi Chameides recalls the sad role of the English administration in the Land of Israel, their hypocrisy, their unscrupulous [?] intrigues, their failure to fulfil their obligations, which were also guaranteed by the whole civilised world.
But — the esteemed rabbi exclaims — there is no power that could stop us from continuing the work we have begun. For the Jewish people the Land of Israel is more than a land of colonisation; Zionism is a revolution in the Jewish psyche, our worthy answer to other Jewish troubles.
The speaker protests sharply against the murderers of Jews in the Land of Israel, who incite the Arabs to their cruel deeds of destruction.
The speech, which expressed Jewish grief and anger and was delivered in a very sharp tone, made an enormously strong impression on the large audience, which filled not only the kehilla hall but also the adjoining halls.
Rabbi Chameides then reads the corresponding resolution, which is adopted unanimously, and the Jews of Katowice warmly applaud the esteemed speaker for expressing their pain and for his very interesting remarks.
After the singing of "Hatikvah" the grand popular demonstration is closed in a serious mood.
———
On Tuesday morning a delegation composed of Rabbi Chameides, Dr. Majer, Director Klein and Dr. Tarsan [?] handed the resolution to the English consul in Katowice.
On this occasion Rabbi Chameides (in English) gave expression to the feelings of bitterness and pain that now prevail among the whole Jewish people, and to the demands contained in the resolution.
The consul assured the delegation that England does not wish to do any injustice to the Jewish people (a glaring contradiction of reality!); he promised to forward the resolution promptly to the higher authorities, and listened very attentively to the Jewish complaints and demands.
Yes, polite and gentlemanly the English are — if only [?] they were a little more honest and sincere towards the Jewish people, they, the masters of all kinds of foggy formulas, as Rabbi Chameides aptly characterised the British politicians.
Petard thrown at a Jewish shop.

In the night from Monday to Tuesday a petard again exploded at a Jewish shop in Katowice.
Police came at once to the site of the explosion and established that unknown criminals had placed a petard under Eichenbaum's grocery (colonial goods) shop on Francuska Street, which exploded with great force.
The explosion damaged the entrance door and the fittings of the shop; besides that, in Eichenbaum's apartment, which is on the first floor, 12 window panes were smashed.
The police are conducting an energetic investigation.

From the Katowice kehilla
In connection with the "Haynt" report in Monday's issue, the president, Mr. Abrahamer, asks us to state that the double registration slips for Jews at the Katowice magistrate's office were introduced specially for the kehilla's records and serve exclusively its purposes.
The accusation against the magistrate is therefore unfounded.
A r o y.
Katowice lawyer accused as accomplice in currency smuggling.

In Katowice the English citizen Daniel was arrested; with the help of a forged permit he had wanted to take three and a half thousand English pounds out of Poland, i.e. about 26 thousand złoty.
In connection with this the lawyer Markowicz [?] was also arrested; he is accused of having helped to take foreign currency out illegally.
Demonstration by supporters of the Spanish government.

On Saturday morning about 70 young people gathered in front of the Spanish consulate in Katowice and shouted slogans in honour of the Spanish government and the "Red Army".
The demonstrators chose a delegation from among themselves, which handed in at the consulate's office a declaration, as volunteers, that they are ready to leave for the Popular Front in Spain.
Begged for alms and committed a theft.

A Christian came into the flat of Mrs. Helena[?] Neuman in Katowice, introduced himself as a poor unemployed man and asked for alms, or else something to eat. When Mrs. Neuman went into the kitchen for food, the so-called unemployed man meanwhile stole from the table a gold ring, a silver watch and 25 zł. in cash.
This week the thief stood before the Katowice court, which sentenced him to 6 months' unconditional imprisonment.
Don't leave flats unguarded.

Fajwel Fuks of Chorzów[?] went out for a walk on Sunday and left a window of his flat open. Thieves took advantage of the opportunity, got into the flat through the window, and there stole jewellery worth 2000 zł.
Affair with tourist tickets.
In Katowice Icek Ajzenman of Będzin was arrested; he is accused of having traded in tourist tickets valid for 10 days. After the interrogation Ajzenman was put into the Katowice prison.
From the Polish theatre.

On Tuesday, 1 September, a premiere will be given at the Polish theatre in Katowice. For the first time there will be performed: 1) "Marcowy kawaler" (The March Bachelor), a one-act play by Bliziński, and 2) "Majster i czeladnik" (Master and Journeyman), in 2 acts, by Korzeniowski.
Beginning 20.00, end — 22.15.
Terrible death in a "shaft".

In the area of the "bieda-shafts" (biedaszyby, primitive coal pits dug by the unemployed) in Katowice an accident occurred on Tuesday afternoon. The unemployed man Weber fell into one of the "shafts" and was killed on the spot.
The Jewish Tragedy

[Zagłębie — editorial; public institutions and leadership.]
L. Szpigelman.
(Understanding for representation — among us and among them.)
How[?] often, and sometimes [—] too often, we occupy ourselves with the local social problems. We talk about the responsibility of the masses, of the citizens, toward their institutions, toward those who have to see to it that it is possible, as far as possible, to come to the aid of the hungry and suffering in their bitter need.
We demand of the masses that they come to the aid of the institutions when fund drives[?] have been carried out, which [are] not in action[?]; and one cannot say that the public does not listen to these appeals and that the population remains apathetic. No, we know how many times the population is simply electrified in urgent cases; we know of moments when the masses listen to the cries of woe and, with their last groszy, almost[?], come to the aid of the institutions — so long as they have the possibility of helping those who need support, those whom one must not let fall.
But — as we have said more than once, and not long ago — there must also be a mutual responsibility. If one comes to citizens, to sisters and brothers, and calls on them: you must maintain your fallen and oppressed, your poor and sick, and support them according to your means — then those same people have the right to see what is done with their donations, with the hard-earned Jewish groszy.
We have said several times that just as the community must be responsible toward those who concern themselves with the people who need to be supported, so too the institutions must show their spirit of self-sacrifice[?] and their intensity[?]. They, the institutions, are obliged to prove to the community that the moneys entrusted to them are conscientiously used for the good of the community.
Why did we demand this? Quite simply: first, it is the elementary duty of every institution to do so of its own accord. One must give society a public account, so that everyone may see the benefit that this or that institution renders the community. And second, not only did the institutions not take this into account, but on top of that their prestige fell to such a degree[?] that all trust in public activity was lost; and even then the leading public figures did not find it necessary to want[?] to save their prestige.
When we saw the decline in the Jewish street, when we felt with what eyes the masses had begun to look at public work, how cheap it had become, we said that institutions must not be treated this way, because to an institution — so we said then — one does not give charity when one pays the monthly contribution; rather, one thereby pays a debt that one feels toward society.
The institutions unfortunately paid no heed to any danger, and so they began systematically to slide down to the deepest decline, and it reached the point that institutions which had enjoyed due respect and trust not only lost the last of it, but grave accusations fell upon them, which were not denied; and so, naturally, the accusations were stressed all the more, so that they set off[?] on the road of complete resignation and bankruptcy.
Today the Zagłębie institutions find themselves in an unbearable situation; decline and frivolity occupy the top place, and let it be said here that the population is not to blame for it, nor the Jewish citizens, who in any case have understanding for public and honest work. With full awareness everything can be confirmed: what led to this were our public delegates, who regard themselves — or nowadays want to be regarded — as unlimited rulers and dictators, in whom the population is to believe blindly and have full[?] trust.
The decline that has arisen, the bankruptcy on the entire front, the complete resignation, must be a lesson to them: blind trust cannot be demanded of society; it has to be earned, and one can raise oneself up only by honest and conscientious deeds, by true good deeds, which must be applied toward the most varied strata of the Jewish population.
* * *
Now that the summer is over, the holidays are already approaching, and after them the autumn with all its complications, and then the hard, long winter, which the masses do not gladly welcome. These are now, without any doubt, very hard times for the whole Jewish people, not to speak of the middle strata of the people and of those who live in need and poverty.
In summer the poor man „smuggles“ himself through somehow; he does not clothe or shoe himself or the children, nor does he need coal to heat his cellar or attic room. But hardly does the first cool wind begin to blow when a shiver runs through his bones, because he remembers how poor, naked and hungry he has remained after the „hot“ summer.
Usually, among normal, healthy nations, one passes from summer to autumn and winter with composure, and everything is prepared according to a certain system and calculation. Quite different is it with us, when we live in such dreadful conditions that we cannot imagine today what face and shape our tomorrow will have.
And precisely in such poverty and decline we have no representatives on whom we could rely; our whole communal body is dissolved and dishevelled, and we cannot point out which is this or that representation, this or that representative body, called upon to defend or to care for these or those elements.
Besides, surely no nation in the world needs as many guardians as we Jews, because no nation in the world is as persecuted as we are, who have no place of rest anywhere and are not allowed in any country to earn our piece of bread. The hounding and suffering have no limit. Which nation is as „enriched“ with refugees as we are, for whom provision must be made wherever they may be driven? Can other nations feel this taste? Do they know what grief this is, and what it is to be hounded[?] by the dogs?
We must therefore have remedies for every disease, which are ascribed only to the Jewish people, and therefore we need nothing but caretakers, so that we are not wiped out completely.
We need healthy, steel-firm[?] representations, which would have the possibility of seeing to it that the bullets fired at us are deflected, and at the same time of healing those who have already been wounded by all our antisemites.
And here we are stark naked in the social sense, and we do not even know who our true representatives are and whether they exist at all.
Does one need a greater tragedy than all this?
Toruń.

[Feuilleton — travel impressions; Toruń.] By P. Blumenkranc (Częstochowa).
(Impressions of a guest for a while)

First of all, when one comes to Toruń, one goes to visit the "Ratusz" [the old town hall]. A historic and very well-known building in all of Poland. Part of it was built in the 13th century and the rest in the 16th century.
According to what our guide told us (we had little time to check it), the "Ratusz" displays as many windows as we have days in the year, as many halls as there are weeks in the year, and as many little turrets as there are months in the year too.
The local magistrate even has a cabinet for things[?] from the 16th century with 4 doors, on which are painted symbols of the 4 seasons — showing how the things[?] of each season were kept in the proper part of the cabinet.
But besides all these "wonders"[?] stands the main tower of the "Ratusz," which symbolizes the year as a whole, and to go up it one must crawl 50 metres high over crooked wooden stairs.
From the height one sees the magnificent panorama of all Toruń, which is divided into new and old. Together with the suburb "Bydgoskie," which is to be[?] united with Toruń in the nearest future.
In general Toruń is an interesting town. Arriving along the Wisła [Vistula], one starts walking through narrow little streets with narrow three-storey houses. The widest house has four windows, for, as is known, ordinary people were permitted to build houses with only two windows across, and the nobility [szlachta] with 3–4 across; that is, without researching the family tree, one knew at once who was of distinguished lineage and who a plain commoner ["chai vekayam"].
* * *
Like every old town, Toruń has many legends connected with its buildings.
Some of them:
In Toruń stands a building which supposedly[?] began to be built in the year 1271, which leans by one and a half metres and is a strange phenomenon in architecture.
The local inhabitants tell the reason for the building's crookedness.
In the 13th century there lived a "goyr"[?] [apparently: a monk]. He belonged to a "zakon" [monastic order]. Once he caught sight of a beautiful woman and fell in love with her.
He went about day and night bewildered; no sleep came to his eyes, his heart had no rest.
The clergyman at long last could not master himself and ran away from the order to the woman.
The order assembled and condemned the offender to death.
The clergyman repented of his deeds, did penance, and as a sign built the tower.
But how astonished everyone was when, the next morning after the building was completed, it was noticed that it leaned. Everyone saw in this a sign that the sin had not been forgiven the clergyman, and so the tower stands crooked, and it is therefore called "Krzywa Wieża" [the Leaning Tower].
A second one (and perhaps it is true?)
In Toruń there are ruins of the buildings where the participants in the Crusades lived. They settled there after doing their holy bit of work.
But they had enemies among the local and the Danzig [Gdańsk] inhabitants.
And when they caught their opponent — so it is told — they tied his body to a horse, dragged him over the pavement and afterwards threw him into the water (by the ruins there is a little pond, which is pointed out as the place where they threw in their enemies).
* * *
Apart from the fact that Toruń boasts that already in the Middle Ages it was a great trading town (in the market stands a hotel named "Modry Fartuch" [Pod Modrym Fartuchem, "Under the Blue Apron"], which has existed since the year 1489), it is proud that it produced one of the greatest men in the world — Mikołaj Kopernik [Copernicus], whose monument, made by the German sculptor Wolf in the year 1852, stands in the town centre.
As to the house where Copernicus was born, however, there are differences of opinion between the Germans and the Poles.
The Germans hold that Copernicus was born in the house that today bears the number 30; the Poles, on the other hand, maintain [that it was] in the house with the number 17 on the same street.
The Poles base their claim on documents found in the year 1921, and on that basis they set the memorial plaque into the wall of house number 17 on the street, which today is called by the name of Copernicus.
But Toruń also shows off its churches with pride and especially prides itself on the church named after Saint John, which began to be built in the year 1233 and was completed in the year 1447.
In this church there are many works of art and characteristic paintings. In the year 1921 frescoes were discovered by chance, which are said to date from the year 1400, depicting various biblical and moral scenes. Extremely characteristic frescoes. On one wall of the same church, again, stands a sculpture of the Holy Mother, and beneath the figure — a bust of... Moses our Teacher from the 16th century. The guide explains the connection to us: the New Testament owes much to the Old (that, apparently, is how he was taught to explain the placing of Moses our Teacher together with the Holy Mother).
In the same church hangs a characteristic picture by an unknown author, partly painted and partly pasted, in which the history of the world from biblical times up to Christ is depicted.
And so on and on, an abundance of interesting works, of greater or lesser artistic value.
* * *
But enough. Something about ourselves.
How do things stand with the Jewish community?
Unfortunately Jews neglect the history of their communities. One often comes to Jewish communities that count hundreds of years, and the local Jews have not the slightest notion of the origin and development of their community.
As regards Toruń, we had no opportunity to talk with the local leading Jews.
A Jew we met by chance, an educated man, a local resident, told us that the Jewish community numbers 120 families and that Jews feel no antisemitism.
This Jew is, as usual, a local patriot. First of all he wanted[?] to show us the new bridge over the Wisła (a truly imposing one), which was built only two years ago.
But antisemitism — not a mention of it ["man dekhar shmei"].
So the Jew said. We, on the other hand, had a somewhat different impression.
When we were in the church (with a Christian guide), a Christian came up to him several times in the name of the priest.
At first the priest ordered that he should not talk so loudly, and afterwards he came with other orders, into his ear. Our guide blushed each time, and evidently in the end he received a strict instruction and hurried through the explanations.
Yes, the Jew said it with pride.
But when we observed the shops and found in the market one Jewish watch shop belonging to a certain Grinbaum (perhaps there are a few more) among 67 thousand inhabitants (with the Bydgoszcz suburb), we did not see the grounds for pride.
If one does not search with torches for the local handful of Jews, there is still no cause for pride. Not even a whole percent Jews, and on top of that the Germans occupy the top place in commerce...
But on the other hand — we thought it over — this too is good. If one wants[?], even one percent is too much and harmful.
Our neighbours have shown us that clearly..

On the Road to the New Kehilla. 3rd Article: To Whom We Appeal.

[Sosnowiec — kehilla elections; opinion.] At last we already have plenty of lists and candidates, "envoys[?] to the kehilla".
Every list was brought to the kehilla's election office with festive faces, with the air of heroes returning from a battlefield. There — they have pulled off a stunt, stitched together a list, and lo, a leader of the generation is ready.
Do these important list-makers also think about the kehilla? About giving it people for work and for representation? No. All these operators are gravely worried and frightened, nervous and scattered over one single subject: will my first candidate — or will I myself — come out of the lottery wheel with my mandate? And when people, poor things, carry such a worry, when each of them, poor thing, looks into the eyes of his relatives and acquaintances and wants to read the truth there — will they really vote for him, or, God forbid, are they fooling him — well, how can one demand of such a person that he remember the kehilla? That he put the interests of the kehilla above his mandate?
Of the individuals, the seat-seekers, nobody demands any such thing at all; one cannot take them seriously, people laugh at such types — and if there are nevertheless several dozen Jews who agreed to assist such a person as candidates on his list, and several dozen more Jews who give signatures — then we truly stand before a riddle, and it is hard to grasp the psyche and the mind of this kind of Jew. Jews are not fools, after all; Jews understand business — so how is such a very[?] sad and demoralising phenomenon to be explained? Do the Jews of Sosnowiec really hate their kehilla so much, do they really want to spite it and send into it every deaf-mute, imbecile and minor! Do our Jews not understand that their interests and their honour demand that the kehilla, too, be placed on a higher level, both in its practical day-to-day work and in its appearance[?] towards the outside? The Jews of Sosnowiec certainly understand this — so how is the fact to be explained that they do everything possible so that the result should be exactly the opposite?
And perhaps those are right who hold that every Jew separately, as an individual, is a wise man, but Jews together, as a collective, are far from wisdom and are specialists in harming their own interests and their own honour?
———
And the parties?
We have parties whose approach to the problems of Jewish life is a very serious one. We have parties whose leaders and activists are people of many virtues, of intellectual seriousness and of an honest intention to serve the interests of the community. Do these leaders really think about the future shape of the kehilla?
They would like to, but unfortunately they are not able to.
When it comes to the kehilla, the situation is quite different from elections to the Sejm or the city council. We have the impression that, as regards the kehilla, the parties do not dominate the Jewish street. The riff-raff ("erev rav") — the candidates and petty candidates, the gabbaim with beards and without beards — crawl out like demons ("nisht-gute") from every corner and create such a poisoned atmosphere, arouse such sickly ambitions and petty ambitions, that the road for ideologies and principles is blocked[?] by all kinds of stones and thorns.
And then a situation arises in which the leading bodies of the parties can no longer think about the kehilla, but look for a way to save the party's prestige — so that at least they will not be left ashamed...
We put the question to experts who know the Jewish street and are considered good estimators:
— How do you estimate the outcome of the elections?
— The list of party X will get two mandates, the list of party Y one mandate... But the list of Reb Lemech will have two, perhaps three; the list of Reb Grunem — also some two mandates. They do have friends[?], whole herds...
In short — the wild lists will flood the kehilla. The parties, with their world-views and programmes, with their experienced[?] activists who have years of honest and idealistic public work behind them — they will barely fight their way to a little corner in the kehilla.
Is it really going to stay that way?...
———
More than one reader will think: how naive must one be to come with such a proposal, and precisely now, after the various little "factories" have already, after hard toil and drudgery, put together their candidate lists? Was it for this that those fellows sweated and toiled — so that at the last minute they should follow your advice and walk away from the election bowl like a cat from the butter?
It is already too late, someone told us, to come with such an appeal. Even if everyone agreed you were right, it would not help now; the lists are already lying with the election commission.
But we do not intend at all to appeal to those individuals. These individuals are too scorched by the fire of the evil inclination to crawl into the kehilla; with them it is a disease from which no doctor and no newspaper articles will cure them.
Such individuals can be cured when they get a cold compress on their overheated brains, when on the morrow after the elections they realise that their effort was in vain, that the Jewish voter does not look upon the kehilla as an ownerless garden where all kinds of horses, cattle and donkeys may come to graze. Only then will they begin to acquire respect for public institutions, for public work and for this kind of[?] elections.
So, if we do not appeal to those "who already have the mandates in their pocket" to withdraw, we may — and must — precisely now appeal to the mass of voters.
The Jews of Sosnowiec still have everything in their hands. The 7,500 adult Jews who were included in the voters' register now have the choice to decide the fate and shape of our future kehilla: shall it again be the "balagan"[?] where no decent word is heard; shall it again have a kehilla council that does not know the difference between "cursed be Haman" and "blessed be Mordecai"; shall the parnassim once again look for "a roll with fish and 50 zł.", again not knowing when to praise[?] and when to protest; shall the future kehilla council again be the Jewish laughing-stock of the town — or shall the kehilla council be able to claim to represent honestly and worthily the congregation of the Jews in Sosnowiec, to represent a kehilla in such a large Jewish city?
Shall the kehilla bodies form the Jewish parliament, where the important[?] and historic struggle between currents and ideas is to be continued, or shall they become a stock exchange where people trade in whatever they can...
All this the voters can decide, and let us hope that even those who signed the wild, faceless lists will, at the decisive moment, feel the responsibility and will help to defeat[?], down to a complete rout, all the lists that have one goal — to quench the sick ambitions of the seat-seekers.
Y. G—baum.
A Law That Jews May Not Pray in Congregation

(From the series "Strange Laws"). By Z. Haber, Vienna.

In every country there is a law that everyone who lives in the country must know its laws; if one does something that is not according to law and justice, one cannot excuse oneself by saying one did not know that it was forbidden.

And yet in every country there are strange laws, hundreds of years old, which are never put into practice, and nevertheless people have forgotten to declare them invalid. If these laws were put into practice, one would hardly be allowed to go out into the street; for everything in life there is a "stringency".

The Leipzig Fair has compiled all these strange paragraphs that have been forgotten. More than two million such paragraphs exist in all countries. Some countries have deliberately not repealed the paragraphs, because sometimes one has to hold on to such an old paragraph if one wants to achieve something. Most of the paragraphs are in America; over a million stringencies still exist there.

In Sweden, for example, there is a law that Jews may not pray in congregation. They may not set up synagogues, [although] synagogues have existed there for hundreds of years. The government does not care. Still, the law that "one may not set up synagogues" is still in force.

In Switzerland one may not drive faster than 10 kilometres an hour, in many towns only 6 kilometres; if one really drove so slowly, one could get there faster on foot.

In Norway there is still today a law that from 6 o'clock in the evening until 6 in the morning a watchman with a lantern in his hand must run or ride in front of every train. You can imagine how fast the train may travel at night.

In Poland the Russian law is still valid that everyone who buys a packet of tobacco must first tear the stamp, so that it cannot be used again. Although such stamps have long ceased to exist.

In Italy one may not dance in any venue that is not well lit; all the lamps must be burning while doing so.

In France one may not curse in the street. For every curse one must pay a fine of 67 centimes.

In England the law is still valid that for playing cards on Sunday not only the players are punished, but also those who watch.

In Denmark, according to the law, every man who sits next to a woman in a park [must] keep at least 15 centimetres away from her.

In several countries of South America women may not wear sleeveless dresses; in several countries the law prescribes how long shirts must be, for women and for men.

In Connecticut anyone who reads a newspaper describing murders is fined a thousand dollars.

And so it goes, one law after another, sheer strange things, which fill us with either fear or laughter.

And yet these laws are in force to this day, and the government can make use of them whenever it wishes.
Heard and Seen

[Sosnowiec — satirical feuilleton; kehilla, elections and begging.] By Ben Amotz.

The Jew is to blame...

Sabbath. At the time of Minchah the battle began. Symbolically, in the holy war — "When thou goest forth to war" is the first verse of this week's portion — on that day the ammunition arsenals were opened, and one shoots at the enemy...

We go from one place to another and listen to the "perlrige" [?] opposition, accompanied by heavy calibres, from which there rings out the echo of the election campaign of styczeń [January] 1934.

And when one reflects on the public, one sees that nothing has changed: the same lies, the same sins, the same praises, and also the same sold souls...

And in the very heat of the elections, together with the election appeals in which both worlds are promised, this world and the world to come, there appeared a report of the so kind-hearted commissarial kehilla administration.

In the "sprawozdanie" [report], which may be compared to a modern "Ma'avar Yabok" (in the Polish language), we find absolutely not one single new word (apart from the "mi sheberakh" of pan komisarz [Mr Commissar] himself — that the great Jewish mass in Sosnowiec has known him for 40 years as a Zionist activist, and that the "kapores" slaughtering lasted, thanks to him, until 2 at night...). That we had already had the opportunity to hear during his countless sermons in the town synagogue and also in the synagogues and batei midrash in the suburbs.

And if we nevertheless say a "word" about the "witty" report, it is only because we do not find in the expenditure section of the report how much it cost the Sosnowiec kehilla to maintain the "house organ" of the honourable kehilla commissar, who, from the moment he took over the office of head of the community, acquired a weakness for writing "articles" about kashrut, repentance and about the power of the good inclination, which led him in this way onto the Szopienice road, where a little Jewish soul [?] waited for a kehilla commissar as sandek...

Possibly the head of the community did not publish this item in order to avoid the shame before the wider public and before his colleagues in the administration, who reproach him that the very same dog in the guise of an "editor", whom he fed for so long, has now begun to bite him too?...

We have many more questions to ask, but go and ask questions of a kehilla commissar who excuses himself with the pretext that his great plans were not realised because of the disloyalty of the Jewish population of Sosnowiec and the attacks in the Jewish press, such as the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" and "Haynt".

An old, well-known excuse, passed down by inheritance, that
— the Jew is to blame...

Rabbis or kehilla elections?

The Jewish population of Sosnowiec has a difficult problem to solve, namely: are rabbinical elections taking place, or kehilla elections?

The question is actually not new. Already in 1934 it stood on the agenda. The difference, however, is that then the question was posed more sharply, and now it is half veiled, so that the mass of voters stands gaping and asks itself:
— Rabbis, or kehilla elections?

Here a speaker stands on the platform and says: Gentlemen, you should know the truth, that it is not kehilla elections that are taking place but rabbinical elections, and if indeed rabbinical elections, then it is self-evident that I am "Kurter" [?], because, literally, "I am a khisher" [?]...

Along comes a second side and says exactly the opposite: "What are rabbis to us, who are rabbis to us? First of all," he says, "we must build a kehilla; and just as a carter needs a whip, a kehilla needs a rabbi. But let it not enter the head of any of you that we are waging the election campaign for the sake of a rabbi."

So now we are already sure that what the speaker says is the pure truth — that it is in fact kehilla elections, and simply a business — but it soon turns out that we were "mistaken" again: the floor is taken by a colleague of the previous speaker, who gets carried away [?] and reveals the "secret" that "rabbinical elections are taking place"...

An outcry is heard — "va-yitz'aku" — is it possible? Is this what we brought you here to us from Katowice for — to play the role of "Megaleh Amukot" [revealer of deep secrets], or, as they say in plain language, to "pasim [?] the gallery"?...

— Gentlemen! — a correction comes at once — the speaker "erred"; he meant to say kehilla elections, and the word rabbinical elections slipped out of him. "A person is, after all, no angel" — did not our Reb Barukh, too, err and, instead of list 17, call out
— list 7...

The simple public accepts the excuse, but in the minds the above-mentioned question keeps gnawing [?], to which no proper answer is yet known, and it is truly a cruelty to living creatures that the mass of voters should still not know a clear answer to this day as to what will take place on 6 września [September]:
rabbis, or kehilla elections?

The "business" is growing.

I have come to the editorial office to inform you that the business has, thank God, grown — says an acquaintance of mine, a Jew who is a communal worker.
— Which business do you mean?
— we ask him.
— The "business" of begging...

And seeing that we do not yet fully understand the meaning of his "tidings", he explains and says:
— The cadres of beggars, who in Zagłębie are more numerous than in all of Poland and blacken our face, are now being reinforced with new types of beggars — these are boys of 14–15, yeshiva lads, "delegates" of various yeshivas in our town.

At first their number was negligible; only seldom did a party of yeshiva lads go "out" across the town and collect money for a "respectable" Jew.

Other yeshivas envied this and doubled the number of collectors, so that nowadays the collectors "for respectable Jews" play a significant role in our philanthropy...
— Well, what do you want from the editors?
— I want you to write that our situation is not so bad: the "business" in the field of begging is growing...
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Ki Teitzei)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Ki Teitzei
—o—
a) "When thou goest forth to war against thine enemies, and the Lord thy God delivereth them into thy hands."
The previous portion ends with the verse: "So shalt thou put away the innocent blood from among you" — if Jews themselves are clean of bloodshed, then they will be victorious in war. First Jews themselves must have clean hands, a clean conscience, and only then, when they are called out to war — the victory belongs to them... Zera Berakh.
—o—
b) "And thou wouldest take her to thee to wife" (21:11)
"The Torah spoke only against the evil inclination." Rashi.
Those who went out to war were very pious young men: "the fearful — of the sins in his hands"; whoever was afraid because of his sins had to turn back from the war. So — only pious young men, and yet such men could have an affair with a "beautiful captive", because the evil inclination had to persuade such men that they were actually doing a mitzvah... Leket Amarim.
* * *
"And compel our inclination to be subservient to Thee" — we say every day in our prayers.
For as long as the evil inclination keeps within its bounds and does its work as an evil inclination, it is not as dangerous as when it switches its role and presents itself as the good inclination... Therefore we pray "and compel our inclination to be subservient to Thee" — force our evil inclination to be subservient to its own calling... Dvash ve-Chalav.
—o—
c) "A full month" [yerach yamim] (ibid., 13)
Everywhere in the "Tokh" [probably: the Tanakh] it says "chodesh yamim"; why does it say here, of all places, "yerach yamim"?
But the "Levush" writes that in a ketubah one must write "la-chodesh" and not "la-yerach", because — do not open your mouth to Satan: for at betrothal the word "chadash" appears ("When a man hath taken a n e w wife"), and at divorce [?] the word yerach appears ("geresh yerachim").
Therefore here, where it would have been wished [?] that she be "afgefigdet" [?] with him and that he should indeed divorce her — the term yerach is used. Ran Midgiel [?].
—o—
d) "Then it shall be, in the day that he maketh his sons to inherit" (ibid., 16)
"In the day that he maketh his sons to inherit" — what remains of a person, for him to bequeath to his children — "that which he hath": only what was truly his, what he did not steal from anyone — only that remains of a person... Chemdei Genazot.
—o—
e) "I gave my daughter unto this man" (22:16)
A match was proposed to the Noda BiYehuda [R' Yechezkel Landau] with a certain rabbi and gaon. The matchmaker began praising the groom and said: "Why, he is simply an angel of the Lord of Hosts."
The "Noda BiYehuda" answered:
— That is exactly why I don't want him as a groom: "I gave my daughter unto this m a n" — but not to an angel...
—o—
f) "And because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Aram-naharaim, to curse thee" (23:5)
In Kovno [Kaunas] a police chief once wanted to prepare a pogrom. The Jews interceded with the higher authorities and an order came to prevent the pogrom. Then the police chief came to the kehilla and demanded a reward, because the pogrom had not taken place.
Then R' Yitzchak Elchanan [Spektor, rabbi of Kovno] said:
— Now the meaning of the verse "An Ammonite shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord" is answered for me: be not good to them [?], even when they come with the claim "And because they hired against thee Balaam... to curse thee... and the Lord turned the curse into a blessing unto thee" — for if Balaam had the claim that a reward was due to him, since God after all made blessings out of his curses — no thanks whatsoever are due to him for that, because what he meant was to curse...
—o—
g) "Nor take a widow's raiment to pledge... But thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt" (24:18)
What connection do these two whole verses have?
But in Egypt the Jews suffered most [?] from a lack of clothing. On "And they asked every woman of her neighbour jewels of silver and jewels of gold, and raiment", Rashi says: "The garments were more precious than everything," because as slaves they were not given the right to dress themselves; and therefore "Nor take a widow's raiment to pledge... and remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt" — for you knew the taste of having no garment on yourself... Panim Yafot.
—o—
h) "For all that do such things, even all that do unrighteously, are an abomination unto the Lord thy God."
Mishneh Torah [Deuteronomy] is a repetition of all the commandments. Now the verse says: even "all that do such things" — even when one performs all the commandments, if he is at the same time "one who does unrighteously" — it is an abomination to the Lord... Ktav Sofer.
A Word to Jewish Society

(Concerning the campaign to enrol apprentice youth in the supplementary vocational schools.)
(Specially for the „Zaglembier Tsaytung".)
In the period from the 25th of this month until 5 September, enrolments will take place in the supplementary vocational schools (Fach-Ergänzungsschulen) for young people who are over 15 years old and are employed as apprentices („terminators"), trainee boys or trainee girls in crafts, industry or trade.
Even though the provisions of the various laws on working youth stipulate 3 years' attendance at a supplementary vocational school, and also set a penalty for master craftsmen who do not see to it that the apprentice attends the vocational school, and even though the apprentice is later not admitted to the journeyman's examination — the number of Jewish children in the supplementary vocational schools is very meagre.
We must admit, however, that although the demands of the Christian master on his apprentice regarding the work are greater and stricter than among Jews, there is on the other hand among them a greater understanding of enabling the employed apprentice to attain higher qualifications, both in the workshop and at school. Among non-Jewish craftsmen there is a longer-range view; there they take care to have properly qualified new blood in the trade.
At a time when Jews live only for [?] the present day, just „to get through", among Christians they care a great deal about tomorrow and prepare for it thoroughly with the help of organisations designated for that purpose.
Not all the causes can be enumerated in a newspaper article, but we must stress that the main reason why Jewish artisan youth does not make use of its right to obtain the necessary education is the disregard for this important problem on the part of the artisan youth itself as well as of the parents. People do not think of the future and have no sense of responsibility for themselves or for their fellow men.
One can say with full boldness that the attitude to craftsmanship and to engaging in it has not changed much among us Jews compared with before the war.
Even then, when the organisation of Jewish society — artisans' organisations, trade unions, etc. — was still in swaddling clothes [?], there were already some who understood that to be a good professional and make [?] a living one must show a minimum of general and theoretical vocational education; and because they indeed [?] had this, they did not slacken, they exerted themselves in their youth and indeed [?] obtained higher qualifications.
One may be for or against the industrial movement [?]. But one cannot be so backward as not to understand that all over the globe, wherever people live, they live today in different conditions, with greater demands of the times and of society regarding craftsmanship, and consequently it is clear that a young person aged 15 to 20 must adapt himself to the new times and to the newly created conditions in the trade. He must improve himself in the supplementary vocational schools, in order to acquire the necessary knowledge of raw materials, drawing, bookkeeping, etc.
It is true that the network of supplementary vocational schools is still quite small and they do not everywhere stand at the proper level; surely this is a result of the small state budget, but nevertheless there are supplementary vocational schools in about 260 towns in Poland, compulsory for apprentices.
In case a number of candidates apply [?] that exceeds the number of places in these schools, the school authority must open parallel (double) classes.
Jewish apprentice boys and girls! Make use, then, of the short deadline and submit written applications to be admitted to the supplementary vocational schools that exist in your town.
Jewish workers, artisans and small traders! Remember that 80 and perhaps 90 per cent of the youth employed in crafts, industry or trade are your own children. It is therefore your direct duty to see to it that your children who are employed as apprentices enrol in and attend the supplementary vocational schools.
Jewish artisans' organisations, trade unions, youth and school organisations!
Take an interest in this important problem; help the commissions for Jewish craft affairs, to which detailed circulars, application forms and posters about this important campaign have been sent — to move the artisan and working youth to enrol in the said schools!
The duty lies on all Jewish public activists, and in general on the whole of organised Jewish society, to take up this important matter and to enable Jewish youth to get into the schools, so as to obtain through them the necessary general and theoretical vocational training that the trade demands: if we want to maintain the productive Jewish economic positions at the proper level, and if we want a healthy influx of Jews into the crafts, we must now, without delay, join this serious and important campaign!
Chanan Hofman.
Back from the Dacha

[Będzin and Sosnowiec — satirical feuilleton; end of the summer season, kehilla.]
[unclear word] in a good and lucky hour — it is already the month of Elul.
The storks, sensing the coming of Elul, have set off in good time for the south.
I too gazed at the Elul sky spreading out above the pines of the Reitscher [?] forest, and fell into thought.
Somehow it is not the same sky as a few weeks ago.
It still strives to play in wine-coloured [?] hues, the sun still yearns [?] early in the morning for the tops of the pine trees. But then a small cloud first steals in, spreads itself out [?], and you no longer recognise the sky — a sort of fascist [?] — dressed in a grey skullcap and dozing [?]...
The pines too suddenly give a kind of whisper, "poshene" [?] — and fall silent.
Somehow everything is mourning [?]...
One feels an eeriness...
I run to my "Dulcinea", with whom I "flirted" a little all summer long, as they call it nowadays; perhaps she will console me a little and, with her Madonna face and her light smile, drive away a little the heavy clouds, the approaching gloom.
But I find her quite different. The "tekiah, shevarim, teruah" just blown have had the proper effect on her.
She is carefully packing her belongings, her few textbooks, which, poor things, were terribly bored all summer, and is getting ready to leave for the Kraków university, where those who will help her hammer into her head the difficult studies of the 3rd semester are surely already waiting for her....
We silently shake hands and take leave...
I too begin to take stock of my soul: that I have been here too long already, that I cannot abandon a town to its fate.
And although I am not a candidate on any of the 14 lists for the Sosnowiec kehilla, nevertheless in our [?] time even a "jednostka" [an individual] has some worth.
Who knows, perhaps you are needed there?
Who knows what the town looks like without you?
Now they say that a hard fight is going on between the kehilla board and the council.
The kehilla board claims that it is the sole representation of Będzin Jewry and decides who may sit in the kehilla, and the council claims the opposite — it is entirely its own competence...
The old-age home, only [?] it is looking for homeless, lonely [?] old people to take into the institution, and does not find any...
Likewise the hospital chases after poor patients to treat free of charge [?]...
A real upheaval, God preserve us, has taken place in town since the shofar sounded.
Well, can one sit at such a time, grazing and weighing the kilos one has gained?
I decide to pack up and go home.
On the way I meet my 90-kilo lady acquaintance, and with a wistful [?] smile she says to me:
— "Well, Pfefferl, are you really leaving already? Frightened by the shofar blasts? I'll tell you the honest truth, I would have left too, but a misfortune befell me and I must stay here a little while longer...
You surely remember that week the "imieniny" [name-day party] at Madame Pfeinkuchen's? Well, I fell upon the various sorts of jams and "ciastka" [cakes], and as you know, I am very delicate, and indeed I soon upset [?] my stomach. But that I forgive you already!
The main thing is that because of those cursed jams I lost a whole 3 kilos, and now, after such a dacha season, which cost me a fortune, I am going [?] home with only 87 kilos!"
I shook my head at her in sympathy and wished her to recover her function [?] and to come back a full 100-kilo madame.
Having arrived in Będzin, I immediately felt the civilisation of the big city.
First I met an acquaintance of mine [?], a certain Wald, who used to try to talk me into taking a walk with him on the "Górka" [the hill], and always used to laugh at me and call me "trus" [Polish: rabbit, i.e. coward] when I declined such a walk.
This time my acquaintance had black eyes and altogether a hapless look.
That, he explained to me, was how the wind on the "Górka" had "fixed him up" [?] — he had caught a draught [?]...
I also learned that the kehilla council is preparing to publish a popular edition of "Shoftim".
It is preparing to popularise the idea "if there are no officers — there are no judges", and it is also considering modern technical sticks and straps with which the officers shall rule over the people, so that they obey [?] the judges.
Cities of refuge will also be created for those who travel on the Sabbath, as, for example, happened with the president [?], who was taken for a Ger hasid, and in the end the correspondent of "Haynt" saw him travelling on the Sabbath...
In short, one must go home; one cannot abandon a town to its fate.
A Pfefferl.

[Humour — “Der Kokh-Lefl”; poem.]
“Der Kokh-Lefl” [The Cooking Spoon] — humour and satire. Compiled by Amotzli.
Mai ka mashma lan [what does it teach us], the Endek [member of the antisemitic National Democrats],
What is it, then, he lets me hear —
With his wildness, with his coarseness,
With his lust to disrupt?
That is how every drunkard behaves;
In the street he fell down,

Will there ever be a bit of unity
In the Jewish camp?

Jews lie and debate
About elections and principles.

What is it, then, it lets us hear?
Who can be a prophet and guess
When things will finally get better?
Our ship is on the waves,
And the storm is dangerous,

The Weekly Portion on the Left Side

[Satire — the weekly Torah portion (Ki Teitzei) “inside out”.]
“When thou goest forth to war” — what do you want to wage war for? For a “beautiful woman”? It isn't worth it. “And thou wouldest take her to thee to wife” — you can get her without a “kosef” [without money, i.e. without a dowry].
“Then she shall shave her head” — she will have her plait cut “à la garçonne”. “And pare her nails” — she will get herself a manicure. “And she shall put the raiment of her captivity from off her” — you may as well order her a new winter costume, because if not, “and shall remain in thy house and bewail” [so printed] — she will not budge from the house and will make scandals for you. “Thou shalt not sell her at all for money” — don't be a fool and don't haggle with her over bargains...
“If a man have two wives” — if someone is destined for a double misfortune, “the one beloved” — one a sweetheart, “and the other hated” — and the other a lawful Jewish wife.
“The woman shall not wear that which pertaineth unto a man” — don't let her wear the trousers.
“Thou shalt in any wise let the dam go” — first of all send off your mother-in-law.
“When thou buildest a new house” — before you lay the foundation of a new house, take three years' rent “z góry” [in advance].
“Thou shalt not plough with an ox and an ass together” — don't harness two beasts together (we don't want any dozór [kehilla board] members and deputies!)
“At his day thou shalt give him his hire” — don't tell tall tales that you redeem a bill of exchange without protest costs.
“Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn” — if you are an ox, then “halt stoil” [?; perhaps: keep quiet].
Translated [“getaytsht”] by R' Gershon.
