In the Tangle of Life (8)

[Serialized novel — Kraków, Zawiercie and New York; installment 8.]
(A novel with dramatic events in Kraków, Zawiercie and New York)

On the day Emma lost both her mother and her father, she wept, fainted and had such fits of hysterics that it was impossible to calm her at all. Bernard did not leave her side even for a minute; he kept encouraging her, spoke to her warmly and explained that from now on he would be both a father and a mother to her.

"My father, may he rest in peace," she said, wiping her eyes, "was a very clever man, a learned man with a very good head, but he was a man of the moment: if something came into his head, he did it at once. And in the last minutes of my mother's life he evidently became convinced that she had been completely innocent and that he had embittered her life for nothing — and suddenly the thought came into his head to commit suicide, and he carried it out at once."

Bernard now treated Emma like a beloved only child. He placed her with a rich cousin of his, Breitstein[?], in Brooklyn, and there she was treated like a princess.

Bernard earned well in America and ran a large business. He fell deeply in love with Emma, but she was proud, just like her mother, and behaved towards him with great tact; she did not encourage him in his love for her.

But there was someone else who was interested in Emma: this was Joe, the former Yosele, Malkale's son. Malkale was doing very well here; her husband treated her well and in America he had become an entirely different man. Malkale had been very friendly with Nechama and the children, and Joe and Emma had been friends too. Now, after Nechama's death, Malkale took a great interest in Emma and came to see her often. Joe, for his part, now began to look at Emma quite differently: she had become in his eyes a mature, beautiful girl who interested him greatly. Emma, however, did not have that feeling for him; she looked on him as a boy and did not take him seriously, and when he began to speak to her of love, she made a joke of it.

But Joe was not one of those young men who give up so easily. He did not stop talking to her about love, about how strongly he loved her.

One evening Joe pressed Emma hard with his declarations of love; he also wanted to kiss her, and then she told him he should not dare even to touch her. Those very words provoked him, and he held her tight in order to kiss her. She struggled out of his hands. At that moment Bernard came in, who had long held a grudge[?] against Joe; he tore him away from Emma and gave him a slap. Joe made to hit back, but Emma stepped between them and talked him kindly into leaving.

When Joe had gone, Emma grew angry with Bernard for having raised a hand against him.

"I couldn't help myself," Bernard excused himself. "He made me jealous. Emma, you are to blame for it too: why are you so cold to me? Don't you know that I love you more than my life?"

"Bernard," said Emma, "there can be nothing between the two of us; between the two of us stands death."

"Death?" Bernard looked at her in astonishment.

"Yes, death! You are to a certain extent responsible for the death of my parents, both of them still young people."

"I?"

"Yes, you! Do you think I don't understand? You fell in love with my mother; she was older than you, and yet she did not want your love. If you had not forced your way into a family and had not kissed a married woman, nothing at all would have happened[?]! They might perhaps both still be alive now. You are very good to me, you have done a great deal for my mother and for me, but still I cannot help myself. When I think of you I see my dead mother. No, leave me in peace, I will never be yours! Never!"

After that scene Bernard understood that the wound of her parents' death had not yet healed in Emma, and that if he wanted to win her for himself, he must treat her very carefully.

At that time Bernard received a very sad letter from Paris[?] from his sister Masha, who had come from Russia. She wrote to him that their parents had been shot and that she herself had barely saved herself because a Bolshevik commissar had fallen in love with her and helped her; but later she no longer wanted to know him and fled to Paris, and she was now leaving for America. She also wrote to him that he should not send her any money, because she had enough money.

And Masha came to America.

On the day Masha arrived, Bernard drove to the ship to meet her. He also took Emma along. Masha came down from the ship together with a young man, an artist, a painter, whom she had met in Paris; his name, she said, was Mikhail Stegers[?]. They had become such friends that she had brought him here at her own expense.

Bernard was naturally very glad to see his sister; she at once introduced him to Mikhail, and Bernard introduced Emma to the two guests. He now proposed that the two girls live together.

At first Masha and Emma lived very well together, but signs soon appeared that their friendship would not last long.

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: A Stormy Meeting of the Kehilla Council

[Head of the local page; Będzin — Kehilla.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, [—] Elul 5696 — piątek 28 sierpnia '936 [Friday, 28 August 1936].)
Będzin
A stormy meeting of the kehilla council.
Paragraphs 69 and 74 have the floor. — Glass and chairs "fly" through the air. — A delegation at the starosta's.
On Saturday night a meeting of the kehilla council took place. The finale of the meeting was a stormy one; ever since the present kehilla council has existed, no such "lively" meeting has yet taken place.
The meeting is conducted under the chairmanship of the newly elected Agudah president, Mr. Rinski [Ryński?], who invites as secretary his "comrade" ("genosse"), parnas Erlich.
On the agenda stood the following points: 1) reading the minutes of the last meeting, 2) reading the rescript of the Ministry concerning the confirmation of Mr. Rinski as president, and 3) economic matters.
Already at the first point the "mood" was tense. It starts with the chairman's declaration that the minutes will not be read, because they are not yet finished. On this Mr. Landner takes the floor and says that the minutes are indeed finished, but they are not being read because of certain intentions...
Then parnas Erlich reads the above-mentioned rescript, and Mr. Rinski afterwards takes the "Shulchan Aruch" into his hand and says: As chairman of the council I establish that the council numbers 18 members; from this number are "switched off" parnas Chaim Welner, who has left for the Land of Israel, president Y. M. Kurland, who has settled in Katowice, and also (this was the main thing) Mr. Landner, who after the death of Mr. Rudzin[?] was supposed to enter the board. Mr. Rinski rules this "halakha" according to paragraphs 69 and 74 of the electoral ordinance.
After this "neutral" lesson things begin to turn stormy. Parnas Herszlewicz shouts: "I ask for the floor on this question!" — and when Mr. Rinski will not give him the floor, a great outcry ("va-yitz'aku") breaks out, in which the gallery takes a large part; suddenly the big water bottle standing on the table bursts, chairs fly, and the hall becomes a pandemonium, a hodgepodge of voices, shouts that carry further out into the street and arouse the curiosity of many people, who come running to see the "evil wonders" taking place in the Jewish "little parliament"...
Little by little the storm is localized; later a policeman also came, who ordered the "remnants" to go home.
— In connection with this, a delegation of the national parnassim, in the persons of Messrs. Goldsztajn, Rozenker, Rozenblum and Rechnic, was received by the starosta, who, after conferring on the matter, declared that the intention to exclude Mr. Landner from the council is legally unfounded.
A 7-Week-Old Child Circumcised after Death

[Będzin — Kehilla; legal case.]
On the strength of an oath, permission was given to bury the child in the Jewish cemetery.
The following rare incident happened these days in our town.
On Wednesday a Jewish woman, a certain Dina Pleszowska[?] of Czeladzka[?] Street, came into the office of the Jewish kehilla and told that in her flat a little boy, 7 weeks old, had died, whom an unknown woman from Kraków had handed over to her a few weeks ago to bring up.
"What is the child's name? Who is the mother?" asks the kehilla official.
"The child has no name yet, because it has not yet been circumcised, and who the child's mother is I do not know either," Pleszowska answered.
With this tangled matter the kehilla secretary turned to the magistrate [municipality] asking that the permit to bury the child be issued, but at the magistrate's they did not want to issue the permit because of the information that the child had been found in a field and that it was more than certain that this was a Christian child and must be buried in the Christian cemetery ("cmentarz").
The situation became even worse when the magistrate official reported the matter to the starostwo [district office] and drew attention to the lack of certainty that this was a Jewish child.
Then a delegation on behalf of the kehilla held a conference with the starosta, after which the starosta passed the matter on to the municipal court, so that on the basis of an oath and witnesses a verdict might be pronounced that the child was of Jewish descent.
As a witness Rabbi Fridberg was called, who declared that Mrs. Pleszowska had called him several times to circumcise the child, but because of its weak condition the child could not be circumcised.
After Pleszowska's oath that a Jewish woman had left her the child, the court decided to give the child the name Wolf and permitted it to be buried in the Jewish cemetery.
The child's burial took place only on the fourth day, in the old cemetery.

Inquiries Concerning R' Mendel Lewin

[Będzin — Kehilla; rabbinate.]
The day before yesterday the kehilla board received from the starosta the following inquiries: 1) whether the kehilla board concluded any agreement with R' Mendel Lewin concerning his salary ("pensye") as moreh hora'ah [rabbinic decisor], and 2) when the kehilla council struck the item out of the budget.
The strike at the cable factory — settled.

On 31 July (lipiec) an occupation strike (sit-in strike) broke out at the cable and wire factory. The negotiations, which went on throughout the strike, produced no positive result.
This week the Kielce voivode, Dr. Dziadosz[?], came specially for this purpose and worked on both sides to have the strike settled.
The workers obtained a 5 percent raise.
The Froebel school in new premises.

The board of the local Froebel school (kindergarten) run by WIZO has at last succeeded in having the school moved to new premises on Sączewska[?] Street, in the house of Mr. M. K. Erlich.
In addition, other improvements have been made which are of great importance for the development of the Froebel school.
Registrations will be accepted from the 1st of next month at the above-mentioned premises.
The work was disturbed...

On Saturday, in broad daylight, a thief tried to get into the premises of the "Merchants' Association". By chance there was a person inside, who prevented the thief from carrying out his further "work".
—o—
Bitter "customers".
From the textile (manufaktura) shop of Mr. Salomon on Kołłątaja Street, a piece of textile goods was stolen on Wednesday
Accident with a tram conductor.

One of the tram conductors, while riding along Kościuszki Street, leaned out and received a heavy blow from a telephone pole.
The conductor was taken to hospital.
The "operation" on the budget of the commissarial kehilla board.

Shochtim's pensions reduced. — Salaries struck out for the new shochet, the supervisor and the beit-midrash cantor. — Subsidies reduced for the Jewish hospital and the old-age home ("Moshav Zkenim").
These days the commissarial kehilla board received the kehilla budget approved by the supervisory authority. The budget somewhat disappointed the head of the kehilla, who has only now realised that he is not the complete master of the purse, that there is a supervisory authority which does not agree with the kehilla management he conducts, and which does not permit him, in the present hard times, to engage a new staff of kehilla officials and to put high salary sums on the account.
In this budget the supervisory authority struck out the salaries for the new shochet Zweigenhaft, for the supervisor at the slaughterhouse Mr. Zajonc, and for the beit-midrash cantor and shammes Motl Walter.
Then the shochtim's pensions were reduced from 7 to 5000 zł. a year.
The Jewish hospital also suffered from the "operation": its subsidy was reduced from 12 to 6000, and the old-age home from 6 to 3000 zł.
In connection with this, the appointed kehilla president called together his colleagues of the appointed board and proposed to them to send an appeal to the voivodeship office against the struck-out items for the new officials, because the greater part of the salaries had already been paid out and it may still come about that the commissarial kehilla board will have to refund the money spent on unnecessary purposes.
During the discussion of this question it came to a sharp exchange of words between the head of the kehilla and the board members Garfinkel and Eng. Lipszyc, who were against the appeal, arguing that the president, who had done everything on his own authority, should now bear the consequences.
In his reply to Mr. Garfinkel the president said: "If the beit-midrash cantor were a Radomsko hasid, you, Mr. Garfinkel, would be for an appeal."
Mr. Garfinkel, who felt offended, reacted to the president's words, and the end was that Garfinkel and Lipszyc left the meeting in protest.
From the Jewish gymnasium in Sosnowiec.

From year to year the number of pupils at the Jewish gymnasium in Sosnowiec grows. This year in particular the attendance has risen greatly, and the number of pupils already reaches up to three hundred.
Because of this the gymnasium board was compelled to enlarge the school building by one more storey, so that the school building will have[?] three storeys. This is only for the time being, since the main aim of the school management is to set about building, next year, a school building of its own, suited to the city of Sosnowiec, where there are some 20,000 Jewish souls.
Advocate Hofmokl-Ostrowski sentenced to a month's arrest for insulting the court.

On Tuesday a sensational trial took place in the local municipal court: in the dock sat the well-known advocate Hofmokl-Ostrowski of Warsaw, defence counsel of Grusheshalski[?], who, on learning that his client had been sentenced to life imprisonment, sent a telegram to the Sosnowiec district court in which he insulted the court.
After the defendant's speech the court withdrew for lengthy deliberation and then pronounced the following verdict: Hofmokl-Ostrowski is found guilty and is sentenced to one month's arrest and a 5 zł. fine.
The convicted man announced an appeal.
Election rally of List 18.

This Saturday a large election rally takes place here, organised by List 18; speeches will be given by Dr. Melaristo[?], A. Liwer and others.
As reported, a meeting of the Jewish intelligentsia in Sosnowiec took place this week, and after acquainting themselves with all the lists it was decided to vote for List 18.
Dąbrowa

Conference of artisans.
As we have already written, in connection with the kehilla elections in our town a conflict arose between the Artisans' Association and the tailors' guild. The conflict led to the guild putting forward a separate list, which the election commission annulled.
Last Sunday a conference of both sides was held here. Also taking part in the conference was the member of the Central Committee (Ts"K), Mr. Goldsztajn (Będzin), who brought it about that both sides agreed privately to make peace.

The local kehilla president, Mr. L. Rechnitz, has turned to the starosta with a memorandum, in which Mr. Rechnitz expresses his wish that the supervisory authority release him from office, because of the sabotage that the dozór members are conducting against him, and because they refuse to come to the meetings of the board.
—o—
Accident.
The local shoe merchant Mr. Birnbaum met with the following accident in Krynica: while Mr. Birnbaum was washing in the morning, he slipped and broke his right arm.
Life in Kielce — An Imposing Protest Meeting of the Jews of Kielce against Arab Terror and against Stopping the Aliyah to Eretz Israel

[Section head “Life in Kielce”; Kielce — Eretz Israel, protest.]
Life in Kielce
(Date boxes: Friday, 10 Elul 5696 — piątek 28 sierpnia 1936 [Friday, 28 August 1936].)
An Imposing Protest Meeting
of the Jews of Kielce against Arab terror and against stopping the aliyah to Eretz Israel.
Together with the whole of world Jewry, the tens of thousands of Kielce Jews too yesterday, Thursday, made heard their word[?] of grief and anger, indignation and strong protest against the Arab murderers and against the attempts of the English Mandatory Power to sacrifice our right to build the Jewish National Home, the right of the Jewish people to aliyah to Eretz Israel — as a means of calming the run-amok Arab terrorist bands, as a reward for destruction, murder and breaking of the law.
Already from six o'clock hundreds of people began streaming to the synagogue from every corner of the town, and at 7 o'clock the synagogue, where the great protest meeting took place, was overfilled with several thousand Jews.
The mood of the many-thousand-headed crowd was very grave; it looked like the eve of Yom Kippur towards nightfall, when every Jew prepares for the great Day of Judgement, and with a holy trembling the great mass of people waited for the opening of the meeting.
A few minutes after seven the cantor with the choir appears before the Holy Ark; he says the first prayer and then holds a memorial for the martyrs who perished at the hands of the Arab murderers. When the cantor says aloud the words “את נשמת הקדושים והטהורים שנרצחו על קדוש השם לטובת עמנו וארצנו” [“the souls of the holy and pure ones who were murdered for the sanctification of the Name, for the good of our people and our land”], weeping breaks out in the synagogue — young and old, women and men are crying. The scene is simply indescribable. Yes, had the representatives of the civilised world (among them our English Mandatory Power) been present at such a scene, they would certainly have come to the conclusion that no power in the world is able to stop the aliyah to Eretz Israel, that no force can[?] destroy the attachment of the Jews to building their homeland, Eretz Israel, which is the only consolation for all Jewish troubles and sufferings.
The first to speak is the Kielce rabbi, Rabbi Rapaport. His voice is broken with Jewish grief; he expresses his sharpest protest against the Arab murderers and against the Mandatory Power and at the same time comforts the great crowd not to lose hope, for the Jewish troubles can no longer be borne and therefore — he says — it must at last become light.
Then the representatives of almost all organisations speak in turn, and they too express their sharp protest against the Arab murderers and against the Mandatory Power.
After the reading of the protest resolution, which was adopted unanimously, the choir sang “Hatikvah” and the huge crowd dispersed.
After the meeting two protest cables were sent, one to the Colonial Office in London and one to the English Ambassador in Warsaw.
The kehilla too sent a protest telegram to London.
On the whole the protest meeting turned out extremely imposing and left an unforgettable impression.
The Zionist District Conference in Kielce

[Kielce — Zionism, kehilla elections.]
The Zionist District Conference in Kielce
As has already been reported in our paper, a Zionist district conference of the Kielce voivodeship took place in Kielce on Sunday.
To the conference, which took place in the Zionist club, came about 20 delegates from 15 towns and townlets of the Kielce voivodeship.
On behalf of the Central Committee, the vice-president Mr M. Kirszenbaum took part.
The conference was opened by the chairman of the local Zionist Organisation, Mr Grünapfel, who greeted the guests and gave a short speech about the present events in Eretz Israel. Those assembled honoured, by rising, the Jewish martyrs who perished through Arab terror.
Then President Kirszenbaum, who has just returned from Geneva, where he took part in the World Congress, gave an interesting lecture on the present situation in Zionism and Eretz Israel.
Afterwards a presidium was elected of the following comrades: A. Grünapfel (Kielce) chairman, M. Kirszenbaum (Warsaw), Dr Steinberg (Dąbrowa Górnicza) and editor Wilani (Kielce) as secretary.
President Kirszenbaum then gives a second [—][?] lecture on the tasks of the kehillas, at the same time calling on those assembled to secure a victory for the Zionist lists.
In the discussion the following comrades took part: Dr Steinberg, M. Ch. Trampe (Skarżysko), M. Langsberg (Pińczów), Y. Szwarcbaum (Szczekociny), Przysuske (Jędrzejów), Grünapfel, Lewin, Maszenber[?] (Kielce), and others.
The delegates at the same time gave a report on the election campaign in their towns.
After the discussion 2 resolutions were adopted: 1) a protest resolution against the Arab terror and against the English Mandatory Power, which plans to stop the aliyah to Eretz Israel, and 2) to call on all Zionists of the Kielce voivodeship to secure a complete victory for the Zionist lists to the kehillas.
At 8 o'clock the conference was closed.
Supervisory authority confirms the list of the bootmakers' guild

As has already been reported in our paper, the election commission disqualified the list of the bootmakers' (kamashn-makher) guild.
Against the decision of the election commission, the election committee of list 8 lodged an appeal with the supervisory authority. Adv. Felc interceded on behalf of the list with the starosta [district head].
As a result of the intervention, the authorized representative of list 8 received a notice from the supervisory authority that the decision of the election commission is annulled and the list is confirmed.
In first place on the list stands Mr. Grensztan[?], and in second place — Mr. Hulfsztat[?].
Thus in the current kehilla elections in Kielce we have no fewer than 12 lists.
Voting will take place at 4 polling stations

At the last meeting of the election commission it was decided to set up 4 polling stations, where the voters will cast their ballots.
The 4 polling stations are located at the following places:
1) the premises of „Achi Ezer“ (Dobroczynność [Charity]), Warszawska 17; 2) the kehilla premises, Leonarda 23; 3) the cheder „Yesodei ha-Torah“, Kozia 12; 4) in the Zionist beit midrash „Sha'arei Zion“, Sztrzgowska[?] 1.
Last course for paint dealers from the provinces

Only a short time separates us from the application of the law of the year 1844, under which only those who have passed examinations will be allowed to engage in the paint trade. A large part of the Jewish paint dealers, however, do not realize the danger threatening them and are indifferent to the very foundation of their existence.
Over 800 Jewish paint dealers, under the direction of Mgr. W. J. Finkler, after completing the courses at the Central Union of Retailers and Small Traders, passed examinations and obtained diplomas, thereby retaining their trading positions. Right now is the favourable moment to take the examinations, and every Jewish paint dealer should make use of this [?] opportunity.
The courses at the Central Union of Retailers and Small Traders, which are conducted in a very popular manner in Polish and Yiddish and without any textbooks, enable the participants to grasp the material quite easily and consequently to pass the examination well.
On Monday the 31st of this month, at 10 o'clock in the morning, the Central Union of Retailers and Small Traders will hold the festive opening of the last three-day course for paint dealers from the provinces, for which a large number of paint dealers from all corners of the country have already registered.
50 million zł for major investment works in the Kielce voivodeship

The voivodeship office of the Labour Fund has drawn up a 4-year investment plan for the Kielce voivodeship.
Carrying out the plan requires a credit of 50 million zł. In the first year 12 million zł would be used. Kielce's share in the first year would be 2 million 700 thousand zł, according to the following allocation:
for new public (powszechne) schools 144.000 zł; for the extension of the hospital 150 thousand zł; for the extension of the slaughterhouse 250 thousand zł; for sewerage works 700 thousand zł; for public municipal works 900 thousand zł; building a Piłsudski Avenue 240 thousand zł; and for sports facilities for the P.W. [military training] 130 thousand zł.
Great public meeting of list no. 12

Tomorrow, Saturday, at 5 o'clock in the afternoon, a great public meeting will take place in the Zionist club, organized by the Religious-National Bloc (Zionists, Mizrachi and the World Union), which bears the number 12.
The Zionist beit midrash „Sha'arei Zion“ for the coming High Holidays

The beit midrash „Sha'arei Zion“ in Kielce has engaged a qualified cantor with a choir for the coming High Holidays. The hall, after renovation, is nicely furnished, and the worshippers will have comfortable seats.
The gabbai of the beit midrash, Mr. Ostrazicz[?], appeals to all worshippers, and especially to the Zionist public, to secure seats in good time by buying admission tickets, which can be obtained daily from 6 to 8 in the evening at the beit midrash.

The starosta restores Landner's rights as a member of the kehilla council / The scrutineers are to sit like mute judges... / Grand election rallies of List 17; Rabbi Nissenbaum in Sosnowiec

Yesterday the kehilla administration in Będzin received a decision[?] from the starosta, according to which Mr. Rinski's declaration that Mr. Landner is expelled as a member of the council is annulled.
—o—
The scrutineers are to sit like mute judges...
As we are informed, the election commission of the Sosnowiec kehilla has decided that the scrutineers will be permitted only to be present, but not to interfere in the competence of the election commission.
—o—
Grand election rallies of List 17. Rabbi Nissenbaum in Sosnowiec.
Today, Saturday, at 4 in the afternoon, an election rally will take place in the courtyard of the „Mizrachi“ (Man-Dushever[?] 18), with the participation of President Rabbi Yitzhak Nissenbaum of Warsaw.
In the evening at 8.30 the great and final rally will take place in the same courtyard, at which Rabbi Hager[?] will speak with a lecture on[?] „The struggle of the ‚Agudah‘ against national Jewry in the Diaspora and in the Land of Israel“.
Theses: 1) The partner[?] of the Besht and the methods of the Agudah, 2) Our ways and theirs, 3) The physiognomy of the kehilla according to the practice of the „Agudah“ and its „creator of ministering servants“, 4) The religious-national struggle at the present moment.
The lecture has aroused enormous interest in the town.

On the trail of the bomb-throwers in Zagłębie / For the struggle against Arab terror in the Land of Israel: a delegation of Zagłębie Jewry to the British consulate in Katowice / Judenstaat members vote for the national lists

The police authorities have arrested several dozen persons, of whom five have been handed over to the judicial authorities.
The 5 are suspected of having had a connection with those who carried out bomb attacks on the synagogue, shops and Jewish homes, and poured incendiary material over the clothes of Jewish women.
The investigation into the matter is under way.
—o—
For the struggle against Arab terror in the Land of Israel. A delegation of Zagłębie Jewry to the British consulate in Katowice.
Under the chairmanship of city councillor A. Hampel[?] a plenary session of the coordinating committee of the Zionist organisations and parties in Będzin took place, at which the question of a protest by the Jewish population of Będzin against the Arab acts of terror in[?] the Land of Israel was discussed.
After a thorough discussion, in which Messrs. Hershlevitsh, Wagner[?], Kaminski, Zimmerman and Plavada[?] took part, it was decided to hold today, Saturday, at 3 p.m., on the sports ground of „Hakoach“ a great popular rally devoted to the protest of the Jewish population of Będzin against the acts of murder and against the attempts to stop the aliyah to the Land of Israel.
Representatives of all the Zionist organisations and parties in Będzin will deliver speeches. We are certain that Jewish Będzin will protest with dignity and turn out in masses at the appointed time for the popular demonstration.
At the same time it was decided to send a delegation of the whole of Zagłębie Jewry to the British consulate in Katowice, which will submit a sharp protest in the name of the whole of Zagłębie Jewry against the Arab terror campaign and against the attempts to stop the aliyah to the Land of Israel.
—o—
Judenstaat members vote for the national lists.
At the consultation of the Judenstaat party members (Jewish State Party) in Sosnowiec, a resolution was adopted to vote for lists 17 and 18.

“To Be or Not to Be” (On Jabotinsky's Lecture in Sosnowiec)

[Zionism — Jabotinsky's lecture in Sosnowiec.]
That is what the political lecture of the President of the N.Z.O. [New Zionist Organization], Vl. Jabotinsky, who is coming to Poland in September, will be called. Since the last lecture of the great Revisionist leader, which was held in Warsaw 3 months ago, the situation in Zionism has changed. In the first weeks of the disturbances in Eretz Israel it was believed that the English administration, under the pressure of public opinion, would suppress the Arab revolt and would not permit Arab acts of terror against Jews in Eretz Israel — but reality has shown that the Eretz Israel administration has not taken the proper measures against the Arabs in Palestine.
The situation in Eretz Israel is worsening from day to day; the High Commissioner confers with the Arab terrorists and is on the point of stopping aliyah to Eretz Israel. The Yishuv in Eretz Israel does not react to the acts of terror of the Arabs; the Jews are adherents of “havlagah” — self-restraint is the slogan of the Jews in Eretz Israel. What must the Zionists do at this moment, when the English betray their obligations towards the Jews; our attitude towards the Arabs at the moment of crisis; what must the Yishuv in Eretz Israel do — yes “havlagah” or no “havlagah”: all these questions will be answered by the well-known Zionist leader in his lecture on the subject “To Be or Not to Be”.
What's New in Upper Silesia? — Lecture by Dr. Nossig

[Upper Silesia — Katowice, culture.]
The day before yesterday, Monday evening, all the Katowice Jewish national societies and economic organizations, headed by the rabbis and the kehilla, arranged in the halls of “B'nai B'rith” a lecture by the well-known sculptor and writer Dr. Nossig, the creator of the monumental and symbolic work “The Holy Mountain”.
The topic: “Judaism in the Light of Art”. The president of B'nai B'rith, Dr. Reichmann, welcomed the audience and the grey-haired lecturer and gave him the floor for his lecture, in which the speaker talked about the role and the influence of Jewish art on the creations of the nations.
Dr. Nossig spoke at length about his great work “The Holy Mountain” and about the events in Eretz Israel, and that Jews must be active, i.e. that it is too little merely to acquaint oneself with Judaism.

In Poland there is a central committee for the above-mentioned work, headed by Dr. Thon and Prof. Schorr.
Dr. Nossig is visiting the larger cities and appearing with lectures.

From the Election Campaign in Sosnowiec

Bloc of the artisans with the League for Labour Palestine.

On Saturday and Sunday there was an abundance of meetings in the town of Sosnowiec, announced by countless [—] [posters?] and election appeals. The public went „from strength to strength“, from one gate to another, since most of the meetings were held under the open sky, and listened to speakers of one list casting sins on the other: for example, the „National Camp“ sees that „Agudat [Israel]“ is to blame for all troubles; Left Poalei Zion blame Right Poalei Zion; the Right claim the opposite, that the Left are to blame — well, go and find out, O people, who the real culprit is!

On Saturday a series of meetings was held, among them one of „Mizrachi“, at which Messrs. Steinfeld and Rabbiner[?] Szejnerson spoke. The latter pointed in his speech to the harmful policy of the „Agudah“ hitherto with regard to Eretz Israel in general and in the Diaspora in particular.

A very large public came to the meeting of the Small Traders' Association. Messrs. Kajzer and Zielonka spoke, describing the self-sacrificing activity of Mr. Aliger and the necessity of peace in Sosnowiec, which Mr. Aliger — as a non-partisan — will endeavour to bring about.

In the course of Sunday 3 election meetings took place (apart from those in the suburbs).
In the morning an election meeting of Rabbi Englard's group took place at the „Eden“ cinema. The first to speak was Mr. Horowitz (Bilin[?]), who enumerated the merits of Rabbi Englard: if he presents himself before a starosta or a voivode — says the speaker — he will achieve everything with his noble personality; who else can come forward like him with a brilliant Polish speech?
The former „kamiger“[?] makes ashes and mud of all the lists, which he constantly „analyses“. All the lists — he says — are worth nothing, only Rabbi Englard's list.
Mr. Dalezman[?] also settles accounts with „Mizrachi“. Various political groupings — he says — are running in the elections. I do not understand at all — says Mr. Dalezman — what political groupings have to do in the kehilla?!...
The closing speech is given by Rabbi Englard himself. When Jonah the prophet — he says — was sailing on the ship and the whole „okręt“ [vessel] was about to go down, the „sa-trau“[?] [sailor] asked him „What is thine occupation“ — what is your trade, are you an artisan or a small trader; „Whence comest thou“ — where do you come from; „What is thy country“ — what is your land? „And of what people art thou“ — of which nation are you? To all these questions Jonah gave one answer: „I am a Hebrew“. We too are what Jonah the prophet answered: I am not an artisan, I am not a small trader, not a nationalist Jew, not of any other party whatsoever; I am simply a Jew without any epithet. Whoever wants to rebuild the kehilla and my house — let him vote for my list. I say that one should not vote even for 22 (the Agudat list); let nobody think he can fool me and slip in another ballot. The Day of Judgement is coming and the Master of the Universe is a „Knower of thoughts“. I wish you a good inscription and sealing, a good year and all the best for all generations.

At the artisans' meeting a storm broke out when Mr. Langer stressed that the tailors' guild has no specific interests in the kehilla. At these words the representative of the tailors' guild, Mr. Eksztajn, jumped up and came out with [sharp] language. In the end the storm was put down and the assembled public listened quietly to the speakers Diamant, Barankiewicz, Eksztajn, Grinberg and others.

At the same time meetings were held by the Right Poalei Zion (25) and the Left Poalei Zion (5).

At the same time a meeting of the Zionist Organisation (18) took place in the „Mizrachi“ courtyard. Messrs. A. Litwer (Będzin), Dr. Meladrista[?] and Szenicki spoke with lectures on the tasks of the kehilla, calling for votes for list number 18.
At the outset Dr. Meladista[?] sharply censured the agitators of the well-known „Kol Kore“ [proclamation] — to come into the synagogue to say Psalms at the very time when Jewish Sosnowiec, in heavy rain, protested against the Arab murder gangs and at the same time took an oath to continue with all its strength the building of the Land.
After the speeches the assembled public sang „Hatikvah“.

In the courtyard at Modrzejowska 29 the „Agudat“ held an election meeting, at which Messrs. H. M. Ejzenman[?] (Dąbrowa), Sz. J. Rinski (Będzin) and Langer[?] spoke.

A very good impression was left by the election meeting held in the afternoon in the courtyard at Modrzejowska 18, organised by list 17 („Mizrachi“). At this meeting the delegate to the World Jewish Congress, Rabbi Awigdor, spoke, giving a political lecture in which he described the attitude of Jews to other peoples and vice versa.
Then Mr. Steinfeld and Rabbi Hager spoke; the latter promised that at the Saturday meeting he would give an answer to the spreaders of lies and to the Sosnowiec school principals[?] who had laid hands on the Jewish printed word.
The thousands-strong public then sang „Hatikvah“.

Towards evening, under the chairmanship of Mr. B. Jasny, an election meeting of the Revisionist Organisation took place. The first to speak was Szabtaj Jungster; then Mr. Lion[?] (Katowice) came forward and said, among other things: „The tragedy of the Jewish people is that it does not want to be blindly obedient to the great leader Zeev Jabotinsky. A genius like Jabotinsky is born once in many years. The Jewish people did not understand Moses and his Torah — so it was driven into exile; and because it does not now understand Zeev Jabotinsky — it does not get out of exile“.
After the list leader Mr. Jasny came forward with his programme speech, a representative of the Betar commissioner (Netziv Betar) spoke about the necessity of a... Jewish Legion in Eretz Israel.
With a resolution in favour of the Revisionist list the meeting was closed.

On Monday the negotiations to create the combined (linked) lists were concluded. The result is as follows: 3 blocs have been formed.
1) A religious bloc, which comprises the lists of: Rabbi Englard, Agudat, Old[?] Sosnowiec (Bigsztak[?]), the Radomsko Hasidim and „Koziegłowy tsar“[?].
Second bloc: small traders, Revisionists, Zionists, „Mizrachi“ and „Torah ve-Avodah“.
Third bloc: artisans and the League for Labour Palestine.
The Kehilla — How It Was and How It Should Be

[Sosnowiec — kehilla; opinion.] (A voice of a Sosnowiec small-traders' activist.)
In my article in the „Zaglembier Tsaytung“ no. 33 I, as a representative of the small traders, dwelt on the representation of the small traders in various branches of economic life, such as the Chamber of Commerce, the tax offices, the town council, etc.
In the present article the writer wishes to show what the kehilla has been until now for the broad masses, and how it ought to have been and could have been. These are, in short, the questions I want to clarify here, although it is possible that not all groupings in our town will agree with my arguments.
I do not wish to criticise here the activity of the old kehilla, nor the activity of the nominated kehilla administration. It is clear to everyone today that the old kehilla had no contact with the masses. This came about because it lost its authority among its voters, and this happened first of all because of the vexatious [?] party quarrels, which also weakened it internally, and it ceased to be what it should have been.
One of the more important causes of all this is the so-called „protectionism“ which developed in the kehilla and from which the budget suffered very badly. I hold that protectionism ate away the organism of the kehilla. Facts reached the masses — often exaggerated and unverified — about reductions granted to various well-to-do persons when their kehilla tax (etat) was assessed.
It was said, for instance, that in burial matters special reductions were given to those who were acquainted with people who stood close to the kehilla.
All these stories, true and untrue, reached the masses, and this led to the kehilla undermining its own authority.
No less important is the fact that a religious kehilla was imposed on us, and this greatly narrowed its activity and also the competences of the kehilla. But if about this last misfortune we can do nothing, the new kehilla that is coming must nevertheless face the question of cleansing the atmosphere that has formed in and around the kehilla.
The vexatious [?] personal and party quarrels and the protectionism must be rooted out with all severity, so that the kehilla, which must be the official representative of the Jews of Sosnowiec both outwardly and inwardly, should enjoy the broadest confidence.
The Jewish small trader, who is weighed down by his daily worries about a livelihood, and who in the present, particularly hard time must fight bitterly for his existence, is in essence far removed from any partisanship. He must therefore have a different approach to kehilla affairs. The Jewish small trader, who is without any doubt the largest part of the etat payers who fill the budget of the Sosnowiec kehilla, wants to see in the kehilla a worthy Jewish representation, which will with its authority protect the honour and the interests of Jewish Sosnowiec.
Within the framework of the kehilla's possibilities of activity there must be: a just distribution of the etat without any reductions. The well-to-do must relieve the less well-off of the etat burden.
In assessing the etat, the material situation of the ruined Jewish small trader or artisan must be taken into account.
The manner of distributing social relief must be changed. The character of social relief must not be that of a charitable handout, but constructive help for the many ruined livelihoods which, with a small subsidy, can be put back on their feet.
As regards the Jewish schools, the new kehilla must know that if the old kehilla lost its standing among the masses, the school question is to blame for this in no small measure, because the mass of parents whose children attend the Jewish gymnasium rightly demanded that the paltry small subsidy that had been fixed be paid out.
We must remember that hundreds of children of the voters of our kehilla study in this school, and that the gymnasium is, after all, the pride of the town of Sosnowiec.
The present attitude towards all the institutions that are struggling in need for their hard existence must be changed; they are entitled at the very least to be represented in the expenditure of the budget in the same proportion as their percentage amounts to [?] in the income of the budget.
One could say much more about the kehilla and how it should be, but the space in a newspaper article is too small. One thing those who go into the kehilla must remember: how heavy is the responsibility and accountability towards the Jewish community which they take upon themselves with the running of the kehilla. Those who go there must be people suited to it, who are far from any selfishness and arrogance whatsoever. They must be ready to give their time and hard work to the Jewish kehilla with complete devotion to the cause, so that it may be the authoritative body which will worthily represent and protect the honour of Jewish Sosnowiec.
M. Z-ek.
New guild statutes must be adopted by the 4th of this month

[Artisans' guilds — statutes.] On the basis of the provisions of the amended guild (cech) law, all existing guilds must submit new statutes for approval by the 4th of September of this year. If by that deadline the new statutes are not submitted for approval, the guilds will be closed by the voivodeship [województwo].
The new statute must be adopted by a general meeting of the guild, which, according to the regulations, must take place in the course of the current month. After the statute has been adopted by the general meeting, it must be submitted to the starostwo [district office].
As we learn, however, because of the short deadline very few general meetings of the guilds have taken place to adopt the new statute; and at the meetings that did take place the members showed very little interest in the statute, because it is not at all suited to the needs of the guilds.
The guilds have, however, the right to apply to the authorities for an extension of the deadline for adopting the new statute by 6 months. All guilds can take advantage of this.
Important explanations concerning the new trades that have been classed as crafts

[Artisans — craft cards.] Recently a series of new trades have been classed as crafts and must belong to the category of handicraft, which may be carried on only with artisan's cards. To this category of new trades now belong: underwear sewing, corset making, etc.
Since many interested persons, both in Warsaw and in the provinces, are now applying to the United Committee for the Affairs of Jewish Crafts for explanations and information on this matter, the committee announces that those who registered their workshop with the industry office before the 36th [sic; read 30th] of June of this year must exchange the confirmation of their registration for artisan's cards.
Those who did not register their workshop and hold only patents [trade licences] must now register their workshops and enclose the patents as proof that they ran their workshop before the 30th of June of this year, and in this way they can obtain an artisan's card.
Those who hold no patents must endeavour to obtain a certificate from the magistrat [municipality] or the gmina [rural commune] that they ran a workshop before the 30th of June of this year. With these certificates they will be able to apply for artisan's cards.
Through Blood and Fire (A Letter from the Land of Israel)

[Land of Israel — letter; the 1936 Arab disturbances.]
Matek Hampel (Magdiel)
Dedicated to Bronia Kaplin of Zawiercie, who perished tragically.
For 4 months we have been living under the heavy nightmare, under the smoky atmosphere of the bloody events in the Land of Israel. For 4 months now the murderous hand has been stretched out against the Jewish Yishuv, which has not yet known such a bloody period in the history of its building. More than once have we already gone through the worst of days in the Land of Israel, more than once have we laid innocent victims on the altar of the idea of the Return to Zion, dozens and hundreds of dear martyrs. But what is happening now in the country — this we do not know. Not only we, but probably the whole progressive world does not know such horrifying murders, which go on for months, long months of blood and fire. We have already lived through several of the worst attacks in the Land of Israel; we have lived and are living through pogroms in the lands of the Diaspora; but all those „spontaneous“ events lasted a day or two, a week at most, and then order was more or less restored — and now we have been standing in the midst of the events for 4 months, and we do not know at all when there will be an end to the bloodshed in all corners of the country and to the fire that is eating the fruit of our hard work. How much longer? Until when? And there is no answer.
We know our neighbour, the Arab, not from today and not from yesterday. We know his psychology, his thinking and his life. We knew his „national“ movement, but we did not know the „freedom movement“ that for months has been calling for blood to be shed in the name of God, the „movement“ that trains its people to rob men, women and children and to murder from holes and mountains like venomous snakes and wild bloodthirsty beasts. We have the impression that the lowest instincts of man have run riot [?], and that the blackest and most evil spirits have awakened in order to annihilate, overthrow and destroy what we have created so laboriously and honestly over decades.
„Ala-Yahud!“ „At the Jew!“ — they tell the Arab neighbour, whom they drag by force out of his father's house and out of school. „Ala-Yahud“ — they tell the fellah (peasant), whom they tear by force from his field and family. „Here you have a knife, a bomb, a rifle — go into the holy war and murder every passing Jew, every woman, child and old man, no fear! It is a mitzvah to kill Jews; we promise you Paradise“... So teaches the „freedom“ movement, so teach the leaders, and this „Torah“ finds an echo, and indeed they go out against the Jew and lie in wait for him, and the unclean, accursed hand has already killed over 70 of our brothers and sisters, and the heart asks: will these already be the last victims? Will this already be the last horrifying page of a new „Yizkor“?
It was a bloody Friday, the 14th of August of this year, in Haifa. A car with several passengers — among them our comrade Bronia Kaplin, of blessed memory, from Zawiercie — set out from Mount Carmel on a visit to the woods there. They spent a few hours in the forest, delighting in its enchanting beauty and finding shelter from the burning sun in the shade of the tall trees. Here, in the lap of nature, when the soul enjoys so much beauty, tenderness and gentleness — young Bronia was far from any thought of death, dreaming of a new life, of a future. The Sabbath is approaching and one must return home. The same car drives back, and it has barely managed to go a few kilometres — suddenly an obstacle: the road is blocked with stones and there is no way in and no way out. The car stands still. An Arab appears on a horse, gives a signal with his hand and vanishes. A flood of bullets pours from all sides, the car is shot at, and the driver with his passengers soon meet their death. A short story, but full of blood and tears.
The martyr Bronia Kaplin, who perished so tragically in the Carmel hills, came from Zawiercie and had already been in the Land of Israel for 5 years. As a child she lost her parents, who left 3 daughters orphaned [?]. Bronia joins the pioneering youth movement, goes out to hachshara (training) and finally emigrates to the Land, full of eagerness and courage. On arriving in the country she joins a kibbutz of „Hashomer Hatzair“: „Ein HaKoreh“ in Rishon LeZion; here she becomes acclimatised, here she learns the new language, here she learns hard work and helps the kibbutz in its development. How many times did I meet her at work, and she always expressed her contentment with her new life on the mother-soil. Because of private circumstances she is forced to leave the kibbutz and goes to Tel Aviv, where she finds work as a children's nurse and then as a worker in the workers' kitchen in Tel Aviv. Leaving the kibbutz, parting from her closest comrades, does not pass without effect on her. She goes about with various plans, which she reveals only to a narrow circle of friends. She seeks rest for soul and body and travels to Mount Carmel. She wants to gather new strength, new energy for new work — and here comes the cruel hand and cuts the pulse of a young life, of a 25-year-old daughter — honour to her memory!
The pure souls of the 70 martyrs who perished for the „sanctification of the nation“ we will not accompany and bewail with dirges and wailing, although the heart is bursting with grief and pain; we will not take revenge in mutual [?] bloodshed, although the blood in our veins boils and seethes; we will not let our hands drop, although we are already physically exhausted from work by day and guard duty by night — with more strength, with more effort and with redoubled diligence and élan we will continue our work until the final victory of our idea.
To our brothers in exile we say: do not despair! Today's Yishuv of 400 thousand souls is not the Yishuv of 1929; we are strong enough, we can defend ourselves on our own, if only we are not hindered. We defend ourselves truly heroically, courageously, and more than one attack on the peaceful labour settlements has been repulsed by us. Annihilate, lay waste, burn, kill — we certainly could do that too, but we do not do it, not only because of our Jewish morality, because of the Jewish teaching: „Thou shalt not kill“, but also for political reasons. At every opportunity the Yishuv is called upon to show „havlaga“ (self-restraint), patience, forbearance, because we know that various factors in the country are interested in throwing us off balance and provoking a civil war, whose results would not be long in coming... For the time being we rely on the Government, which we accuse of neglecting its duties during these few painful months; we accuse the Government of a lack of responsibility towards the peaceful, industrious Jewish Yishuv; we accuse the Government, which strengthens the bloodied hands of the murderers, with whose leaders it conducts negotiations at our expense, the „sufferers“ [?], at the expense of „aliyah“ and land purchase. This Government, which lets the blood of children and women be shed, we will summon to judgment before the world tribunal, demanding a verdict for this pure blood that is being shed in Safed and in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv and Haifa, Kfar Saba and Hadera.
The sighs of the martyrs and their death-throes, the pain and suffering of the hundreds of wounded, the bitter weeping of the orphans and widows and the last prayer of the slain, „Shema Yisrael“ — must carry from all the ends of the world and must shake the conscience of mankind against the wrongs committed against us Jews in the lands of exile and in the Land of Israel, where we want to build a home for a better and finer tomorrow for the eternal Jew.
Jewish landlords, come to your senses

We are living through a time whose like, it seems, the history of mankind has never known.
A storm of lawlessness, wickedness and savagery is sweeping across the length and breadth of the world and laying waste, more and more, the minds and hearts of peoples and countries.
This plague, this [?] beast, is however felt most acutely by us Jews. On our weak shoulders we, poor souls, must bear all the evil winds, all the brutal moves and the direct reckonings of wrathful [?] and [?] hearts.
We are almost running out of strength to sigh and groan. We try to appeal to the world, we would like to demand of it the fairness of justice; we have proper grievances — why does no one listen to our weeping and our cries?
At the same time, however, we forget that in our own ranks the leprosy of arbitrariness and boorishness [chamstwo] is already running wild to no small degree; the fist decides, naked pocket-interest and striving [?] — and the tender feelings of compassion and humanity become deafened [?] and dulled.
In noting these phenomena we do not mean the whole complex of negative relations in Jewish life; this time we dwell on only one aspect, namely: the relationship of the Jewish house-owner to the Jewish tenant.
What else, then, can one call it, if not savagery and lawlessness — the growing number of cases in which landlords take no account of any legal proceedings, cast off their humanity and, exploiting a court verdict — be it one long shelved, one [?] long since paid off, or one obtained by a trick — carry out the cruellest evictions, with no wish [to spare] widows and orphans, old people and children.
Or one takes a hounded, worn-out [?] man, who in today's bitter times is choking for a penny's livelihood, and for the slightest delay in paying the rent, or for some other trifle of a few groszy, summons him to the courts, drives him into enormous costs, many times exceeding the actual sum, and later auctions off from his home his last poor bits of household goods.
And with all this these heartless, thick-skinned creatures still remain "fine Jews". They go on occupying the eastern wall in the shtiblekh and societies, or the seat of honour in other spheres of life.
We do not say that a landlord must forever let an impoverished tenant live in his house for free; but he must show understanding, come to terms with him in a humane way, and on no account let it come to an eviction or a distraint.
For an eviction is a cruel act, a desecration of the most sacred human feelings. If in normal times such a distraint was ugly and mean, today it is atrocious, murderous.
Y. A.
Beauty aids — then and now

By Z. Haber, Vienna.
There is nothing new under the sun. Whoever thinks that all the beauty aids women use today were born only recently is greatly mistaken. We know precisely that already in ancient Roman times women used all sorts of preparations for the face and the hair. We just do not know what these preparations consisted of, and the descriptions that exist from those times are very unclear.
Before me lies a booklet from the year 1796 — a certain Francet [?] from Paris [printed "Parin"] brought various beauty aids to sell at the Leipzig fair, and for this he published a description of what these preparations he wished to sell consisted of. In this description we find almost the same preparations that women use today.
Smearing the face with eggs or laying sweet cucumbers on it, as is done today, was known already then. From eggs they made a little dough [?] mixed with barley flour and packed the face in it overnight or for a couple of hours in the daytime. Of sweet cucumbers they used only the juice and washed the face with it.
Red colour for the face was also used then. The colour was made from red beets [?] ("Rüben"). Later people began to smear the face with colour from a red paper, which badly damaged the skin.
Powder, of course, was also used then, but mostly these were waters with which one washed the face — when the water dried, a white flour remained on the face. In the beauty salons of the great world they are now also beginning to use liquid powder, which is supposed to be healthier than other colours.
Certainly they also knew of flour powder; they had powders for pale faces and for red faces.
Dyes for eyebrows and hair, too, were known 150 years ago; they had exactly the same preparations as today, only the little bottle, the jar, the little brush and the like have changed. Today they are merely called differently and have prettier labels.
In those times women also made themselves blue under the eyes, so as to look more interesting, just as today; but the best means of beautifying the face was held to be camomile tea. The face was packed in soaked camomile herbs, wrapped in cloths dipped in hot camomile tea, and it seems it really was worth something, because this cheap home remedy has survived to this day.
It is worth telling, too, that until the year 1740 it was forbidden in many countries, England among them, to paint the face, to wear false or dyed hair, to wear false teeth and to use artificial means in order to seduce men. For this women were put in "prison" for up to 5 years, and if she did not mend her ways even afterwards, she could, according to the law, be punished by death.
Whether this did any good, we do not know to this day.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion

[Oneg Shabbat — weekly Torah portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parshat Tavo
—o—
a) "And it shall be, when thou art come into the land" (26:1)
The preceding portion ends with "thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven", and only then — "And it shall be, when thou art come into the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance, and possessest it, and dwellest therein"; for as long as Amalek has not been exterminated, as long as Amalek still lives somewhere, you will not have the land; what is more[?], he will turn your land into a field of blood[?]. First blot out the remembrance of Amalek, and then — "when thou art come into the land".. Leket Amarim.
—o—
b) "I profess this day unto the Lord thy God, that I am come unto the land."
"I profess this day" — "every day it shall be in your eyes as new": the Land of Israel is conquered every day; every day of living in the Land of Israel means conquering it afresh... Imrei Chen.
—o—
c) "And we cried unto the Lord God of our fathers" (ibid., 7)
We are actually crying out for God's sake: so to speak, He is badly off in exile, the Jews cannot stay faithful to Him; and "he who prays for his fellow while needing the same thing himself is answered first" — so we pray for Him, so to speak, in order that we be helped first in our own affairs. And when "we cried unto the Lord God of our fathers", when we pray for His sake, then — "the Lord heard our voice, and looked on our affliction"... He sees our bodily suffering. Kiflayim le-Tushiya.
—o—
d) "This day" (ibid., 16)
Everything is about one day: both the evil inclination and the good inclination want no more from a person than one day. Tomorrow you may already be different — only today be so...
And on this, indeed, everything depends! Amarim Shnunim.
—o—
e) "This day thou art become the people" (27:9)
A Polish rabbi once reproached R' Samson Raphael Hirsch that it is not the Jewish way to write books in foreign languages; that is already half-assimilation.
R' Samson Raphael Hirsch answered him:
— Remarkable: after Moses had written the Torah on the stones in seventy languages, God said to him: "This day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God." That is to say: on the day the Torah was written down in all languages, and the whole world could become acquainted with lofty Jewish ethics — then the Jews became a people, and precisely "the people of the Lord thy God"...
—o—
f) "And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God" (28:1)
"And overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God" — the blessings shall reach you even when you are a pious man, "if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord"; for mostly, when a person is pious, when he heeds God's commandments, it is rare that he is blessed with all of that... Ha'amek Davar.
—o—
g) "The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee" (28:7)
Before it comes the verse: "Blessed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and blessed shalt thou be when thou goest out" — both when you leave a country and when you enter a country, there are always enemies rising up against you; nothing pleases them: both when you arrive and want to build up a country, and when you want to leave a country. There were times in England when Jews were not allowed to leave the country, because by doing so they would have harmed the country... Divrei Yehoshua.
—o—
h) "And thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow" (ibid., 12)
For mostly, he who lends money to another must later himself become a borrower... Otzar ha-Chaim.
* * *
And then the following verse ends: "And the Lord shall make thee the head, and not the tail", and so too in verse 43. It must be — said R' Eizel Charif [R' Yehoshua Isaac Shapiro of Słonim] in jest — that lending money is not one of the superfluous wisdoms...
—o—
i) "A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person" (28:50)
"These are the 974 generations that were crumpled up and not created; the Holy One, blessed be He, arose and planted them in every generation, and they are the brazen-faced of the generation." Tractate Chagigah.
And just as in every pack of a larger quantity the small ones are placed on top and the big ones at the bottom, so too with the brazen-faced: God first spread out[?] the small ones, and left the big ones for the footsteps of the Messiah... Patshegen Ktav.
—o—
j) "And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you"
A time will come when you offer yourselves as bondmen and bondwomen, as those who serve the rulers slavishly — and you will not be gladly taken by them[?]: "and no man shall buy you". They will no longer want to buy your servility, your "Ma Yafit" [obsequious fawning]... Imrei Chen.
The festive closing of the Katowice kehilla's children's camp

As is well known, the Jewish community of Katowice distinguishes itself in the field of education, to which it devotes large sums from its budget for the upkeep of a kindergarten, schools and the Talmud Torah (our towns in Zagłębie do not think much of such things; they have other, more important matters to attend to). Besides this, the Katowice kehilla takes care of the children's health, and in recent years, thanks to the efforts of Dr. Kaufmann, Mrs. Neumann and others, summer camps for needy children are organised every summer. This summer too such a camp was organised in Jeleśnia, in 3 shifts, which 140 children enjoyed. The community spent 8 thousand złoty on it, but it was worth it, because the camp was so well set up[?] and organised that the children had all good things and were under good supervision, both in the religious and in the hygienic sense — and this must be strongly emphasised and underlined, because in other charitable camps, regrettably, this is not so. I know of facts where small children brought back with them from the camps "pa[—]us" and "szchienszbes"[?] as well... [garbled Polish words, apparently Catholic devotional items or prayers.] Therefore the Jewish community in Katowice should be a model for the Zagłębie kehillot, especially for the kehilla now being elected[?].
In the last days before the camp closed, Dr. Kaufmann, Dr. Lipmann, Mrs. Neumann and others came from Katowice and brought presents for the children, which were distributed in the form of a lottery draw. The children gave a fine performance and spent a whole day with the distinguished guests. From my conversation with the guests I learned that the Katowice kehilla enlarges its activity every year in the field of charitable and public welfare, regardless of the greatest exertions.
On Thursday evening the children organised a "medura" (a bonfire), around which they "fierily" [pun: feierlich = festively / Feuer = fire] closed the camp with song.
Elchanan Zider.
Public Declaration to the Jewish Population of Będzin

In connection with the latest events in the Jewish kehilla in Będzin, we consider it our duty to issue the following declaration:
1) We declare that the struggle being waged against the president of the board, Mr. Rubinlicht, in no way bears a personal character between Mr. „Landger[?]—Rubinlicht", as the „Torah-true" Jews with Mr. Rubinlicht at their head wish to pretend. This hypocritical interpretation is obvious enough, and everyone understands that it aims to cover up the truth and to sow confusion of minds among the broad Jewish masses.
2) We solemnly declare that we stand in solidarity with the honest struggle against Mr. Rubinlicht for his deeds. Having been elected president of the kehilla board with the votes of the national groupings, he allowed himself to abuse the presidency we had entrusted to him, and shamefully deserted the national camp, became a „turncoat" in the Agudah camp, votes openly with the „Agudah" and comes out publicly against the national interests. We therefore demand, in the name of human dignity, in the name of ethics and according to all accepted parliamentary custom, that Mr. Rubinlicht resign immediately from his presidency of the kehilla. Nobody has the right to act thus and abuse the mandate we entrusted to him; so is every person who has a spark of human dignity obliged to act. Even more painful is the matter when a man can allow himself to say publicly „I spit on the entire Jewish community": it is truly chutzpah when such a man still wants the honour of representing the Jewish community, and with the greatest indignation we must cry out: shame and disgrace!
3) As long as the accusations (of a material nature) against Mr. Rubinlicht have not been established as incorrect and he has not been rehabilitated by the elected council commission, Mr. Rubinlicht must leave all the honorary offices he holds in Jewish public life.
4) We protest and express our greatest indignation against the shameful attempts of the Agudist „daveres"[?] with Mr. Rubinlicht at their head, and especially against the freshly baked president of the council, Mr. Ryński[?], who wish by illegal means to rob Mr. Landger[?] of his mandate, in order to render him harmless in his courageous and honest struggle against the demoralising kehilla administration.
5) We also draw the attention of the entire Jewish community to the struggle being waged around the affair of Mr. Mendel Lewin, where Mr. Rubinlicht supports the „Agudah" with all his strength in order to force through the candidacy of Mr. Lewin, which from the very outset was created by repressive means and with the help of outside factors.
It is the duty of the entire Jewish community to take stock of this unheard-of scandal, which may become „a wrong that cannot be righted" and „a lament for generations", a disgrace for us, „a city and mother in Israel" such as the Jewish kehilla in Będzin, that such a thing should happen.
