A Bit of "Pshat" on the Candidate Lists.
Yelamdenu rabbenu — let our rabbis teach us: for what reason, why is the number of all the lists in our holy community neither more nor less than 14 (the numerical value of "dai" — "enough")? Because He who said to His world "Enough!" will say "Enough!" to our generations [?] and to our lists and to our little benches of kapores [?] —
to atone for all our sins...
Chatskele Khalbonis on the Blocs

Chatskele has always been a weak politician; where there is politics — says Chatskele — there is falsehood. — But when it comes to Jewish "unity", Chatskele can no longer keep quiet; he plucked up courage and handed the bloc-makers the true verdict, and he says:
As it looks to me, the whole gang [?] can go into my left heel [?]. It doesn't matter to me in life whether you sit in the kehilla or sit at home. Did I have any great benefit [korzyść?] from you when you were in the kehilla? Never mind [nie szkodzi] — don't sit in the kehilla, you have other livelihoods [?]. But one thing I don't understand: why do you prattle ["bang a teakettle"] about programmes and platforms — why don't you tell the truth?
Chatskele still wanted to say a few words, but in the middle he remembered and asked:
I don't know — when does the new moon [molad] fall?..
Election Appeal!

To all voters!
The day of the great Day of Judgement is approaching, when it will be judged who is to become the Dozór [kehilla board] and who is to stay at home with his mandate.
This is a very important matter; no one may make light of it, and a great duty lies upon every citizen, as a Jew, a human being and a compassionate person, to support with all his strength, in the present critical time, the philanthropic campaign to provide 2 minyanim of Jews with little benches for a period of five years.
No one may hold back; let everyone go to the ballot box and cast his ballot for me.
I promise to defend my interests in the best possible way.
Berele Benkl-Zukher [Berele Bench-Seeker].
Jewesses and "Panienkas"

Members of the female sex, unite!
(A memorandum, za przeproszeniem [pardon the expression], on the kehilla elections in Sosnowiec)
Szanowne przyjaciółki [Honoured friends]!
A [?] świństwo [dirty trick] has been done in the women's street. Openly and frankly our womanly honour has been robbed; without "pardon" the wstrętne [disgusting] men have [?] us and taken away our voting rights. The enemies [?] closed our mouths at the gmina [community] elections; they are robbing us of the only weapon we possess: the nine measures of talk!
We women [?] — since we and only we are the living nerve of society, since without us there is no wedding — we must get into the gmina and "clean out" the "zhaber" [?] that for years has nested in every corner; the whole management must pass into our hands.
First of all we will take care of the hospital system: a grandiose maternity clinic must be built with all wygody [comforts] for little wives [?] who [?].
We must demand a revision of the housing decree [?], so that the sublokatorzy [subtenants] receive "autonomous rights" and have a "voice" in the management.
The outdated decree of khupe-vekidushin must be reformed so that the wedding canopy and betrothal will be required only after the wedding.
The kehilla administration must publish, at its own expense, a wedding organ.
Every month the kehilla is to publish a brand-new fashion magazine.
Jewesses and panienkas, if we keep to a "zamknięte kółko" [closed circle], we can liczyć [count] on pełne powodzenie [full success].
The General Women's Election Committee for the kehilla elections in Sosnowiec.
A Clever Answer

Husband (to his wife): Gutshe, what is that supposed to mean — yesterday I saw your photograph in a wives' placement bureau?
Wife: Oh, it's nothing; I handed the photograph in to the bureau 5 years ago already, when you were — not to be mentioned today — sick with the flu.
Practical Advice

How to behave at the election meetings.
The "Kokh-lefl" ["Cooking Ladle"] here gives practical instructions on how to take part in the election meetings successfully and unharmed, without being injured, strangled, slaughtered, crushed and killed [?] in the process.
1) If on the day of the meeting you were in the bathtub and took only a bath with a Priessnitz compress and had no massage, then enter the meeting by the front door.
2) The best and "most comfortable" place is by the presidium.
3) Your boots must be shod with iron, so that when you stamp and tramp with your feet you will not tear the soles, pardon — the "zoyln" [?]...
4) Before you go to the "wiec" [rally], cut the corns [odciski] off your feet, so that nobody treads on them.
5) Over your woollen undershirt put on an iron cuirass, for the tzitzit alone can protect you only against demons, but not against your [?] "bakes" [?]...
6) If someone tears your coat [palto], take the cotton wadding [watolina] out of the lining [podszewka] and stuff your ears with it, so that you hear the shrieking a few tones lower...
7) At a meeting it is advisable to wear a stiff hat [kapelusz], so that the packs of proclamations and placards thrown down from the gallery will pierce only the hat, but not your head...
8) On coming home from the meeting, take something to make you sweat, rub yourself with French turpentine, have yourself given 50 wet [cut] cupping glasses, put a cold compress on your head, next morning take a bath with Ciechocinek salt, and have yourself transferred for three weeks to the Jewish hospital — and we guarantee you that you will then be almost a normal person.
I Believe.

I believe with perfect faith that every party wants to get mandates through. Whether they will get them through — is a big doubt.
* * *
I believe with perfect faith that the Aleksandrów Hasidim are going together with the Koziegłowy Hasidim. Whether they will vote for the Koziegłowy people — is a big doubt.
* * *
I believe with perfect faith that the "Srebners"[?] are going together with the Right "Poalei Zion". Whether they will vote for the P.Z. — is a big doubt.
* * *
I believe with perfect faith that the National Camp wants to have a majority in the new kehilla. Whether it will indeed have a majority — is a big doubt.
In the Tangle of Life.

(A novel with dramatic events in Kraków, Zawiercie and New York)
(9
Michael began to come and visit them. Usually he came to see Masha, but Masha was not as pretty as Emma, who had her mother's beautiful big eyes. Michael began to show more interest in Emma, and Emma for her part felt for the first time that she had at last met a man whom she could love; she was drawn to him, and when he proposed that she meet him alone, she was unable to refuse the invitation. But so as not to hurt Masha, Emma arranged that they meet outside, mostly in the park. It did not take long and both were in love, truly and sincerely in love with one another.
When Masha found out about it, she had a sharp conversation with Emma, and Emma soon moved out of the flat.
For a long time Masha could not calm down; she was waiting for an opportunity to settle accounts with Emma.
When Emma lived with Masha, Joe used to come up from time to time, despite the scandal with Bernard; he was still in love with Emma and was not afraid of Bernard.
Masha was waiting for Joe to come so that she could tell him what had happened to her and that Emma was about to marry Michael soon; she knew that he would surely do something.
But as if out of spite Joe did not show up; she was very disappointed that her partner was not there just when she needed him so badly.
On the other side, Michael found it very hard to settle down in America. He had been brought up in Vienna among artists and had distinguished himself with his paintings already as a child, but he could not make a living from it; his parents were also poor and could not help him — on the contrary, whenever he could, he himself still helped his mother, who was none other than — Thelma, the Christian woman who as a student had been Dor's beloved. Yes, Dor was Michael's father. Thelma later married a government official, Arthur Sanders, and Michael received the family name of his stepfather — Sanders. But after the war, when the upheaval took place in Vienna, his stepfather lost his post and could not get another; he took up bookkeeping, but from that he could barely earn a dry piece of bread.
Michael's stepfather, Arthur, was younger than his mother Thelma; he longed to leave poor Vienna, he very much wanted to go to America, but he did not have the money for the expenses. Arthur and Michael got on very[?] well, almost like two brothers.
Before he left Paris, Michael had assured his parents in a letter that as soon as he came to America he would at once try to bring them over.
When Emma fell so deeply in love with him and began to talk of marriage, he said:
— What does it mean to marry, when I cannot even make a living for myself.
Emma had a different calculation: after all, she was studying at a school and had food and lodging; she therefore told Michael that he would not have to worry about her, and whatever he earned he could keep for himself; let them marry and have even one room, and when she was free she could come home and be with him.
Michael agreed, but at the same time he revealed a secret to her. He told her he wanted her to know in advance that he was not a full Jew; he was not religious, and indeed he had been brought up in a Catholic home. His mother is Catholic and his father was a Jew. Where his father is he does not know; he had never seen him.
Emma assured him that all those things did not bother her; she was interested only in him himself.
— But now comes the most important thing — Michael told her — I have written to my mother that the first thing I will do in America will be to bring her and my stepfather here. So I cannot marry; I want to bring them here.
— And what does it depend on for you?
— On money.
— How much?
— Expenses for two people, at least 300 dollars.
— I will give you 500 dollars.
— You will give me 500 dollars to bring my parents? Where will you get so much money? — Michael asked in surprise.
— Yes, I will give you the money, only you must never ask me where I got the money.
— I promise you!
— If so, you will have the money tomorrow evening; send it to them right away. See me tomorrow at 7 o'clock in the evening.
A little later Emma telephoned Bernard.
— Bernard, I need 500 dollars and I want you to bring me the money!
— All right — Bernard answered her.
— But I will take it on one condition: you must not ask me what I need it for.
— Also all right — Bernard agreed good-naturedly.
— Then bring me the money to the hospital, to my room.
The next day Bernard brought Emma 500 dollars.
In the evening Michael already had the money, and on the following day he sent it off to his parents together with the necessary papers.
It did not take long and Michael received a letter from his mother and stepfather saying that they were setting out. Of course they also wrote him on which ship they were travelling and when he should expect them in New York.

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: A Large Consultation on the Catastrophic Situation of the Talmud Torah

What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 17 Elul 5696 — piątek 4 września 1936 [Friday, 4 September 1936].)
Będzin
A large consultation on the catastrophic situation of the Talmud Torah.
On Tuesday evening, on the initiative of President Mr. Fürstenberg, a consultation was held in the kehilla premises on the catastrophic situation of the local "Talmud Torah".
Taking part in the consultation were the dayanim Lipszyc and Frydberg, as well as a larger number of householders from all strata of the local Jewish population.
In his speech Mr. Fürstenberg criticised the Orthodox section, and in particular the rabbinate, which stands aloof from the religious institution.
After the discussion, in which Rabbi Frydberg, President Rubinlicht, President Rigski[?], A. Tenenbaum and others spoke, Mr. Fürstenberg's proposal was adopted that a committee be created to carry out a fund-raising collection and [set up] a new board.
Ordered: Mr. Landger Must Be Allowed to See the Kehilla's Minutes
On the basis of the interventions, the kehilla board received by telephone an order to give Mr. Landger the opportunity to acquaint himself with the minutes of the kehilla meetings.
The Magistrate Is to Come Forward with a Proposal That the Express Trains Stop in Będzin

At Monday's meeting of the city board the interpellation of the residents of Ksawera was considered, that the local trains should stop at Ksawera.
In connection with this, alderman (ławnik) Mr. Rechnic submitted a proposal that at the same time the Magistrate, together with the Starostwo (district office), should intervene so that the express ("courier") trains stop at the local station.
New Committee of the Religious Artisans

In the premises of the "Mizrachi"[?] a farewell evening was held on Sunday[?] evening in honour of the president of the religious artisans, Mr. Yechezkel Wrocławski, who has emigrated with his family to the Land of Israel.
After the greetings a new committee was elected, consisting of: Moshe Dawid Plesner (president), Yosef Barchinek[?] (vice), Chaim Majtlis (secretary), Ch. M. Zylberberg, A. Elbaum and Moshe Szpajzer.
Jewish Workers on the Public Works Will Not Have to Work on the High Holidays

A group of Jewish workers employed on the public works turned to alderman Mr. Rechnic to intervene with the Magistrate so that their working days be allotted in such a way that they will not have to work on the days of the High Holidays (Yamim Nora'im).
As reported, the engineer promised to settle the matter in favour of the Jewish workers.
Stationery Shops May Stay Open until 8 p.m. This Month

The board of the Small Traders' Association intervened with the starosta and the police commissioner to permit stationery shops to stay open during the current month from 7.30 in the morning until 8 in the evening.
The above-mentioned authorities promised to settle the matter favourably.
He "Treated" the Customer to a Piece of Cloth over the Head

Motl Lencman, a tailor from Strzemieszyce[?], came to the editorial office and related the following fact:
On Tuesday Lencman was at the firm H., where he wanted to buy a piece of cloth of 16 metres, and when he offered 1 zł. less than Mr. H. had asked, he received from Mr. H. a blow over the head with that very piece of cloth, from which he fell into a faint.
Lencman reported this to the police and also obtained a certificate from Dr. Kaszybowicz[?], and the epilogue will take place in court.
Sosnowiec — One Generation Goes and Another Comes...

Sosnowiec
One generation goes and another comes...
A Jew who does not want his child circumcised, and a Christian who wants to convert to Judaism...
At Rabbi Schwarz's the following characteristic scene took place in recent days:
A young man, a resident of Sosnowiec, comes to the rabbi to register his child, a little boy.
"Has the bris already taken place?" the rabbi asks him.
"What bris, who needs a bris — I don't hold with such 'superstitions' ('zabobony') and I won't have my child circumcised."
"If the child is not circumcised, I as a rabbi cannot register him."
[Phrase unclear: "פך הוות"[?], probably 'in short'.] The rabbi would not register the child, and the young fellow went away.
At that very moment a Christian came in and told the rabbi that he wanted to convert to Judaism.
"In these present harsh persecutions of the Jews you want to convert?"
"I don't want to be a burden to anyone," the Christian answers, "I possess several thousand zł. I just want to go over to Judaism for the sake of my Jewish bride from Będzin."
The rabbi referred the Christian to the rabbinate in Bielsko (Bielitz).
Jewish tenant stabs his Jewish landlord

On Monday an incident occurred in Dańdówka[?] that illustrates the relations prevailing between landlords and tenants.
The tenant Szmul Lejb Perlgerycht was moving out of Weiler's[?] house. At a certain moment a sharp quarrel broke out between the two parties, during which Perlgerycht, a shoe-upper stitcher by trade, stabbed Jechezkiel Weidler with a shoemaker's knife; Weidler was taken to the hospital at Pekin.
District conference of Betar

On Sunday a district conference of Betar took place in its own premises.
On behalf of the headquarters, the Netziv's officer (katzin ha-netzivut) Sanimonski[?] took part in the conference.
Various lectures on organisational and educational matters were heard, on which a very interesting discussion developed.
A series of resolutions was adopted, among others to organise in winter, on the estate[?] of Mr. Citer[?] in Przeszla[?], a winter colony, as well as a two-week synthetic[?] course for branch leaders (menahalim).
Finally a district command was appointed with the following composition:
Lazinger, Triger (Sosnowiec), Sztajn (Będzin), Cukrowski (Dąbrowa).
The seat of the district command is in Sosnowiec.
A counterfeit-money factory in a peasant's hut

For some time false 10-złoty coins have been circulating in Zagłębie. After a period of surveillance the police succeeded in discovering the factory, which was located in the dwelling of a peasant in the village of Sarni[?].
During the search 13 false 10-złoty coins were found, together with the entire equipment for manufacturing the counterfeit money.
The manufacturer and his son have been arrested.
—o—
Shop windows of Jewish businesses smeared.
In the night from Sunday to Monday the shop windows were smeared of Strazum's[?] butter[?] shop, Jankowski's cloth shop, Fun's[?] shoe shop „Maan“[?] and the pharmacy warehouse „Sanitas“.
—o—
Tram conductor sentenced to 8 months' prison.
Before the local district court the trial took place of a tram conductor who was accused of having caused the death of the 66-year-old Gresz of Dąbrowa.
The conductor was sentenced to 8 months' prison.
New achievements in radio

Among radio enthusiasts the news has recently spread of an extraordinary radio achievement which will undoubtedly be a new era in radio history. One of the main radio factories is preparing for the current season a new type of set which for the first time is adapted to transmit the sound stereophonically. The sounds possess a clarity such as has not existed until now, and a softness of tone. The human voice and every musical instrument come out naturally, thanks to which the listener has the proper[?] direct impression.
Election meeting of List 13

On Saturday at 2 o'clock in the afternoon an election meeting organised by the Malkhut Yisrael movement (List 13) will take place in the courtyard of Mr. Warman[?].
The well-known speakers will appear at the meeting: Dir. M. Bernsztajn (Warsaw), Dr. J. Szechter (Kraków), R.R.[?] M. Gros and J. Elster.
300 „dead“ voters are on the electoral rolls

The agents of List 7, while checking the electoral rolls, found about 300 persons who must be struck off, because many of that number are already in the world of truth, some have emigrated, and so on.
The „discovery“ has been communicated to the election commission.
A Sosnowiec woman collects donations for „Przytyk“ in Wilno
In Wilno a certain Mrs. Rosensztajn[?] of Sosnowiec was arrested; she had been collecting donations around the city for the Jews who suffered in Przytyk and Mińsk Mazowiecki.
Saturday — opening of the theatre season
This Saturday at 8.30 in the evening the winter season will be opened at the local municipal theatre. „Głupi Jakub“, a comedy in 4 acts, will be performed.
Dąbrowa: The Starostwo validates the disqualified election lists.

As is known, the election commission disqualified 4 election lists of the following groups: Rabbi Epstein, the Revisionists, the Najfeld [?] people and the tailors' guild.
Those concerned [?] intervened in the matter at the Starostwo, where the disqualified lists were recognised as valid.
—o—
The Epstein–Rechnic affair is to be settled by an arbitration court.
Last Friday the trial of R' Baruch Epstein was to have taken place at the municipal court in Będzin; he had been accused by the former kehilla president Mr L. Rechnic, [on the grounds] that he had demanded a bribe from Epstein.
Because both parties agreed in court to a court of honour, the trial did not take place.
—o—
Rode into a Jew.
On Sunday, as M. Rybsztajn was walking along Kr[ólowej] Jadwigi Street, he was run over by a bicycle ridden by a young Christian.
Rybsztajn, who fell onto the pavement, was badly injured.
—o—
Car kills a horse.
In the Redeń colony, on Friday towards evening, a Jewish carter from Strzemieszyce was driving along. At that moment a car ran into the cart and killed the horse on the spot.
—o—
From the Zionist election campaign.
For the kehilla elections taking place on Sunday, 14 candidate lists have been submitted. Attention is drawn to the Zionist list (No. 10) as almost the only one not involved in the previous administration, which was constantly in the abyss. Both the people who appear in the first places of this list and the organisation itself give a full guarantee that their entering the fight is exclusively for the sake of reorganising the lamentable kehilla economy, for the good of the whole Jewish population. A special lustre is given to the Zionist list by its top candidate, the esteemed Prof. Dr Icchak Steinberg, who is known for his pure honesty and high intellectualism. Bringing Dr Steinberg into the kehilla signals an end to the dismissive attitude towards this kehilla institution and the beginning of a new era in the kehilla, of its economic and social momentum.

Life in Kielce — The Candidate List of the Bootmakers' Guild Disqualified

[Page head "Life in Kielce"; Kielce — Kehilla elections.]
Life in Kielce
(Date boxes: Friday, 17 Elul 5696 — piątek 4 września 1936 [Friday, 4 September 1936].)
The candidate list of the bootmakers' guild disqualified.
As has already been reported in our paper, candidate list number 8, of the bootmakers' guild, was disqualified by the election commission and afterwards confirmed by the starosta [district head]. On Friday a notice suddenly arrived at the kehilla from the voivodeship office that the said list had been disqualified again.
The head of the list, Mr. Granatman[?] (of Dąbrowa), therefore travelled this week to Warsaw, where he lodged an appeal with the ministry against the decision of the voivodeship office. At the ministry several Orthodox men intervened on behalf of his list, headed by the "Agudist" lawyer Mr. Erlich.
As we are informed, the ministry has requested the list from the voivodeship office, in order to acquaint itself with the decisions of the first and second instance.
The Radomsko Hasidim for List Number 12

[Kielce — Kehilla elections.]
A delegation of the Radomsko Hasidim approached the election committee of the Religious-National Bloc (number 12) and declared that all the Radomsko Hasidim will vote this Sunday for list number 12, on which there figures as first candidate their comrade and long-standing worshipper, the well-known Mizrachi activist Yehoshua Bekerman.
The Intelligentsia Club for List Number 12

[Kielce — Kehilla elections.]
As we are informed, the board of the local intelligentsia club has instructed its members to vote for list number 12, on which there figure their member, the director of the Jewish gymnasium, Mr. Dr. Sauer, and as first candidate for the kehilla board — Prof. Baruch Graubard.
Who Has Concluded Technical Joint-List Agreements with Whom?

[Kielce — Kehilla elections.]
Of the 11 electoral lists for the kehilla council that were submitted to the election commission, 4 technical joint-list agreements were concluded this week, namely: 1) the Zionist-Mizrachi bloc (list number 12) concluded a technical bloc with the League (list number 5); 2) "Aguda", the merchants' association and "Poalei Agudat Yisrael"; 3) the Chmielnik, Chęciny and Aleksander Hasidim with the artisans' association; and 4) the small traders' association with the "Shul" [synagogue party] (R' Yashki Fishman with R' Meir Wlasta[?]...).
Lessons Have Begun in the Jewish Schools

[Kielce — Education.]
Yesterday, Thursday, on the first day of the new school year, lessons already partly began in all the Jewish schools in Kielce.
Last Great Election Meeting of List Number 12

[Kielce — Kehilla elections.]
Tomorrow, Saturday, at 4 o'clock in the afternoon, the last great election meeting of the Religious-National Bloc (Zionists and Mizrachi) will take place in the Mizrachi premises (Bodzentyńska 3).
—o—
50 Per Cent Rail Discounts from Kielce to Warsaw
[Kielce — Transport.]
From the 6th to the 13th of this month one will be able to travel from Kielce to Warsaw for 10 zł. there and back. Discount cards are issued by the tourist travel bureaus and the "Ruch" bookshops.
—o—
2 Złoty 50 Groszy from Kielce to Radom
[Kielce — Transport; Polish politics.]
For the great rally which the P.P.S. is organising on Sunday the 6th of this month, in honour of the 30th anniversary of "Bloody Wednesday" for the independence of Poland, several popular trains will leave Kielce for Radom at dawn on Sunday. The price of a railway ticket, there and back, costs no more than two złoty and 50 groszy. The trains depart from Radom to Kielce the same day at 9 o'clock in the evening. Discount tickets are obtainable at the P.P.S. secretariat.
—o—
The High Holidays in the Zionist Organisation
[Kielce — Religion and holidays.]
As every year, this year too a minyan for Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur will be arranged in the splendid and hygienic halls of the Zionist club. First-class, well-known cantors have already been engaged. Registration cards are obtainable at the secretariat every day from 8 to 10 in the evening.
Tragic Death of a Kielce Jewish Doctor in Vilna

[Kielce — Mourning.]
This Monday the 26-year-old doctor of medicine Hirsh Goldfarb, son of the well-known local industrialist Moritz Goldfarb, met a tragic death in Vilna. The funeral of the tragically deceased young Goldfarb took place in Vilna on Wednesday, the 2nd of this month.
A Year and a Half in Prison for Torturing the Children and Feeding Them with... Urine

[Kielce — Courts.]
A few days ago there sat on the defendants' bench in the Kielce district court a certain Christian, Maksymilian Doliga[?], with his 38-year-old mistress, Agnieszka Katryba[?]; he had been brought to judicial account for torturing in a merciless and bestial manner his minor children, whom he had also fed for about two years with... urine.
The cruel father was sentenced to a year and a half in prison, and his mistress, who had helped him torture the children — to one year in prison.
Last Deadline for Paying the Income Tax

[News — taxes.] For all merchants and manufacturers who received payment orders (nakazy) for this year's income tax before 16 August [sierpień], the last deadline for paying the tax is 15 September [wrzesień]. After this deadline penalties with interest will already be added, and there is the right to carry out an immediate [?] distraint (execution).
Those who received the payment orders later have as their last deadline for payment 30 days after receiving the order.
It should be noted in this connection that the heads of the tax office have the authority to allow the tax to be paid in instalments, in 6 monthly instalments over the period up to 1 April [kwiecień] 1937. These concessions, however, are [readily?] granted only to those who apply about it before the last deadline expires.

Premier Składkowski — honorary citizen of Czeladź.
On Tuesday, at an extraordinary session of the Czeladź town council, the resolution of the town administration to confer on Premier Składkowski the title of honorary citizen of Czeladź was adopted.

„To be or not to be“
Jabotinsky's lecture in Sosnowiec yesterday.
Yesterday evening the president of the New Zionist Organisation, Wł. Jabotinsky, lectured in the „Palace“ cinema in Sosnowiec on „To be or not to be“.
In his lecture the speaker touched on the most topical problems that stand on the agenda at the present moment.
The huge audience listened with great attention to what he said about the present tense situation in Zionism.

Next Monday, on his way from Paris to Warsaw, the French Minister of Commerce Bastid will stop in Katowice.

A big butter theft.
In the night from Wednesday to Thursday the back door of Barnsztajn's butter shop in Będzin was broken open, and a large quantity of butter goods was stolen from it.

A shoemaker's bestial deed.
The 29-year-old Senderowicz[?], a Christian shoemaker, having „accounts to settle“ with his sweetheart, slaughtered her with a shoemaker's knife.
After carrying out the bestial murder, Senderowicz[?] came to the police station and confessed that he had murdered his „przyjaciółka“ (girlfriend) because she had betrayed him.
Senderowicz[?] also robbed his victim of 40 zł.

Yesterday morning Będzin welcomed Inspector-General Rydz-Śmigły.
On the platform of the railway station in Będzin there gathered yesterday representatives of the administration, the municipal authorities, Polish and Jewish public organisations with their banners at their head, and hundreds of schoolchildren of the Jewish and Polish secondary and elementary schools, to welcome the Inspector-General of the army, Rydz-Śmigły.
As the train approached, the orchestra played the national anthem and the air rang with the cries: „Niech żyje“ („Long live!“).
The ovations lasted until the train was far away.

From „HaNoar HaTsiyoni“
In connection with the loss the movement has suffered through the death of Yitzchak Steiner, a memorial lecture was held in the premises of „HaNoar HaTsiyoni“, attended by 400 people.
Mr. Ribin Gis[?] [spoke] in moving[?] words about the great merits of the deceased, who was the creator and founder of the Polish Zionist youth movement „HaNoar HaTsiyoni“, about the role he played in its founding and also about his merits for Zionism in P.Y.[?]. With his death the Zionist Organisation has suffered an irreparable loss.
With the scout call „Chazak ve'ematz“ the lecture was closed.
— On the same day a memorial meeting was held at „HaNoar HaTsiyoni“ in Sosnowiec, at which the memory of Yitzchak Steiner was honoured.
This Sabbath a festive lecture will take place in the premises of „HaNoar HaTsiyoni“ in honour of the opening of the new working year.

Rabbi Gold in Zagłębie.
The president of the „Mizrachi“ in America, Rabbi Gold, is staying in Zagłębie with his daughter on family matters.
Rabbi Gold will probably spend Rosh Hashana as the guest of Rabbi Hager in Sosnowiec.
—o—
A Silesian wanted to have a merry moment in Sosnowiec and paid dearly.
A certain Wieczorek from Siemianowice came to Sosnowiec carrying several thousand zł. which he had saved up.
On Warszawska Street Wieczorek made the acquaintance of a „merry lady“, who invited him to a restaurant. There the „company“ grew larger and the Silesian was „taken for a ride“ (literally: put on the „cymbal“). Drunk, he fell asleep; when he woke from his „sweet“ sleep he saw that together with the „ladies“ his wallet with the money had vanished.
The epilogue took place these days before the district court in Sosnowiec, which sentenced each of the accused to a year in prison.

Complaint against the kehilla elections in Strzemieszyce.

On Sunday kehilla elections took place in Strzemieszyce. 8 parnassim (board members) were elected. The elections in Strzemieszyce too were played out against the background of a struggle over the rabbinate. The rabbi's side fought it out with the side that supports the heir of the old rabbi of blessed memory.
The result of the elections is a draw (remis), i.e. each side obtained 4 parnassim.
As is reported, an appeal has been lodged against the elections, in which it is shown that 23 more votes were found in the ballot boxes than the number of voters.
The elected parnassim are: Icchak Waliszewicz, Gerszon Horodisz, Bugajski, Szabtaj Erlichman, Lejbl Szmukler, Szmul Szwarcbaum, Motl Majtlis and Zygelbaum.
An important address book.

For many years there has been felt a lack of an accurate information book on the trade and industry of the Upper Silesian, Kraków and Kielce voivodeships.
The initiative to realise this has been taken upon themselves by the owners of the Zagłębie and Upper Silesian printing works, Messrs M. Kazinski[?] and B. Firbnowski[?] in Sosnowiec (Sienkiewicza 5), who have set about publishing an address book which will be a living informant on the branches of trade and industry in the above-mentioned voivodeships.
In the publication there will be, besides a large section of monographs, also all the firms of industry and trade, large craft workshops, enterprises, and a list of all the liberal professions.
The monographic material has been compiled according to official sources, from the voivodeships and state institutions.
It is therefore to be expected that this important address book, which will contain up to 150.000 addresses and comprise 800 printed pages, will arouse due interest in the circles concerned.
The price of the address book is only 8 zł.
A letter to the editors.

Esteemed Mr Editor!
I ask you very much to publish the following lines in your esteemed newspaper, for which I thank you in advance.
Some time ago Messrs L. Goldsztajn and Sz. Pelc came to me and proposed that I sign a document addressed to the starosta. I was very busy and could not allow myself to read it through. Having the fullest trust in both gentlemen, I asked them to tell me the content of the document. Messrs Goldsztajn and Pelc explained to me that since the president, Mr Rubinlicht, absolutely wants to push Mr Landner out of the kehilla, they are turning to the starosta with a request to protect Mr Landner.
I signed the document without reading it. Unfortunately I was misled. Both gentlemen exploited my trust and informed me falsely about the content of the document. Now I have learned that its content is a denunciation (mesirah) against the president of the Będzin kehilla — Mr Rubinlicht.
I therefore declare publicly that I dissociate myself from the above-mentioned document and withdraw my signature.
Respectfully, M. Kajzer.
Obituary.

A huge crowd gathered last Friday in front of the Sosnowiec railway station to take part in the funeral and to express sympathy to the director of the „Piast“ company, town councillor Mr Sz. Lejwrowicz, and family, on the untimely death of their only daughter Natalia, wife of Mr Kandelis, who died in Vienna.
Behind the wreath-covered coffin, which was brought from the Mysłowice kehilla, followed hundreds of mourners from all strata of the Jewish population. At the cemetery Rabbi Hager delivered a short eulogy, in which he described the heavy misfortune that had befallen the Lejwrowicz family, in which so young, modest[?] and blossoming[?] a branch had been cut down. Then the cantor with the choir sang the appropriate chapters of Psalms and recited El Male Rachamim.
May her soul be bound up in the bond of life.
What's new in Upper Silesia? / Secrets of foreign-currency smugglers before the court.

In the Chorzów district court a whole series of trials for foreign-currency smuggling took place. One trial took place against the merchant Szymon Lauer[?] of Mysłowice. The border guard had detained him while he was trying to cross the border near Beuthen (Bytom); three bills of exchange and a cheque were found on him.
The court sentenced Lauer to a year and a half of imprisonment and also to pay a fine of 5000 zł.
A second trial took place against the maidservant Emma Zweig of Katowice. She too was detained while crossing the border into Germany; she had on her a savings book for 2150 zł.
The defendant defended herself by saying that a day before her departure she had deposited a certain sum of money in the P.K.O. in Katowice and, travelling the next day to Germany, she had, through carelessness, not taken the savings book out of her handbag.
The court believed the defendant's explanations and sentenced her merely to pay a fine of one hundred zł.
Besides this, further trials of this kind took place: against the medical student Włodzimierz (Waldemar) R., who had tried to take a cheque for 3 thousand zł. out to Germany. He too defended himself by saying that before leaving he had forgotten to put the cheque away. The court sentenced him to 22 days' arrest and suspended the execution of the sentence; in addition he must pay a fine of three thousand zł.
A certain Weronika Kędziel[?] of Świętochłowice was sentenced, for trying to smuggle 50 zł. into Germany, to a year's imprisonment, which was suspended for 5 years. She will, however, have to pay a fine in the amount of 150 zł.

The election result compared with the result of the kehilla elections in 1931.
When we compare the outcome of the kehilla elections just held with the result of 1931, it turns out that only thanks to the splintering in the national camp did it come out this time "with tooth and eye" (i.e. damaged), for the number of votes for the national camp is this time much greater than in the above-mentioned year: for example, then all national organizations went [?] on one list (number 6), which received 949 votes, and today — 1044. Not even counting that among the votes for the list of the Small Traders' Association there is a considerable number of votes that would certainly have gone to the national lists.
Compared with 1931 one sees a decline among the other groupings, for example: the Koziegłowy faction then received 448 votes, and now, in union with other Hasidim — only 362.
The "Agudah" then received 344, today 316 ["ar"g" as printed]; on the other hand one sees a great "upswing" among the followers of Rabbi Englard, who received in the elections about 40 per cent more votes than in 1931 (then 590 — today 924); possibly this was caused by the "cultural" ghetto [?], which has grown in the course of time...
The League "lost" 8 votes in the elections, because at that time the porters, who went "with a list of their own", had 177 and the League 61; today both together received 230 votes.

Back to School — The Popular Masses of Sosnowiec and the Role of the Jewish Gymnasium

[Sosnowiec — education.] And now it is over, the dear and pleasant summer with its refreshing rays of sunshine, which turned the little children, the school youth, into delightful summer-birds.
Until last week they were freed from the school walls, within which they are shut up the whole year. Now they are back in the [?] of the lessons and are beginning again to bear[?] the yoke on their shoulders.
With fresh courage, well rested, they step up to the new lessons. The teaching staff, too, their professors, have come back to their laborious and responsible work with fresh strength, which they devote the whole year to their pupils.
So it is inside the school. But it is not easy to get into this temple of education, and once one is already there, one already belongs among the fortunate. Getting in there, both on the part of the pupils and of the teaching staff, involves no small self-sacrifice, protection (pull), intrigues, and quite often one goes through the seven chambers of hell before one can finally be counted among the fortunate.
Not to mention that keeping one's children in our gymnasiums involves the greatest efforts, above all for the middle class of the population, which has to pay for the free and half-free children whom the school admits.
Thus a father of a child complains to the writer of these lines that he has had to take his child out of the school only because I — he says — am not in a position to pay the required tuition fee that is demanded of me, as they explain to me, only because the school has many half-paying and entirely non-paying pupils. To go on looking for protection, with which one achieves everything nowadays, I am not able, for two reasons: first, I do not know whether I am able to obtain it, and second, no offence meant, I hate it with utter hatred; and therefore I have to sacrifice the child, so long as I need not turn to people and „bow“ and stoop before them.
As we are informed, the Sosnowiec Jewish Gymnasium has lowered the tuition fee, which is a great plus in today's bitter times, so that the deed must be warmly welcomed. The only question is: have the prices been reduced in all classes, or only in the preparatory classes? If the reduction is indeed to apply only to the latter, it is of course to be appreciated, but it ought to be applied to all classes.
We know that those interested in the gymnasium may come and tell us that it is a fine gesture[?] on our part when we demand[?] that prices be reduced at a time when the medal also has another side, and one must take a look whether it is sustainable, whether a gymnasium can be maintained on minimal payments, when under today's conditions it involves colossal expenses. Yes. We know that perfectly well. We take account of the state of affairs, and precisely because we must look at the other side of the medal, therefore a general reduction must come. It must come once and for all. Let popular prices be introduced, for we have no rich people in our gymnasiums; they will surely not „lower“ themselves and send their children to us Jews; and if there is a rare bird[?] who has understanding and love for a Jewish education and entrusts his child to us, such a one will[?] also understand that he is obliged to pay, let us say, for a poor child; on the other hand one cannot demand of the average public inflated prices, with which one only pushes the pupils out. One must not forget that the pupils' parents belong to the middle strata of the population, who in Poland today are not at all to be envied; for this reason exclusively popular prices must be applied to their children.
True, under these conditions existence is harder; we will not deny it. So one must look for means and possibilities to reduce the internal expenses.
Earlier, when the school had few pupils, a price reduction could not come into consideration, because the expenses were colossal at that time, while the income was minimal, so that there was nothing to deduct from. Now, however, the situation looks quite different: the income has risen, the number of pupils has grown considerably. So much so that, although the school has a building of its own, another storey must be added, and at the same time people have begun to think seriously about building a building of its own, which should be an ornament for the whole of Sosnowiec Jewry.
Besides, the school is after all a public one, not only in name. You want the public to take an interest both in your joys and, God forbid, in your sorrows — so hold consultation meetings with the public, with the parents, where appropriate resolutions will be adopted, which should make it possible to increase still further the prestige of your and at the same time our educational institution.
We must see to getting more pupils, to educating them properly and thereby raising the condition of the educational institution. We must not forget that there were times for our institution that were truly catastrophic, a matter of to be or not to be — that is how far it went; and since we have overcome all that and are already on the road of upswing and progress, we must reach the proper level at which we have aimed the whole time of our existence.
Dr. Papuri[?].
Town and Village

Because of Ksawera, Będzin too is reminded...
In all towns people keep thinking about how to enlarge the town, how to beautify it, how to find more sources of income for the inhabitants; in short, they look for means by which to rise to a higher level and onto a secure footing.
Yes, so it is in all towns and little towns; everywhere they busy themselves with enlarging and beautifying, so that the eye too should see something and the citizen should benefit from it.
So it is everywhere — except, self-evidently, with us, in the town called Będzin. Out of villages towns are built up, and with us the town is becoming a village.
And it is characteristic: last week the session of the Będzin town administration considered an interpellation from the residents of Ksawera, who demand that the trains should stop at their place too. And then one of our aldermen [ławnicy] remembered: how far have things gone, that Ksawera wants a station of its own, at a time when we have to travel to Sosnowiec to catch an express train? Things have surely reached the point where the village will soon overtake us. And here our representative saw that this was the opportune moment to demand that Będzin, too, should get the express trains back.
We have grown used to village life; we no longer remember that when Będzin was a big town, Sosnowiec was a village. And so we fall asleep and doze peacefully until someone comes along and reminds us that we are asleep precisely when we think we are wide awake...
Such is the sad truth: everywhere progress is being made, everything is being enlarged and improved, while we peacefully fall asleep and keep going along the road backwards.
And more than once the question arises: can one exist under such conditions? Can one find oneself in a "village" and bear the expenses of a town?
Upon my life, it would be only right to put the question on the agenda and consider it with all seriousness, because our town is being turned (and perhaps has already been turned) into a village, at a time when the citizens bear all sorts of municipal obligations.
If the leaders are after the good of the town and its inhabitants, then it is absolutely necessary to take up this very problem, which has an important significance not only for the future but also for the present. One must remember that Będzin has not only not grown, but keeps on shrinking, in such a way that both the town and the inhabitants are at the same time becoming of lesser worth. That is what must be remembered well today, so as not to allow the town to be turned into a real village.
R. Let.

Mazel Tov, I've Already Got a "Shtot"!... — Y. Oberzhabek

(Monologue of a Sosnowiec Jew, an eternal seeker.)
As you look at me, I am an eternal seeker. My whole life I keep on searching: in my mother's womb I searched for the bright light; when I was born, I searched for my mother's breast. When I started going to cheder, I searched for an excuse to play truant; later I searched for a purpose in life, I searched for a way to free myself from Fania's[?] claims[?]; when I grew older I searched for a bride, I searched for a fat [rich] in-law; after the wedding I searched for a livelihood — and so I keep on searching to this very day.
Yes, gentlemen, I keep on searching and finding exactly the opposite: I searched for a purpose and what I found was poverty; I searched for a fat in-law — I found a fat mother-in-law; I searched for a boy, a "Kaddish", for after a hundred and twenty years — I found half a dozen girls; now I am searching, for the six girls — six bridegrooms; every year I get eviction notices and search for flats; every Sabbath I search for an interest-free loan (gemilut chesed) — I am the eternal seeker...
A whole round year I keep on searching: at the end of winter I begin searching the villages for a dacha for my wife. I bring her a dacha with rye fields — she wants a forest; I bring her a forest — she wants water with a beach (plaża); I bring her water with a beach — she wants a "polanka" [a clearing]; and once I have finally found a village, I must start again[?] to search for — a "shtot"!..
— Shaberele (my name is Yeshaya Ber, but out of great love for me my wife has twisted[?] it and pronounces both names in one word: Shaberele). Shaberele, my wife says to me this week:
— What's new?
— What, I say, should be new — it's still a crisis!
— Crisis-shmisis — my wife answered — have you got something "na widoku" yet?
— What does that mean, "na widoku"? — I didn't understand my wife's foreign words.
— I mean — she said — have you already got something in your eye [in view]?
— In my eye? In my eye I have nothing for the time being; for the time being I have it on my shoulders — here, I carry a hump. But tell me, what am I supposed to have in my eye?
— Well, a "shtot" — have you already got in view a decent "shtot" for me for the "Yogiruoim"[?] (read: Yamim Noraim, the High Holidays)?
Hardly had I finished searching a village for my wife when I set about searching a "shtot" for her.
— Shaberele — she said — you know my "taste" (gust) by now; I hate any-old-thing; I must have an "intelligent shtot" — "tsush"[?]!...
So I went off again to search for an "intelligent shtot", a "tsush", for my wife, and the same troubles I had in searching for a village, the same troubles I have with the "shtot". Whatever "shtot" I bring, it is not "da gusto" [to her taste]. I bring her a seat in the "German shul" — she twitches her nose: the "German shul" is not for her. Why? Because Yentl the Half-Taxes prays in the "German shul" — she, together with Yentl the Half-Taxes — feh!...
I bring her the "Sala Angielska" ["English Hall"] — no good again: how will she get along with the women of the "Sala Angielska"!...
I bring her the town shul — again she is not satisfied: there is no suitable "towarzystwo" [society] there for her; what has she to do with that "halaste"[?] [rabble]!
I bring her the Mizrachi shul — she is no Zionist. I bring her the "Vayoushorn"[?] — she says the "Vayoushorn"[?] are good for playing bridge, not for praying the "Yogiruoim"[?].
— Whatever I bring her is no good. Here it is not "vygorne"[?] [comfortable?], there the "towarzystwo" does not suit her; here the cantor is not "sympathetic"[?], there she doesn't like the gabbai — go and find my wife an "intelligent shtot", a "tsush"!...
— Shaberele — she says to me yesterday — wish me mazel tov, I've got one!
— What have you got?
— An "intelligent shtot", the real "tsush"!
— What sort of "tsush" have you found? — I was curious.
— At the minyan on Czysta[?] Street — now that is a "tsush", that is an "intelligent shtot"; together with the whole Sosnowiec "śmietanka" [cream of society] — there we shall have the real "towarzystwo"! Am I right, Shaberele?
— Who would have dreamt it this night or that night — how do the likes of us come to "Maccabi"[?]? There, after all, they pray into their sleeves[?] and preach in Polish; instead of tallitot they wear gloves. How do I, Yeshaya Ber, come to such heights[?]?
But it's no use! A wife has said "Maccabi" — nothing will help.
— But at least you know — my wife tells me later — that to pray in the Maccabi hall one needs an "odpowiedni strój" [appropriate attire]!
Now there is searching again: she is searching for the newest Paris fashion journal, she runs around to the biggest dressmakers, she is searching for the latest "krzyk mody" [the last word in fashion], because it is no small thing — she will be praying at "Maccabi".
Well, my wife is my wife; she has already found the latest "krzyk". But what do I do? What way out have I got? At the Maccabists' minyan they wear top hats on the High Holidays. How will I, Yeshaya Ber, look in such a shiny round hat on my head — and where does one get top hats nowadays anyway? A top hat is worn by the President when he takes a parade (defilada), by Foreign Minister Beck in Geneva — but an ordinary flesh-and-blood mortal in a top hat?
My whole life I keep on searching, and now too I am searching for... a top hat.
Perhaps you know, gentlemen, where one could get somewhere "na prokat" [on hire] a used[?] round hat — after all, I'll be praying among the "intelligent towarzystwo" at "Maccabi".
Hear, O World!

“And cursed be he who says: Revenge! / Such vengeance — vengeance for the blood of a little child — / Satan has not yet created”! / “And if there is justice — let it appear at once! / But if after I am destroyed beneath the sky / justice appears — / may its throne be overturned forever”! (“On the Slaughter”, H. N. Bialik).
Yes, an “Thou hast chosen us” people — not for nothing were we crowned with that name. A chosen people — chosen to be a scapegoat, a lightning rod that must[?] suffer for millions; whatever evil may happen in the world, we are to blame for it all — Reb Yankev pays [i.e. the Jew always pays]...
In Tsarist Russia the Jews were to blame for all the defeats at the fronts; in Hitler’s Germany the Jews are the spectre, the embodiment of all evil; is there unemployment somewhere — the Jew; hunger — the Jew; a civil war in Spain — the Jew.
Actually it is a continuation of the dark Middle Ages — Jews poison the wells, because of the Jews an epidemic strikes little children, the Jew is a demon, an evil spirit — and which people can boast that it is clean of our blood?
And it seemed that all was not lost after all, that a divine spark still smoulders in the human heart, that into the pitch-black sea of hatred one clear drop had been poured, that “one little flame had been saved from the destruction of the Temple” — so it seemed to us then, when Great Britain, and with her all the nations of the world, set out to right a thousand-year-old wrong — to return the Land of Israel to the people of Israel.
For a moment a light shone in our dark homes, and the millions of hearts of a whole people gave a tremble; tried[?] in suffering and in pain, hunted and tormented, we ran with a thirst for redemption and a sweet faith from the ruins and conflagrations of the world, from the gallows to “my refuge”[?] — to our last fortress.
Millions of the despairing and hungry once again found content in life, a desire to work and create.
And the work of building began. In every field it seethed and flared. Those who had been used to twirling a little stick [i.e. idlers] mastered[?] the hammer, the plough and the tractor, and the building rose in town and village, matter and spirit — everything grew feverishly.
Faster, hastier, tempo! — for who knows what tomorrow will bring, whether it will not betray?
And you, England, stood at a distance, and instead of help you quite often put spokes in our wheels.
So what do you want of us now, England, son of Albion? Have we not filled your coffers with millions of pounds, toiled for with our blood and sweat? Have we not passed the examination of industriousness, diligence and readiness to sacrifice for the land? Who else has shown such systematic efforts for this desert, which we have turned into a human settlement?
Do you want to bring back the desert and extinguish the hope of a whole people?
Have we brought too few sacrifices to the thirsty Moloch?
Or perhaps you want, England, to force us to become such bloodthirsty wolves as our wild, blinded neighbours, so that we too, as they shoot innocent women, children and scholars, should burn and uproot whole forests like vandals?
Do you want to rob us of our Jewish mentality, our inborn hatred of cruelty and brutality, of murder?
And you, world, world of radio and telephony, why are you silent when you know that a whole people is struggling for its existence and is perishing[?] in blood? When you know that its best children are shot in broad daylight — why is your mighty protest not heard, your “J’accuse”?
Why are you silent when you know that this [people], which also helped a little to pull the wagon of culture in the world, which did not let one weighty verse be cast[?] out of itself: “Thou shalt not kill”! — that this people is not allowed to build its home, its little corner?
But you, world, are busy with more important matters; you must produce poison gases, tanks, bombs, fratricide and hypocritical Moscow trials.
You, world, are busy creating race theories, Nuremberg laws.
You, world, have been turned into a Sodom and Gomorrah — is it not yet time that an overthrow like that of Sodom and Gomorrah should come upon you?!...
Yankev Goritski.
A Strange (Jewish?) Tribe

[Feuilleton — travel; an African tribe with "Jewish" customs.] By Z. Haber, Vienna.
I met him many years ago at the Leipzig fair. Black like all Negroes, dressed in fine European clothes, he made no particular impression and nobody gave him a second look. Were it not for the long black beard that reached almost to his knees.
I went around with him to several fair halls, where he bought various goods, and everywhere people looked at him as at a [?] wonder.
— A Negro with a beard?...
When we had grown tired and went into a restaurant for a bite, he himself began to tell his story.
He lives on Barana, an island situated between Italian Somaliland and English "Senia" [= Kenya]. At that time they belonged to the kingdom of Abyssinia.
On the island of Barana live several hundred Negroes, who differ from all other Negroes in that their skin is not as dark as the skin of other Negroes. They have various customs and ceremonies of which the other Negroes know nothing; besides that[?] they are indeed more intelligent. They all speak English and some of them Italian too. Most of them carry on various trades and travel around all of Abyssinia and also in all the colonies. A large part of them are rich.
Where they come from he could not say, although he is the chief and foremost on the island and is indeed — as he says — the most intelligent of all.
He thinks that they once came there from Persia; beyond that he did not know.
What he did know is that they are direct descendants of Adam and Eve, who are called among them "Adem" and "Ivan"[?]. When Cain killed Abel, Abel was left with a son, from whom they descend... All other people descend only from them...
They believe in one single God, whom they call "Ulgapi"[?]. Their God cannot be seen, but He rules the whole world... He is a terrible, fearsome God, who punishes evil deeds and does good for good deeds... There is no begging Him for mercy, because He is just and pays honestly according to desert; therefore they never pray to Him and also have no houses of prayer.. Only once a year do they have a holy day... Then they adorn the apple trees most festively, because apple trees are very holy to them. Calves too are holy to them..
They may never let the hair of their beard be cut; only the hair of the head do they cut. The eldest of each family lets locks (peyes?) grow; this is a sign that everyone in the family must pay him great honour. When he feels he is dying, he cuts off the locks and hands them to one of the family who — in his opinion — is worthy to be the head of the family...
They marry only among themselves. With them the woman chooses the man and not the man the woman. She may pick as many husbands as she wants, and the man too may have as many wives as he wants.
More than this about this strange tribe, which has many Jewish customs, I could not find out.
After the Elections

[Kehilla elections — commentary.] As we write these lines, the result of the elections is already known — who is "in" and who is "out"; the election fever has already dropped to zero, the walls with their election posters are like Purim players after Purim, and not just one dozen candidates are resting after the sleepless night. Embittered and disappointed, they think philosophically that life as a whole has never had any sense, that man is a nothing with nothing, that it is a sin to want to do something for humanity, that one knows nothing of anything good and[?] — there is no lack of things to philosophize about when the heart is grieved.
And of "grieved" ones there are not a few. Poor victims of a kehilla epidemic that raged[?] for several weeks.
And all the same, to the "numbers" [the numbered lists] that appeared in the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" and to the numbers that merely crawled over the smooth walls, we hereby send our condolences.
Be consoled and do no more foolishness; tell your children and children's children that no desire should seize them[?] to become [?] among Jews.
The troubles of the defeated candidates are a matter for their relatives — let them apply cold compresses; what interests the Jewish public is that organism on which people allowed themselves to experiment so much.
The election campaign supplied a great deal of characteristic material for getting to know various groups, parties and individuals, organizations and cliques. But there remained one sphinx — the object[?] that was fought over. This sphinx spoke up only on Sunday after 12 at night, when the speech-hearing and proclamation-reading Jewish population was thinking about the 24 lists that had paraded before it so long, so artfully[?], effectively and noisily.
And therefore it is high time and necessary to go into an analysis and to draw up a balance of the kehilla election campaign. We do so in another place.
A Shvartser [i.e. "A Black One"].

By the Ineffable Name..

Ben Zoma says..
Dąbrowa did not withstand the "test" and overstepped the "measure". The whole election period Dąbrowa also "said" with pride: "We'll behave decently, no worse than the Sosnowiec folk." The defenders, who try to smooth over the events, explain that "the Pirkei Avot chapter is to blame": since Jews — so they say — use Sabbath afternoon in the [?] ("redner") beit midrash to study the chapter, the candidate for the rabbinical seat of Dąbrowa should not have come there wanting to deliver election sermons..

(authentic).
As it is written in the chapter:

The "child" has been seized..
Because of the heavy rain the streets were "cleaned" of the election papers; but people gathered in the apartments of the interested parties, where the telegraphic reports of the chief election commission, which was counting the votes, were received with great curiosity.
Tired, worn out, half dozing, the agitators sit on the soft armchairs; it is already past midnight, eyes are closing. But hardly does the telephone ring when everyone jumps up from their places, runs to the telephone and "swallows" the news about the "temperature" of the lists and about "gabbai posts" — which list will "pull" more...
On the western horizon the glow of the coming day can already be seen. There, at Magdushever [?] 18, they have reached Ne'ila, the closing of the gate. Soon the result must be announced — who is on top and who is below. The tension is great, and suddenly — news, but not a happy one: the "Blacks" want to snatch by force one "child" from the counted bloc.
"A doctor! Run for a doctor!" storms the Democrat. "Get the combatants back on their feet!" shouts one of the young men. "Our 'child', which we raised with sweat and blood, they want to take away from us! Help, a doctor!"
The doctor hurried to help, gave an "injection" ("zastrzyk") against "poisoning" [?], but for the time being he did not manage to stop the [?] ("trashten") of the "enemies", and
the "child" has been seized...
How Much Longer?...

[Palestine — the disturbances; correspondence from the Land of Israel.] By Motes Hampel. (A correspondence from Eretz Israel.)
The situation in the country has still not changed for the better; on the contrary, it has become much, much sharper and appears [?] even to be a bad one. I am far, very far from spreading, God forbid, fear and panic among the readers, but neither do I want to deny and hide the bitter truth, the sad reality and the true situation in which we have found ourselves for months, and especially in the last few weeks. The murders in Safed and in Haifa, the horrifying death of the two Jewish nurses in the city of killing [?], Jaffa, the murder of the professor of the Hebrew University in the midst of his scholarly research, the bomb on the train in the heart of Tel Aviv, the frequent attacks on travellers on the dangerous roads — all this shows that the situation is very tense and menacing; more than once it seems to us here that we stand on the eve of new mass attacks on Jewish settlements in the country, attacks that remind us of the sad year 1929. True, in that bloody year we were weak, we formed a small number of Jews, we were not prepared for the attacks; but since then, over the 7 years, we have grown much stronger, so that today we can withstand the war forced upon us...
All the wild spirits of the desert, the evil urge of destruction, the basest bestial feelings in man have risen to life and [—] [?] against us. These human beasts are far from the image of God, far from feelings of pity for children sleeping in their mother's lap, for a nurse who eases the pains of suffering patients, and for a mother in whose arms the souls of her three little children are smothered. The beast has broken loose from its chain, hurling itself on innocent victims, drinking the blood and not wanting to know what blood it is — whether of a child or an old man, of a woman or a man. In the hearts of the Arab leaders and men of religion every spark of human feeling has been extinguished, and they encourage further disciples to further murder and robbery. Can we turn to these leaders and clerics in the language of a human being: "Enough shedding of human blood!" — when they themselves, these leaders and teachers, have robbed themselves of the spirit and with their own hands destroyed within themselves the faith in God?
Nothing remains for us but to turn to our government, before whose eyes dozens of Jews are killed, before whose eyes Jewish property and goods are destroyed. It is a disgrace for the English state, for a cultured nation, for the world's emissaries who took upon themselves the obligation to help us build our land — that until now they have still not put the frenzied beast back in its chains and punished it for the blood of the nearly 80 victims. The English lion, at whose disposal in Palestine stand 15 battalions of troops, 20 thousand soldiers, warships, aeroplanes, tanks, gas and artillery — is as powerless as a feeble weakling ["lemeshke" ?] and calmly looks on at this tragedy. This lion, which rules over seas and continents and which within a quite short time liquidated an uprising in India — cannot cope with the Arab "uprising", with a few gangs, with a few thousand murderers. Is that understandable?
We are disappointed in the government, which cannot establish order in the country; we are full of despair over the government, which cannot break the terror and suppress the criminals, who go about openly and freely, continuing their further "fine" deeds. We are disappointed in our guardian, who has neither the power nor the strength to [subdue ?] the evil and to bring [—] and calm to the country. The government, thanks to its false policy, thanks to its hesitation, thanks to its long deliberation — has with its own hands brought the country to demoralisation, to confusion, to chaos, to a great tohu-va-vohu. Instead of extinguishing the fire before its flames engulfed the country, which has now become "a land that devours its inhabitants"; instead of disarming the murderers and destroying their nests, which over these months have grown even stronger and better armed; instead of punishing the leaders for their incitement; instead of breaking up the strike that provoked terror in the country — instead of all this the government has treated the bloodbath with Olympian calm, conferring again and again with the emissaries of the murderers, wishing to give them a reward for further deeds...
A true picture of the situation in the country and a genuine expression of the bitterness against the government is painted for us in an open letter to the High Commissioner by the president [i.e. mayor] of Tel Aviv, Mr. Dizengoff. Mr. D., who has worked together with the government for over 20 years, who has never been one of "those who rebel against the rulers", who is one of the most moderate public figures in Palestine — has expressed in his letter the cry of woe, the great protest and the unbearable pain of the suffering Yishuv. He writes: ... The government, by its attitude to the events, has brought lawlessness and anarchy into the country, and it itself has undermined the authority of the law and of civic discipline. The country is governed not by the High Commissioner but by the Arab strike committee and by the murderers. A state of "there is neither law nor judge" has arisen. Everything is now permitted in the country. Wherever you turn — you will come upon destruction, murder and annihilation, Sodom and Gomorrah. After every vile deed the High Commissioner "regrets" and the police "investigate", and meanwhile the country has been turned into a hell. How shall we live in such a hell? I turn to the rulers: why are you not ashamed [?]? Break off the immigration! If you cannot protect the lives, property and honour of those who came here at your invitation, relying on your promises — then have the courage to declare openly that your obligation is no obligation...
You proclaim loyalty to the Mandate, and you hand its implementation over to colonial antisemitic officials who are against our idea, stop the immigration and write upon the gates of the country: "The Jew is hopeless, do not enter the country, for evil awaits you here"!... The Royal Commission of Inquiry, too, has probably come to the conclusion: the Mandate remains in force, we may not touch it, but since the Arabs fear "lest the Jews multiply", it is desirable to restrict immigration and the possibilities of colonisation, creating in Palestine a National Home that will be a hell for the Jewish citizens, and you will be the righteous ones, saying: "Our hands have not shed this blood"... In spite of everything the National Home will be built after all, but only by those who are worthy of it...
This cry of woe is without any doubt the cry of the whole of world Jewry, and if the letter quoted reaches its addressee, it must make the hearts of our rulers tremble — if only they have a heart.
For more than 4 months our institutions called on us to be patient, to exercise havlagah (restraint). With the full force of their influence they educated the Yishuv and called on it to refrain from acts of revenge, from "blood vengeance", not wishing to deepen the abyss between us and the Arabs and not wishing to turn the country into a tohu-va-vohu. For months we waged with ourselves a hard inner struggle — not to go in the ways of the beasts and not to imitate their bloody deeds. We said that we would not hinder the government in restoring order in the country, we would not pour oil on the fire, we would not cause the country any misfortune, and in spite of the bloody terror and the many victims we would restrain ourselves and go on along our trodden path of work and creation. Let the farmer go on ploughing — we said — let the mason go on building, let the merchant go on trading, each to his work, to his daily routine. Even when death stands face to face. With the sword in one hand and the hammer in the other, by day and by night, we did indeed continue our work: planted and sowed, ploughed and harvested, showing that we are the pioneers, the emissaries of the people of Israel, which wants a new life in its land, on its soil. But what does time show? Even with our "havlagah" a misfortune has come upon the country — anarchy, disorder — and the explosive bomb rules instead of the law. Patience — patience too has a certain limit — is bursting. One can no longer bite one's lips, one can no longer keep silent, for "the waters [?] have come in even unto the soul". The Yishuv asks: how much longer will Jewish blood be shed? How much longer will the government be helpless and powerless against the murderers, who have allied themselves with the devil, dancing a demons' dance on the back of the Jewish Yishuv? How much longer can we carry in our hearts the [spear ?] of anger? We came to our land to live and to work, but we are also ready to bring sacrifices — sacrifices in the struggle with nature, in the struggle with the swamps, for the "conquest of labour", for guarding and defence. But we do not want to be prey for beasts and snakes, and if the government cannot protect us, let it tell us so openly, and we shall know what to do...
Magdiel, 24 August 1936.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Nitzavim-Vayelech)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Nitzavim-Vayelech
—o—
a) "You are standing this day, all of you, before the Lord" (Deut. 29:9)
"On the day they seated Rabbi Eliezer at the head, he opened and said: You are standing this day... your little ones, your wives..." Tractate Soferim, ch. 19 [?].
Why should a rabbi who has only just taken up his office choose to expound the verse "You are standing this day"? What does this verse say?
But in the Tanhuma (on this portion) the verse "You are standing this day, all of you, before the Lord your God, your heads, your tribes" is expounded: "Although I have appointed heads, elders and officers over you, you are all equal before Me, as it is said: every man of Israel." The verse thus teaches that after you have been elected, whether as rabbis or as leaders, you are equal with the multitude before God.
And every newly elected rabbi and leader ought indeed to learn this homily by heart... Olat Hodesh.
—o—
b) "The secret things belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed things belong to us and to our children" (Deut. 29:28)
Before God one can fulfil one's duty with hidden things alone, by being a Jew in secret; but "and to our children" — for our children's sake — "the revealed things": here you must already demonstrate your Jewishness. Before them you must show openly that you are a Jew, so that they will follow your example... Devash ve-Halav.
—o—
c) "Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your seed" (Deut. 30:19)
The Gemara in Berakhot says: "A righteous man who suffers — is a righteous man, son of a wicked man"; that is, even if your son is righteous, he suffers for your sins when you are wicked. So the Torah says: "Choose life, that you may live, you and your seed", i.e. so that your child should not suffer for your sins... Kol Yevaser.
—o—
d) "Gather the people, the men, the women and the little ones" (Deut. 31:12)
"Why do the little ones come? — To give reward to those who bring them." Hagigah 3.
The children are brought to be shown before God, for on their account, on account of the growing generations, the elders receive reward, and the elders become complete tzaddikim... R. Shimon Sofer.
• • •
The famous Berezhany Gaon, R. Shmuel [?] Mordechai ha-Kohen, once travelled to Karlsbad for a cure. A Maskil Jew asked him, to provoke him:
"You, the Berezhany Rabbi, also believe in the Karlsbad remedies?"
The rabbi answered him:
"Rabbi Hershele of Zhidachov once fell ill and had the well-known Lemberg doctor Rapaport brought to him, who was reputed to be a great heretic and a sinner-out-of-spite. When the doctor came, R. Hershele said to him: Don't think, Dr. Rapaport, that I believe in you more than in my house doctor. I sent for you precisely because my house doctor is still a little pious, so I preferred to invite you — for beside you I am surely already a great tzaddik, and when you sit at my bedside, the Blessed Name will surely have mercy on me...
"So too," the Berezhany Rabbi concluded, "that is why I come to Karlsbad, which is full of sinners and lustful people, and beside such a generation of the wicked I am surely already a tzaddik; you understand, then, that the Blessed Name will have mercy on me."
—o—
e) "Put it in their mouths" (Deut. 31:19)
The whole Torah depends on a person's mouth; the whole Torah is found in a person's mouth... With a clean, guarded mouth one fulfils the whole Torah. Arono shel Yosef.
—o—
f) "And it shall come to pass, when many evils and troubles befall them, that this song shall testify before them as a witness" (Deut. 31:21)
Does one really need a witness, a proof, of troubles?
But sometimes the troubles are so disguised that one does not feel them if one does not delve into them, if one does not study our history... Ohel Yaakov.
• • •
Formerly Jews blamed their wickedness on the fact that they were in exile: "Because my God is not among me" ("Whoever lives outside the Land is as one who has no God") "these evils have befallen me." To this God says: "For I will bring them into the land" — I will bring you into the Land, and there we shall see whether you become more pious and better; and if there too you sin — "this song shall testify as a witness": the Torah will be a testimony that in exile, too, you were not bad merely because of the exile... Imrei Avraham.
—o—
g) "For I know your rebellion" (Deut. 31:27)
"Your rebellion" (et meryekha) means your bitterness. I know how embittered you have remained, and that this bitterness causes "your stiff neck", your stubbornness... Kelilat Yofi.
• • •
R. Itzele of Volozhin once came into a company of Maskilim and told them he was ready to answer their questions on matters of faith.
One of them began to pour out question after question, and R. Itzele did not answer him at all. The man asked him:
"Where is your promise, Rabbi?"
R. Itzele answered:
"When a person believes, but certain doubts torment him, it makes sense that questions are hard for him and he needs answers. You, however, have cast off the yoke, and no questions on matters of faith are hard for you; what you ask are merely excuses for your uneasy conscience."
Netzhiyut ve-hagash [?].

[Der Kokh-Lefl — humour and satire; a poem for the Days of Awe.]
Here they come already,
the fearful days,
the moments of dread
and of terror;
the trees in the forest
stand frightened.
In the field
the cattle tremble.

The fish in the rivers
swim [—?]
and want
to escape the whip
and seek in the abyss
a deeper place
and seek there
to find shelter.

And wherever there is just a little group,
and wherever a garage
is now turned
into a little shul,
and worried[?] Jews
run about
sweaty, in a stew,
and [—].

The alarm is already sounding,
the Jew is already being roused,
the market is
flooded with tickets [for High Holiday seats],
for one cannot come
with empty hands
to the Father in Heaven
and plead...

The barbers — they are
the first at stake;
they are
the first victims:
Jews let themselves
grow little beards anew,
and start
practising cantorial singing.

I seek no faults
in the cantor system
and I don't wave it
off-hand[?] away;
I hold that cantorial singing
and writing a poem
are one and the same
"trade".

There are cantors

who wail, sob
and lament

understands a hint,
He does not need
