A "Living" Letter from a Group of the Dead

[Der Kokh-Lefl — satire; Sosnowiec — kehilla elections.]
To the newly elected Agudah "dozory" [kehilla board members]
(Especially for the "Kokh-Lefl").

Dear comrade editor of the "Kokh-Lefl" (we call you "comrade" because a writer is likened to a dead man...): we, a group of the dead, ask you to convey to the new Agudah dozory the following request;
Since in the kehilla elections we gave our votes to the "Agudah", and thanks to our votes they were "victorious", we deserve as compensation the following:
1) To provide for our widows and orphans with the help of the social relief committee.
2) Not to admit our wives to our graves, since we had enough of them in life.
3) Not to bury the dead so deep in the earth, for in life too we were nine ells deep in poverty.
4) To bury every party man next to his party comrades — let them at least have rest after death.
5) Not to bury the "bearded notables" at the top.
6) To forbid entry to "couples"; we really cannot bear to watch living people go and bury themselves alive.
We hope that the Agudah dozory will take our request into consideration and thereby give compensation for our "lively participation" in the kehilla elections.
With greetings,
A group of the dead from the Sosnowiec cemetery [lit. "house of life"].
Sleep Well, Then!..

[Der Kokh-Lefl — humour; train stories; followed by two short jokes.]
From the railway tales.

On the train that runs at night from Sosnowiec to Warsaw, a Jew with bundles gets on at Zawiercie. Several other Jews were sitting in the carriage, and the Jew asks:
— Gentlemen, are you going to Warsaw?
— Yes. All of us, — the Jews answered.
— If so, I have a proposal; since lately one hears about thefts on the trains, I propose the following:
— I'll sleep until Radomsko, and from Radomsko you will sleep.
— Good, agreed, — the Jews answered.
The Jew stretched out on the bench and fell sweetly asleep. He was sure that his bit of merchandise was being watched[?]. Arriving at Radomsko, the Jews wake him:
Reb Jew, Radomsko!
— Radomsko? Very good, — he picked up his bundles and said to the Jews:
— Have a safe journey, to life and peace — and headed for the door.
— Reb Jew, where are you going?! — they asked him. Why didn't you say at once that you were going to Radomsko?
— Because nobody asked me. I did say that from Radomsko you would sleep, so sleep well, then!..

—o—

At the Graves of the Ancestors.

In a corner, by a fresh mound, sits a young woman pouring out her heart: Where have you left me? You cut short my young years; neither do I eat, nor do I sleep. Like a shadow I wander about and can find no place for myself. Without you my life isn't worth a pinch of snuff.
— What[?], you're crying here? — an acquaintance passing by interrupts her
— When did he die?
— Three years ago already.
— Three years already? How is that possible? — the acquaintance wonders — why, only a few weeks ago I saw your husband in the street?
— My husband, thank God, is alive — the young woman answers — it's my bookkeeper lying here!..

In the Tangle of Life (10)

[Serialized novel — Kraków, Zawiercie and New York; installment 10.]
(A novel with dramatic events in Kraków, Zawiercie and New York)

When the ship arrived in New York, Michael was in seventh heaven with happiness. He hugged his mother and stepfather, kissed them and embraced them. Emma was not at the ship, because she could not get away.

The newly arrived immigrants settled in for the time being. That very same day Michael told his mother about Masha, and above all about Emma, and that he intended to marry her soon.

When Emma was free, she quickly went off to meet Michael's mother, Selma.

Selma greeted her warmly, began talking with her about various things, and then asked her whether it would not be hard for her to answer a few personal questions, because she wanted to know whom her son was going to marry.

"Certainly, I'll answer you everything — just ask whatever you like," said Emma.

She asked her who her parents had been.

"They are already dead; my father's name was David and my mother's Nechama."

Selma turned pale.

"What did you say your father's name was — David?"

"Yes."

"And his family name? What is your name?"

"Teitelbaum."

"David Teitelbaum? Was he from Kraków?"

"Yes."

"Your mother was from Zawiercie?"

"Yes. Strange how you guess everything — could it be that you knew them?" Emma asked.

"It may well be, my child. Do you have his picture?"

"Yes, I always carry it with me."

Emma showed her his picture, and everything went dark before Selma's eyes.

"Wait a moment, child," she said, and began searching for something in a drawer.

And soon Selma showed Emma exactly such a picture of her father David.

"How do you come to have it?" Emma asked in astonishment.

"Because he was my beloved — or better said, my first husband, Michael's father."

"Michael's father!" Emma cried out.

"Yes, my child!"

"What did you say, Mother?" Michael stammered in fright. "My father was also Emma's father? We are sister and brother?"

"Yes, so it is, my child!" Selma said, agitated, swallowing her tears. "And it is lucky that I came. I have saved you from a calamity."

Emma and Michael fell on each other's necks and wept bitterly. Selma wept too.

It goes without saying that there could no longer be any talk of a wedding between Emma and Michael.

Bernard was supremely happy when he learned that Michael was Emma's brother and that they could not marry.

Bernard now expected that Emma would come to him. But that did not happen. Bernard therefore decided to keep up the same tactics toward her as before.

After the dramatic conversation with Emma, Selma asked her to come and see her often, and Emma did indeed begin to visit Selma often. She now began to feel quite differently toward Michael — just as toward a brother. Besides, she found it very pleasant to talk with Selma's husband, Artur Sanders, who was a very likeable and highly educated man.

In time Selma began to talk Michael into making up with Masha and marrying her.

Michael telephoned Masha and they met. After long arguments and complaints they renewed their friendship.

But things were still going badly for Michael. He was still earning nothing, and Masha asked her brother Bernard to take Michael into his business.

Bernard gave Michael a small salary and told him that if he proved capable, he would give him a better salary.

Michael was very content; he and Masha began to talk seriously about marrying. But one day Masha said to him:

"I didn't know before that you are half Christian; I took you for a pure Jew. But now I want you to become a complete Jew."

"That's what you mean — a ceremony! Do you really believe in that?" he asked Masha.

"Yes, I believe! I believe that if you do it for me, it is a sign that you love me. If not, it is a sign that you don't. Besides, my brother Bernard will under no circumstances let me marry someone who is not a Jew."

Michael promised her.

"If it matters to you, so be it!" he answered.

And for the time being they decided to postpone the wedding for a year, until he had worked his way up a little.

At the same time Bernard still kept hoping that Emma would change her mind after all and marry him at long last. Michael and Emma too now wanted this.

But suddenly a blow fell on everyone: they discovered that Emma was in love with Selma's husband, with Artur, and that Artur too was in love with Emma.

And this is how it came about:

In the early days Emma used to come often to Selma, and the two of them used to keep each other company. She used to go shopping with her and in general regarded her as family.

Artur earned little and it was not enough to live on, so Selma went out to work.

But soon Selma found out that Emma was meeting Artur often while she was at work; and at the same time Emma stopped coming to their home[?].

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: A Hooligan Attack on Dr. Taraszejski

What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 24 Elul 5696 — piątek 11 września '936 [Friday, 11 September 1936].)
Będzin
A hooligan attack on Dr. Taraszejski.
On Thursday, at around 10 in the evening[?], Dr. Binyamin Taraszejski[?] was in Grodziec[?] on a visit to the district physician, Mr. Rirel[?]. On the way back he stopped at the bus station and waited for a car to Będzin. At that moment he was attacked by several local hooligans ("łobuzy"), who threw him to the ground with the aim of carrying out a robbery.
Fortunately a car with passengers arrived, and the attackers then ran away.
The police have arrested the attackers.
A Meeting in the Kehilla Premises on the Survival of the Talmud Torah

A meeting in the kehilla premises on the survival of the Talmud Torah.
As we have already written, President Mr. S. Fürstenberg has taken upon himself the initiative to create the means that would secure the existence of the local "Talmud Torah".
For this purpose a council and a board were elected at the first meeting, which took place last week.
On Tuesday evening a meeting of the council and board was held under the chairmanship of Mr. Fürstenberg; after a short discussion it resolved to carry out a one-time collection in the town and to recruit new members for monthly pledges.
The one-time contribution began at the meeting itself, where those present pledged[?] larger donations.
A High School for… Merchants

A high school for… merchants.
At the last meeting of the board of the "Merchants' Association" the question was discussed whether, in connection with the new trade laws, the "Merchants' Association" should open a high school (gymnasium) for merchants. (The Polish merchants already have such a gymnasium.)
After the discussion it was resolved to call in experts who will work out the plan of the gymnasium.
At the same meeting the wish was expressed that the association intervene with the appropriate authorities so that the deadline for putting up new signs on the shops be extended.
An Antisemite Who Does Not Like Jews Riding the Tram

An antisemite who does not like Jews riding the tram...
Into a tram in which there were several Jewish passengers there climbed a Christian, who became very angry on seeing the Jewish passengers. At first he made use only of his "tongue", but later he also began to use his hands and feet.
One of the passengers, Mr. Mendel Gruszes[?], intervened about this with the conductor, who, together with the motorman, "sent off" (meshaleakh geven) the troublemaker from the tram.
„Literarishe Bleter“

„Literarishe Bleter“.
Having carried out a successful subscription drive in Silesia and in Sosnowiec on behalf of the only literary weekly, the "Literarishe Bleter" contributor, comrade H. L. Zylberberg, is staying with us in order to carry out the drive in Będzin too.
We hope that the town of Będzin, with its traditions in everything connected with Yiddish and Yiddish literature, will not lag behind other towns and will receive comrade Zylberberg's visits with pleasure and attention.
A „Kofer Nefesh“ Campaign for the Talmud Torah

A "Kofer Nefesh" campaign for the Talmud Torah.
As every year, this year too the traditional "Kofer Nefesh" (ransom of the soul) campaign is being organised for the first Selichot on behalf of the Talmud Torah.
It is to be hoped that the campaign on behalf of this institution will this year too bring the proper result for the Talmud Torah, where up to 400 poor children study.
The Home-Workers' Strike — Settled

The home-workers' strike — settled.
The strike of the home-workers (chałupnicy) in ladies' and men's ready-made clothing, which lasted several weeks, has been settled, thanks to an agreement between both sides.
The Tishrei Campaign for the KKL

The Tishrei campaign for the KKL.
Beginning on Sunday the 13th of this month, the great Tishrei campaign of the KKL (Jewish National Fund) will be carried out in Zagłębie. The calendars for the year 5697 will be distributed by the thousands; they contain rich statistical material on the situation in Eretz Israel. Artistic greeting cards will also be sold, which represent a map of Eretz Israel with the Jewish settlements marked.
The Jewish population is called upon to receive the pairs of collectors with a friendly welcome and to donate significant sums for the redemption of the land through the KKL.
The collectors must without fail hold credentials and receipts bearing the stamp of the local KKL committee.
By the 15th — Second Instalment of the Turnover Tax / Registration of the 1918 Class / Afraid of Competition..

[Będzin — taxes, conscription and education; followed by two short items.]
The "Merchants' Association" ("Sokhrim Fareyn") in Będzin draws attention to the fact that the second instalment of the turnover tax must be paid by the 15th of this month[?].
—o—
Registration of the 1918 class.
We have been asked by the Magistrate [town council] to announce that during the current[?] month the young men born in the year 1918 must register, so that they may be entered in the conscription ("pobór")[?] lists.
—o—
Afraid of competition..
These days a meeting of the Jewish gymnasia [secondary schools] of Będzin and Sosnowiec took place.
At the meeting an agreement was reached that the two schools shall not engage in any competition between themselves..
Sosnowiec — A Ceremonial Welcome in Honour of the Inspector General of the Army, Gen. Rydz-Śmigły

[Sosnowiec — official visit.]
Yesterday at 8.12 in the morning the Inspector General of the Army, General Rydz-Śmigły, arrived by special train at the local station in Sosnowiec, on his way back from his triumphal journey to France.
The welcome at the station had a ceremonial character.
On the very beautifully decorated station platform there were drawn up 4 guard-of-honour companies of the State Police, Strzelcy [Riflemen's Association], school youth and the orchestra of [the] "Hrabia Renard" [mine].
When the train came into the station the orchestra played the national anthem, the detachments presented arms and the garrison commander made a report to the Commander-in-Chief.
All the public organisations, unions, societies and the school youth took up positions on the square in front of the railway station in the following order: on the left stood the school youth, in the middle — the federations of the military organisations, and the right wing was occupied by delegations and the public.
The Supreme Commander was greeted in the name of the whole community by the city president, Deputy Kaczkowski[?], and the orchestra played "The First Brigade".
The guard-of-honour companies presented arms and, to the sounds of the orchestra playing the national anthem, the Commander-in-Chief departed from the local station.
At all the railway stations in Zagłębie, too, ceremonial welcomes were organised in honour of the distinguished guest.
The Course of Sunday's Election Day

[Sosnowiec — kehilla elections.]
On the whole, election day was cooler than the election campaign.
Early in the morning the chairman of the main electoral commission visited the various polling stations and established that the ballot boxes were in order and that the commission members were in their places.
Most of the electoral committees, as is the custom, sent out their canvassers with number slips.
No particular intensity in the canvassing was to be seen at the polling stations.
By midday 30 to 40 per cent of the voters had voted. Only towards evening did masses of voters begin to stream to the ballot boxes.
The leaders of the Orthodox lists stormed about until between Minkhe and Maariv [the afternoon and evening prayers], calling the voters to the ballot boxes.
At 9 in the evening they were already beginning to bring the ballot boxes into the kehilla premises, and there began the hours[?] of tense waiting for the result, which we report on another page.
Today the Electoral Commission for the Kehilla Board Will Be Elected

[Sosnowiec — kehilla.]
In accordance with the regulations, a meeting of the newly elected parnassim [kehilla councillors] will take place today, Friday, at 12 noon.
The purpose of the meeting is to elect the electoral commission which is to organise the elections to the kehilla board.
Zagłębie Marks the Anniversary of "Bloody Wednesday"

[Zagłębie — labour movement.]
On Sunday Zagłębie commemorated the workers who were killed by the Cossacks on "Bloody Wednesday", in the year 1906. In honour of this a huge demonstration took place, in which many thousands of workers from various places took part; they marched to the sounds of several orchestras and shouted various slogans.
The demonstration passed off quietly.
A Greek Citizen in the Local "Chad Gadya"...

[Sosnowiec — crime.]
The Greek citizen Kukiergis[?], who is a local resident, has been put in the local prison.
Kukienus[?] is accused of committing an act of rape on an 18-year-old girl in Zuglecki's[?] restaurant on Warszawska Street.
Together with him the waiter of the restaurant, who took part in the shameful deed, has also been arrested.
The Premises Tax to Be Collected Together with the Rent

[Sosnowiec — taxes and housing.]
As we are informed, a project has arisen in the tenants' associations that the premises tax should be collected together with the rent by the landlord, in monthly instalments.
It is doubtful, however, whether the landlords will agree to this, although paying the premises tax in monthly instalments would be very convenient for the tenants.
From 1 October Fruit and Soda-Water Shops Must Close at 9 in the Evening

[Sosnowiec — trade and regulations.]
On 1 October the ordinance on winter hours in the trade of fruit shops, soda-water shops etc. comes into force.
These trading businesses, which in the summer months were open until 11 in the evening, will from 1 October have to close at 9 in the evening.
The police commissariats have already received the appropriate instructions to see to it that the ordinance is carried out.
3 Endeks Arrested for Planting Petards at Jewish Synagogues.

[Sosnowiec — Antisemitism; Arrests.]
After a lengthy investigation the security authorities have arrested a whole series of persons accused of planting petards at Jewish houses of prayer and of splashing filth on Jewish passers-by.
Three prominent Endeks [National Democrats], members of the Endek party in Sosnowiec, have been put in prison: the chairman Hincinger[?] and the board members Grudgiewicz[?] and Zacharski.
—o—
Donations to Philanthropic and Public Institutions.
Mr. M. Kandelis[?], in memory of his wife Natalia[?] Lejwerowicz[?], who died young, donates 1000 zł. to the following purposes:
For the Jewish hospital 200 zł., the orphans' home 150 zł., the old-age home 150 zł., the Talmud Torah 100 zł., Linat ha-Cholim 75 zł., "Tomchei Yoldot Aniyot" [support for poor women in childbirth] 75 zł., Malbish Arumim [clothing the naked] 50 zł., and for the Peace Fund at the League of Human Rights 200 zł.
Vows (Nedarim) Campaign for the Gemilut Chesed Fund.

[Sosnowiec(?) — Charity; Free-Loan Fund.]
As is known, year in, year out the board of the local interest-free fund proclaims a vows (nedarim) campaign for the month of Tishri.
This year the vows campaign is being organised on a broad scale, since the aim is to obtain such an income as will strengthen the financial position of the institution, which is the finest in our town.

Dąbrowa
A Brawl over the Kehilla Elections.

[Dąbrowa — Kehilla and Elections; Religious Life.]
Last Sabbath afternoon, in the beit midrash in Dąbrowa [Górnicza], it came to a brawl over "speeches" in connection with the kehilla elections that had taken place.
The brawl broke out because the Krymiłów Hasidim were against the rabbinical candidate R' Baruch Epsztajn speaking about the kehilla elections.
The chief victim of this "holy war" is the universally respected R' Szlama Jurkiewicz, who was sitting and studying a chapter [of Pirkei Avot] with the congregation; for this he received such a "reward"...
—o—
Tragic Death of a Five-Year-Old Girl.
On Sunday afternoon in Strzemieszyce the 5-year-old Stopa[?] was run over by a car.
A few hours later the child died.
Donations for the Orphanage (Beit Yetomim) in Będzin.

[Będzin — Charity; Orphanage.]
In lieu of flowers on the grave of the unforgettable Mrs. Gitla Gutman[?], may she rest in Eden — Icchak Szajn and wife 50 zł.
In lieu of flowers on the grave of their sister Regina W[?]szuriskoska[?], Paulina Stencel (Częstochowa) and Grenia[?] Frenkel (Warsaw) give 10 zł. each.
Results of the kehilla elections in Kielce — the merchants, the small traders' association and the Aleksander Hasidim were left without mandates.

[Kielce — kehilla; elections.] The elections to the Kielce kehilla council proceeded calmly and ended with the following unexpected result:
List no. 2 (Chęciny Hasidim): 299 votes — 2 mandates.
List no. 3 ("shul list" together with the Revisionists): 179 votes — 1 mandate.
List no. 4 (Artisans' Association): 293 votes — 2 mandates.
List no. 5 (Poale Zion): 281 votes — 1 mandate.
List no. 6 (Agudah); 361 votes — 2 mandates.
List no. 11 (Chmielnik Hasidim): 65 votes — 4 mandates.
List no. 12 (Zionist Bloc): 337 votes — 2 mandates.
Lists no. 7 (Aleksander Hasidim): 142 votes, no. 10 (Small Traders' Association): 53 votes, no. 13 (Merchants' Association): 33 (thirty-three) votes — were left without mandates.
List no. 14 (Poale Agudat Israel) did not receive a single vote.
There were 4254 eligible voters; 2572 persons voted, i.e. about 67 per cent.
Who are the new parnassim (councillors)?
From list no. 2 — Moshe Sternfeld and Moshe Simcha Frier [?].
From list no. 3 — Yosef Żyączkowski [?].
From list no. 4 — Yidl Gutman and Shmuel Leichter.
From list no. 5 — Noach Laks.
From list no. 6 — Eli' Rotenberg and Meir Isenberg.
From list no. 11 — Avraham Piotrkowski, Simcha Bunem Goleman [?], Avraham Shlomo Fridenzon [?] and Chaim Pasirman [?].
From list no. 12 — Yehoshua Bekerman and Avraham Finkelstein.
Hanged himself with a handkerchief in the municipal lock-up.

[Kielce — crime; suicide.] This Monday, the 31-year-old Julian Jarosz of Kielce committed suicide in the municipal lock-up.
Jarosz had been detained by the police that same day on suspicion of theft. When he was detained Jarosz was very drunk, and he was therefore put in the lock-up to sober up. He was put in at 12 noon, and [at] 8 in the evening the lock-up duty officers noticed that Jarosz had committed suicide, hanging himself with his handkerchief. The doctor who was called established that Jarosz was dead.
Endek boycott appeals against Jews.

[Kielce — antisemitism; boycott and pickets.] This week Endek gangs spread many anti-Jewish leaflets in town, calling on the school youth to boycott the Jewish stationery shops and bookshops. A large part of the Christian school youth also took part in this "holy work".
Endek pickets were posted in front of some Jewish shops, and they did not let any Christian customers in there.
Gravestones desecrated again at the Jewish cemetery.
[Kielce — antisemitism; cemetery.] This week unknown hooligans again desecrated graves at the Kielce cemetery. Several gravestones were broken and some graves were defiled.
Constituent meeting of the new kehilla council.

[Kielce — kehilla.] On the basis of the binding election calendar, the constituent meeting of the newly elected kehilla council will take place on Friday, the 25th of this month. A chairman, a vice-chairman and a secretary will be elected.
Elections of the kehilla board.

[Kielce — kehilla.] Right after the constituent meeting of the kehilla council, 2 days later, i.e. on Sunday the 27th of this month, the elections of the kehilla board will take place. The board is elected by the members of the council.
A pavilion for tuberculosis patients at the municipal hospital.

[Kielce — health; municipality.] As we are informed, a pavilion for tuberculosis patients will be built at the municipal hospital in the coming weeks. The pavilion will cost about 10000 zł.
—o—
About the House-Owners' Bank.
[Kielce — economy; House-Owners' Bank.] Some time ago we already wrote about the special commission that was elected to restructure the House-Owners' Bank. This commission wanted to come up with an appropriate plan concerning the further existence of the bank.
Unfortunately we hear nothing about any real and truly positive steps for the benefit of the bank.
We therefore consider it our public duty to draw the attention of the bank's management once again to the fact that the restructuring work being carried out there should rest on something substantial and not just be done at random. If something can really be achieved there, let it be done, and the Jewish public will help; and if not — let no new, unnecessary expenses be made that will swallow up the remaining few złotys, for the People's Bank affair has already taught us a great deal.
"To hearken unto the song and the prayer"

[Kielce — notice: High Holiday services at the Zionist club.] In the splendid and hygienic halls of the Zionist club (Wesoła 28), first-class cantors will lead the prayers this year on Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur. Provide yourselves in good time with admission tickets, which can be obtained every day from 8 to 11 in the evening at the secretariat of the Zionist club.
On exempting Jewish children from attending the state elementary schools on the Sabbath.

[Kielce — education and Sabbath observance.] Thanks to the intervention of the board of the society "Shomrei Shabbat", the school inspector has promised to exempt Jewish children from attending the elementary schools on the Sabbath, if their parents apply to the school administration with special petitions to that effect.
The board of "Shomrei Shabbat" therefore announces that it has had such special petitions to the school management printed.
The petition forms can be obtained from the Rabbi of Kielce, Rabbi Rapaport, from Rabbi Harenberg[?] and at the premises of "Shomrei Shabbat" (Cicha 8).
The 13th L.O.P.P. Week in Kielce.

[Kielce — air defence.] At the large meeting of representatives of the Christian and Jewish population, held this Wednesday in the hall of S. H.[?], it was resolved to proclaim the 13th L.O.P.P. Week [LOPP — Air and Anti-Gas Defence League] in Kielce and in the Kielce county (powiat).
The L.O.P.P. Week begins on Sunday the 27th of this month [27 September 1936] and will last until 4 October inclusive.
The funeral of Mrs. Dr. Fleszler.

[Kielce — mourning; funeral.] Last Thursday, after a short illness, Ira[?] Fleszler, aged 38, the wife of the well-known local physician Dr. Y. Fleszler, died in Otwock.
Mrs. Fleszler was brought to Kielce on Friday towards evening, where on Sunday at 4 p.m. she was laid to eternal rest.
Several thousand people from all strata of Jewish and non-Jewish society in Kielce took part in the funeral, among them the children of the local orphanage, for whom the young departed Mrs. Fleszler had done a great deal.
The swift and unexpected death of Mrs. Fleszler has caused understandable grief in Jewish circles, where she was much beloved.
Honour to her memory!
The large 5-złoty coins.
[Poland — currency.] On the 30th of this month the deadline for exchanging the large 5 zł coins of 1929 and 1930 expires. After that date the coins will lose their value.
Blessed be He and blessed be His Name — and the way he does it is thus and thus

[Kielce — fraud.] A certain smooth operator ["khevre-man"] by the name of B. E. (25 years old) found himself, in these hard times, an easy livelihood from "bridegrooming": that is, he would get acquainted with girls, go out with them, become their "intended" for a while, and take an advance on account of the future feelings...
Thus he took 500 zł from a Kielce girl, B., and 250 zł each from 2 girls from Łódź.

Terrible Fire in Katowice / Income Tax Must Be Paid Properly

[Katowice — disaster.]
13 people burnt alive.
On the night from Sunday to Monday a fire broke out in a barn („stodoła“) in Bogucice. Thirteen people were sleeping in the barn; despite the swift rescue operation of the Katowice firemen and those of the surroundings, it proved impossible to contain the fire, and all the people were burnt alive.
Among the victims were 4 children.
—o—
[Poland — taxes.]
Income tax must be paid properly.
The Ministry of Finance this week sent out a circular to the tax offices instructing them to carry out strict checks on all commercial premises — whether they pay income tax on the salaries („pensje“) of their employees and workers, and whether this deduction is actually withheld from the salaries and paid in to the tax offices.
In cases where merchants and manufacturers do not pay the income tax on salaries to the tax office, they will be severely punished.

[Sosnowiec — crime.]
The day before yesterday [?] the police in Sosnowiec arrested a certain Michalczyk, who a few weeks ago attacked the 19-year-old Czarnocha and knocked out his eye with a bottle.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — economy.]
On exports to Portugal.
On the 23rd of this month Minister Ramer [?] [probably Antoni Roman, Minister of Industry and Trade] is coming to Sosnowiec in order to acquaint himself with the export possibilities of the Kielce voivodeship to Portugal.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — house-owners.]
Who are the delegates to the house-owners' congress?
At the world congress of house-owners, which takes place in Warsaw from the 19th to the 23rd of this month, the Sosnowiec House-Owners' Association will be represented by: Dir. Lajzerowicz, Z. Koszuch[?] and B. Majerczyk.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — kehilla.]
On Sunday the presidium of the Sosnowiec kehilla council will be elected.
Next Sunday, at 5 in the afternoon, a meeting of the new kehilla council will take place in order to elect a chairman and a vice-chairman of the council.
The meeting is being convened by the hitherto kehilla commissioner.

Jabotinsky's Great 10-Year Plan

[Sosnowiec — Revisionist Zionism.] From his lecture at the "Palace" cinema, Sosnowiec.
As we have already reported briefly, last Thursday evening the Revisionist leader V. Jabotinsky appeared with a lecture at the "Palace" cinema on the subject [?] "To Be or Not to Be".
Despite the fact that a day earlier a bomb had exploded [?] in the very same cinema, the hall was nevertheless filled to overflowing. At the presidium table — delegations of various societies and organisations, headed by Rabbi Hager.
President [?] Bernard Jasny [?] greets the distinguished guest, who is received by the auditorium with long-lasting ovations.
After the lecture Jabotinsky is greeted by 2 young Betarim, who present him with a bouquet of flowers.
In his 2-hour lecture on the grave situation and the darkness in which we find ourselves today, the speaker expresses the view that there is still hope, that bright days will yet come for the Jewish people, that immigration (aliyah) will not be stopped; but — he says — the time has come for us Jews to undertake preparatory steps for the future that may come. First of all we must see to having a majority [?] in Eretz Israel. A Jewish Legion, and seeking new, stronger factors that will help carry out the "leap" to a majority [?] in Eretz Israel.
And this can be achieved — says the speaker — only through unity among Jews, not as the leaders of the Jewish Agency understand it, but through the National Assembly proposed by the N.Z.O. (New Zionist Organisation), with the participation of the entire Jewish people, even the "Agudah" etc. And at the National Assembly it should become clear who must take over the leadership [?] — I or "he" [?].
The huge audience applauds the speaker, and the lecture is closed with "Hatikvah".
Copies of Import Permits for Foreign-Exchange Purposes

[Sosnowiec — trade and economy.] An explanation from the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce.
(Sh) The Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec announces that, in connection with the efforts of firms to obtain, for foreign-exchange ("Devisen") purposes, copies of the permits issued before 27 May of this year without a copy for the foreign-exchange bank, the Central Import Commission has provided [?] the following procedure:
If the duplicate of the import permit, after partial [?] use, was sent back by the customs office to the Ministry of Commerce, and the firm seeks to obtain a copy of the permit in order to present it to the Foreign Exchange Commission, it must submit to the Central Import Commission in Warsaw, Krakowskie Przedmieście 47, a request for the issue of such a copy. A stamp-duty stamp of 5 zł. must be enclosed with the request for each copy.
Two eventualities may, however, arise:
1) In case the goods were paid for after 27 May of this year, the firm then receives the copy without any further formality.
2) If, however, the goods were paid for before 27 May of this year, the request must be accompanied by a certificate from the territorial Chamber of Commerce, establishing that a payment was made for the goods to the foreign exporter.

A "Fine" Deed by a Group of School Youths

[Dąbrowa — court; antisemitism.] They capsized a "kayak" in which Jewish young men were sailing.
Two months ago the young men Pinchas Lederman and Icchak Glazerman [?] went out to the "Zielona" [?] in Dąbrowa and took to the water in a kayak.
This "outrage" three Polish pupils of the local Mining School could not bear, and they capsized the kayak, and the young men fell into the water.
Only by a miracle were the young men rescued. Against the "heroic" pupils a case was brought, which took place last Tuesday at the municipal court in Dąbrowa.
A Christian woman appeared as a witness and described the danger that had threatened the Jewish young men. On this basis the judge transferred the case to the Sosnowiec district court, since the punishment the pupils face lies beyond the competence of a municipal court.
On leaving the court, one of the above-mentioned "heroes" threatened the complainants. The judge reacted to this on the spot and ordered him arrested.
The judge's order was carried out at once.
Meeting of the Katowice Kehilla Bodies

[Katowice — kehilla; "What's new in Upper Silesia?".] Last Wednesday the kehilla council and the board held a lengthy joint meeting, at which the building plan for the large kehilla house was finally resolved upon and approved.
Council president Dr. Meir announced, under the 1st item of the agenda, the following communications: 1) The leader of the delegation to the English consul, Rabbi Chameides, remains in contact with the consul in connection with the handing over of the resolution on the Arab terror and on the stopping of aliyah.
About the important role of the esteemed rabbi in this action we shall yet have occasion to write.
2) At the "Słuchsztern" [?] public school for Jewish children named after Berek Joselewicz, Prof. Golechower [?] has been engaged as head in place of the hitherto non-Jewish head.
3) The kehilla was invited to take part in the festive reception for General Rydz-Śmigły; the delegation consisted of the presidents Messrs. Meier, Abrahamer and councillor [?] Eng. Zmigród.
4) The Katowice resident Mrs. Berta Widger bequeathed to the kehilla a 40th part of her fortune, i.e. three thousand zł.; and the kehilla allotted one hundred zł. to the volunteer firemen.
On the last and important item: [the building ?], Eng. Schneider of the building firm Korn gave detailed explanations of the building plans laid out concerning the premises and halls — which, by the way, have already begun to be built — and thus the plan provides, among other things: 6 school rooms and teachers' rooms, 10 office rooms, an appropriate rabbinate office, a beth-midrash with 385 seats for men and 265 for women, a large assembly and lecture hall for 800 persons, with a buffet and a kitchen, a mikveh and other important and useful premises.
The large kehilla house will cost up to a quarter of a million zł. The exact financing plan will be published after its approval by the voivodeship authority.
In the detailed discussion the following councillors (parnassim) took part: Wassertheil, Adv. Dr. Breiter, master-builder Szalsza [?], Eng. Zmigród, Besser, Pres. Altman, Dir. Klein; and then Pres. Mr. Abrahamer appealed to the parnassim and councillors [?] to set about energetically creating the great work, which will be of enormous use to the Jewish community of Katowice and a pride for the kehilla.
A. R. W. J.
Gang of Swindlers Insured Dead People

[Katowice — crime.] The police in Katowice have come upon the tracks of a new large insurance fraud, in which 7 persons are involved. The fraud was organised by the residents of Baryna [?] M. Uralf [?] and Leon Buchalik.
The gang fictitiously insured against death, with a German insurance company, people who were no longer alive, for large sums; afterwards they presented to the insurance company false death certificates of the insured, and in this way collected the insurance money.
The whole matter seemed somewhat suspicious to the management of the insurance company. An investigation was therefore conducted, and it did not take long before the whole fraud was uncovered. The gang of insurance swindlers was then arrested.

A Compromise Proposal on Tenant Protection for Business Premises

Thanks to the efforts of the economic organisations to neutralise the decree of the President of the Republic concerning business premises, a conference took place on Tuesday under the chairmanship of the Deputy Minister of Finance, Mr. Lechnicki, in which there took part: a representative of the Ministries of Justice, Trade [and] Finance, of the Warsaw Chamber of Commerce, and of the house-owners', Jewish and Polish merchants' associations.
After a lengthy debate the following resolution was adopted: if a dispute arises between a landlord and a tenant and the landlord demands an eviction, the matter must be handed over to the district court for decision; the court in turn is given the right to postpone the eviction for a definite time, that is, for 2 years.
Besides this, if the tenant has invested a certain sum in the premises and it has not yet been amortised, the landlord will have to meet him with a definite monetary compensation.
Both sides — the representatives of the economic organisations and of the house-owners — signed an undertaking that contracts must be concluded between landlords and tenants when renting premises. It cannot be permitted that a tenant be suddenly evicted from his premises; this is especially impermissible in cases where the tenant has made special investments in rebuilding the premises, reckoning on staying there a longer time.

Jewish Life in Zagłębie and Upper Silesia

[Zagłębie and Upper Silesia — review of the year; article.]
L. Szpigelman.
(A short summing-up of the past year.)
And so [?] a year has passed, and we have to draw up a balance of the past twelve months. And involuntarily, without even giving ourselves any account, the question at once arises: are we able, can one at all stop and count up the troubles and calamities that the Jewish people is going through all over the world, beginning with Hitler-Germany and ending in our own homeland, where we have shown so many wonders [?]? Would that not mean once again repeating sad chapters of misery and want, of brokenness and decay, which hold sway over us all over the world? Are we then in a position to present all this to you here anew? And if so — if we were to make an effort and bring to life before you the cruellest crimes committed against us only because we are the weakest — will that ease your distress? Will it make our heart lighter, the heart that is so strong and bears everything?
Why rummage through pages of grief and pain when they are not even finished yet, when people are still "passing judgement" [?] all around us and are busy with one thing only: how to annihilate us and wipe us off the world arena?
And then — remain in despair? Drop our hands helplessly and say: no, we have no more strength to suffer, we are exhausted and can no longer defend ourselves? That we must wait until "the world" sees our righteousness and then comes to the conclusion that not only do we bring no harm, but that, like every people, like every human being, we too bring benefit? That is too long a distance for a people such as we are, all the more so because justice and honesty, compassion and decency have capitulated completely.
The tactic of dropping one's hands and waiting for a better tomorrow would mean resigning not only the future but also the present, for that is no reckoning at all for a people that lives and acts in life. We must prove to the world that we have the right, like every people, to live where we are and wherever we are citizens.
• • •
What did life look like for us in Zagłębie and Upper Silesia in the course of the last year? What did the economic and living conditions between us and our neighbours look like? Of course, in former times the question would not have been asked at all, because from time immemorial we lived with our neighbours in the friendliest relations. In business it made no difference: whoever suited one, from him one bought. When making a business transaction nobody demanded to know [?] — to be shown the passport, and nobody looked at the nose to see whether it was, God forbid, not a Jewish one, which caused [?] one to mark [?] on the shop, at least for the sake of appearances.
Our Endeks [National Democrats], however, did not content themselves with the "quiet" economic pressure, and began to go at it by storm. The antisemitic hate-"literature" kept on growing, and it was spread through town and village. Posters and antisemitic slogans of the worst sort were pasted up in huge letters on the factory gates and fences, so that the eye was involuntarily drawn to read them. In Zagłębie and Upper Silesia Jews were at times "honoured" with blows.
But the lawless deeds kept on growing, until bombs began to "fly" at Jewish shops, causing no little damage.
The hooligans did not stop even at Jewish holy places, and there too they aimed with their dirty paws. Thus on the Sabbath they threw a petard [explosive] at the Pogoń beit midrash [Pogoń, a district of Sosnowiec], intending to harm the assembled worshippers, which cost the life of an unfortunate little 7-year-old orphan. Later a petard was again thrown at the Sosnowiec beit midrash, and so the hooligans keep on weaving [?], so that the hatred should flare up more and more.
It is therefore no wonder that the Jewish population is terribly nervous and at the slightest rustle people jump out of their skin. Disgust seizes one when one recalls that the Endeks sow hate and enmity.
When one picks up the local press in the morning, one is seized with horror, because we see that each of them strives to outdo the other in antisemitic sensations. The prettier the "little flowers" a newspaper serves us and the better it trips us up — in which the Jewish community surely takes no delight — nevertheless this never prevents our industrialists, merchants and doctors from pushing in there with their advertisements, which often occupy more honourable places than those of the non-Jews.
Yes, with us people like to lick the rod with which they beat us.
• * •
And Jewish life, our inner life — what did it look like in the course of the past year? What positions have we won and what have we achieved in this time? But, upon my life, it is ridiculous to put the question this way at a moment when we are plunging at a huge gallop downhill. What can we gain at a time when we have no understanding of how to hold on to what was already in our possession before? For we are losing position after position — who is even talking about conquering fresh outposts [placówki], creating new ones for the benefit of our most urgent interests.
We have grown used to saying that lawlessness takes the top place among us; now that has become too delicate an expression, so that one would need a new word that would express in its full form and meaning the general lawlessness-complex, in whose name the ugliest and most disgusting things are done at the expense of Jewish public life. Thanks to which Jewish honour sinks deep.
Jewish Sosnowiec felt struck and insulted at every step. At a time when such a kehilla was in the hands of appointees [government-nominated board] who did not understand the interests of the town: the prevailing want did not find the proper echo, the philanthropic institutions were pushed away and could hope for no support or subsidy. Public life was thus orphaned in the past year, and dictatorship ruled over the Sosnowiec kehilla life.
The new kehilla elections have put an end to the autocratic rule, and it remains for us only to hope and wish that in the new year the town will be enriched with fresh kehilla leaders who will know how to revive public life to the degree that such an "ir va-em be-Yisrael" [a mother-city in Israel] as Sosnowiec deserves.
The squabbles in the Dąbrowa [Dąbrowa Górnicza] kehilla life and the rabbi question humiliated us not a little; it went so far that the kehilla president and the rabbinical candidate appeared in court, where one accused the other of wanting to take a bribe.
Precisely these lawless deeds give the Zagłębie press no little courage to carry on antisemitic agitation against our "good deeds", which we bring upon ourselves.
On the other hand we simply took delight in the backward and moribund town of Zawiercie, which understood the great and responsible tasks of its kehilla representation, which chose kehilla leaders from among itself without elections, and therefore no elections took place. Such a phenomenon is, for our many sins, simply unbelievable. Apparently everything there has already been "smoothed out" and there is nothing left to argue and quarrel about — otherwise it is a riddle...
Be that as it may, Zawiercie deserves a "yishar koach" [well done], because at the given moment it broke the record of unity and unanimity, in which one no longer believes;
we in Będzin, on the other hand, were degraded in the course of the past year at every step: economic life has died out, become impoverished, the masses are powerless and broken beyond recognition, and there is no one to help them and lend them a hand. The public institutions, the economic ones, which ought to have come here to the aid of the masses, have been drained [?], and the boards do not bother to render an account and a report.
As for the kehilla affairs, it is indeed beneath the dignity of every decent person to speak of the ugly things that happen there. It is enough if we relate that the entire "activity" of our leaders consists of one long chain of informing [denunciations]. They are already sinking so deep into this "holy" work that one time the "Aguda" [Agudat Israel] goes and informs, and another time our national Jews do the same — who at the same time speak proudly of national honour... And from the first as from the second side it is done openly and freely, in public, as if one were fulfilling a religious mission.
We weep and complain about the antisemites, that they embitter and impoverish our lives — well, against them we have no remedy. We defend ourselves according to our means; but how much more it hurts us that we beat ourselves, that from our own ranks so much filth and infected disease is brought in — for this we have no remedy? Shall we tolerate it thus incessantly?
• * •
The Jewish situation is thus all round a bitter and an extremely serious one, and with this the last link [?] of the year 5696 is closed.
But we wish to enter the new year with the hope that at least in our own ranks, among Jews themselves, there will no longer reign so much corruption and darkness, and that prospects will appear for a finer, better and more ideal life for the whole community of Israel.
At the Bedside of the Old Year

[Feuilleton — Rosh Hashana; satire.]
By Ts. H. Rubinshteyn.
The year 5696 is at its last gasp; its end is expected any minute! A new year, a certain 5697, is already ready to take its place!
The great "calendar doctors" concede that 5696 will no longer rise from its sickbed, and that its last minute will come at the latest today between Minha and Maariv..
We are informed by confidential sources that the Jews are very pleased that 5696 is departing into eternity, and it is said that as soon as the old year breathes its last, people in all the synagogues will strike up[?]: "Barkhu et Adonai ha-mevorakh" [Bless the Lord who is blessed].
The truth must be told: 5696 was no great success; on the contrary, it was a great failure in every detail: whatever it touched came to no good, its every step brought death and devastation.
And if it fell to my lot to draw up an account of the year 5696, I would have the deceased laid out before my eyes, covered with a black cloth, so that the dead need not be ashamed, and I would say:
"Dear 5696! We stand here with heads held high at your open grave, which history has dug for you. Tonight, when Jews spit during the afternoon 'Aleinu', your soul will already be floating between earth and heaven. With a smile on their lips the Jews accompany you on your last journey; they are most pleased that your reign is over.
"When you were born a year ago, we placed a little hope in you, but you went the same ways as your father and your grandfather and your great-grandfather. You did not introduce a single reform, you did not ease the lot of the Jewish people, you did not lift a finger [lit. 'did not put your hand in cold water'] to make our situation in the world easier.
"And therefore the Jewish people does not mourn your death; on the contrary, we go to your funeral with a cheerful heart, and we hope that you will be forgotten and erased from our lives, for in a black hour you came and in a black hour you are going.
"Go to your rest, 5696, and have a bright Gehenna..."
• • •
Enter 5697!
The king is dead, long live the king!
5697 is the name of the new year that is arriving. This evening, right after the burial of the father, the crown prince, 5697, will ascend the throne. Young and inexperienced is 5697, but he has a political sense, and he will probably look for a way to smile at the Jewish people, and he will surely promise good fortune. If only he is given a fine reception in the synagogues on today's Rosh Hashana. All new years like a fine reception. They want plenty of tears, competing "U-netaneh tokef"s, and cantorial "La-El orekh din" — majestic and with pomp! A Jewish new year wants to be granted all the attention; it enjoys having all the shops closed in its honour, and having all the rabbis busy themselves with it, preach sermons, deliver moral admonitions and soften Jewish hearts. A Jewish new year begins with tears and ends with Selichot, and in the middle it wants lamenting Omer-counting days, weeping "Three Weeks", besides, of course, the long fasts and other such "festivities".
And we Jews promise everything. Some of our promise we keep and some we don't. On average, though, the years have nothing to complain about us; on the contrary, we always have good reasons to complain about the years that come and go.
We greet 5697 with the same "alas" in our hearts with which we greeted his father and his grandfathers; we give him a broad "Shalom aleichem", but we demand of him that he immediately set about making order and give the Jewish people a new gift, some kind of thing that would work a little better...
Among the other demands that we put to 5697 we wish to mention here only the most important points, but from these points not a hair may be taken away.
We demand:
1) The Almighty shall make good His promise from Mount Sinai, when He terrorized us with thunder and lightning and pushed[?] the Torah upon us.
2) The Land of Israel shall be handed over to us for real, and we shall not be bluffed with "homeland" phrases and empty declarations.
3) Streicher shall live long — but in a concentration camp of a truly free Germany.
4) A livelihood!...
5) A livelihood!...
6) A livelihood!...
7) A livelihood!...
Of these few points we will concede nothing, and we warn the new year: "Keep your promise!"...
• • •
Have a good holiday and a good year.
A Year of Life (Reflections)

[Rosh Hashana essay — reflections; opinion.] P. Blumenrajch (Częstochowa [?])
Years have the same luck as children. One child, for instance — months before it looks upon our world, the mother is already surrounded with trembling care. She is guarded like a Hasidic bridegroom on his wedding day. She moves — according to medical law — but slowly ("pavolye"), as though glass had been spread under her steps.
She wears out the doctor, torments the maids, gets nervous at everyone around her, but everything is forgiven her: no wonder — something great is coming into the world!
And when the little soul arrives, in a lucky hour, into the world — only then does the real commotion [?], noise and pampering [?] begin: one time it is too hot in the house, another time — too cold; it seems that it coughs, the little head is crooked, the little ear sticks out. They read magazines and debate with other women. They weigh the child before eating and after eating, and, stuffed with "knowledge" from the magazines like a pomegranate, they find each time other frightening [?] suspicions and illnesses, God save us...
That is how one deals with one child.
But there is another mother in the world. She sits all day in the market and warms her frozen hands at the coal-pot. She too is about to have a child. But who remembers her? She drags the peasants by their coat-tails and swears by body and life, works hard and bitterly, with worries different every day, bows before the sequestrator [tax distrainer], weeps before the naczelnik [district official], rises before dawn, toils without end, and in the meantime — the soul comes into the world.
The mother, after sitting at home for a few days, puts a sugar pacifier into the little one's mouth and runs back to the market to trade and talk with the peasants.
When the child chokes with crying in the heat, loses [?] its little rag and cannot manage with its helpless little hands — the mother is haggling with a peasant woman, swearing, and trembling to earn [?] the groschen.
The child [unclear word]. [unclear word — perhaps: falls], is sick with scarlet fever, cannot stand on its little feet, and meanwhile a second one comes, and so round again: the piece of sugar, [unclear word] and the like.
So it happens with years too. There are years that are quiet, wealthy, rested, fat. And there are years like the poor child: sickly, one plague chasing the next, one misfortune the next.
* * *
We, the children of today's time, are "blessed" too much with the sickly years.
Once, so that we should not be too bored, Providence brought in an event of larger scope. But that happened once in years. And sometimes with a pause of several decades.
Even in the stormiest period of the last centuries there was a pause between one bigger event and the next, during which one could rest...
Some examples:
From the French Revolution to the self-coronation of Napoleon, 5 years (1789—1794); from the coronation to the final defeat "behind" Waterloo, 11 years (1794—1815). Later, to the Paris Commune, 33 years (1815—1848). From the first to the second Commune, 23 years (1848—1871). From the Franco-Prussian War to the World War, 43 years (1871—1914).
With the Polish people, from the first uprising to the second, 33 years; the further great attempts at freedom 42 years later (1830, 1863, 1905), and so on, and so on.
We live, unfortunately, in a different time. In one year we live through so much that is stormy that it is hard to draw up a balance.
Take the last year.
There was a country, an independent one. In area three times as large as Spain and twice (and more) as large as France.
A country with thousand-year-old traditions, with a population of 11 million five hundred thousand people, heroic, freedom-loving — and within months they were enslaved in the name of civilization [Abyssinia/Ethiopia].
By the way, it went with this country as with Sholem Aleichem's "Yikhusl" [?]. They just wiped its little nose until it swelled: they applauded the Negus Negesti [Haile Selassie] in the League of Nations, warmly welcomed him in London, wrote about his little dog, from which he does not part — and the country of 2,120,400 sq. km passed to those who spread civilization by bomber planes and who hold the idea of permanent peace to be nonsense and alien to their spirit (from Mussolini's speech at the latest manoeuvres).
Still [?] under the impression of this great event, a noise reaches us from another side. Our relatives, the Arabs, with all their kingdoms, imamates [?] and sultanates, such as Hejaz [?], Nejd [?], Yemen, Mesopotamia, Egypt, Oman, Aden etc., cannot agree that Jews should settle in the tiny Land of Israel.
And those who grew rich through Jewish money, and those who think they have a monopoly on truth — kill with bombs, murder children, shoot at nurses, lay mines with all their Oriental doggedness, with all their Oriental zeal, self-sacrificingly, fanatically, in the name of puffed-up ideas.
And further: just so, in the middle of reading the said sad news, a fire flared up on the Pyrenean peninsula.
And here it is worth giving some details about that country.
One recalls [?] on this occasion something of the events of this stormy state, which already in ancient times produced the Roman emperors Trajan, Hadrian, M. Aurelius, the great writers Seneca, Lucan, Quintilian etc., and which from the 8th to the 10th century was the centre of learning. (The caliphate, founded by Abd al-Rahman in the year 755 in Córdoba, became a focus of learning and art.)
In this land of Inquisition and torment, already in the year 1833, after the death of Ferdinand VII, a fratricidal war broke out between Ferdinand's daughter Isabella, who was supported by the liberals, and her brother [sic] Carlos, on whose side fought the clergy and the conservatives.
Isabella defeats her brother in the year 1839. But the hot-tempered and combative Spaniards throw her off the throne — she who had changed the constitution in a monarchist [?] spirit.
In 1869 the new constitution is adopted, which establishes freedom of religion.
But the country does not rest. There comes the dictatorship of Gen. Prim, later a year of republic (1873—74). After that the rule of Alfonso XII, after him Alfonso XIII, who abdicated in the year 1923 [sic].
The country still does not rest; there come the dictatorships of Gen. Primo de Rivera, Gen. Berenguer, victories and setbacks of the people, up to the present civil war.
And hundreds of thousands of brothers fight among themselves; the Foreign Legion is used to kill their own brothers, they shoot with dum-dum bullets, they carry out an execution of 1200 workers at one time. And Spain, the land of rich estate-owners and the poor peasant, the tormented, starved land, bathes in blood, as [?] a free life has to be fought for.
* * *
"Let us come like a peddler and reckon…" [?] (Aramaic tag)
Is it at all possible to enumerate all the troubles, catastrophes, misfortunes that we have lived through in the past year?
But let us end with consolation (such is the custom): we can compare our past year to a poor child that, not only [?] is it poor, it is also sick, may it not befall you, all the time.
But just as out of a poor child there often comes a decent person ("Take heed of the children of the poor"), perhaps out of the present great chaos too something luminous will hatch.
Let us hope!
Our Educational System.

[Essay — education; Rosh Hashanah.] By Dr. M. Immergls [?].
Every living creature that moves upon our planet has been endowed by nature with an organ that serves it for self-defence. Only man has in this respect been wronged by nature: he stands defenceless before the armed enemy. But here his reason, his spirit, comes to his aid, giving him the ability to master the animal world. Between the Jewish people and the nations of the world, it seems, one can observe the very same relationship as between man and the animal world: in every generation, in every age we have stood defenceless before our enemies, on whose arbitrary will our existence depended, before enemies whose purpose in life was the destruction of the Jewish people. But our spirit managed to keep us on the surface and not to vanish with other peoples, of whom only architectural remnants have remained.
Our spirit — that is the weapon with which we defeat our enemies, and prophetic was the thought of Yohanan ben Zakkai to ask of Rome, instead of a political or territorial concession, a concession of Yavneh.
Our spirit is the spirit of truth and righteousness, which is as necessary an element for life as air and water, and precisely[?] for that reason the bearers of this ideology are also immortal. But the spirit is only the soul of the people, and the soul too must have its tikkun, must also have its body — and that body is the masses. And a body that is to correspond harmoniously to so lofty an ideology must be educated accordingly. It is not enough merely to belong to the Jewish people in order to have the right to identify oneself with the spirit of our prophets. The mere label is not enough; there must also be content, and this person of the masses must be created, must be educated. We must bring the masses, with their countless ideologies, onto the platform of the Jewish people, of the people of the prophetic spirit of righteousness and truth.
But unfortunately a chaotic state reigns in our educational system. Our youth is far more instructed than educated, and instruction as such, without education, aims rather, it seems, at an individual, material preparation[?] for the struggle of life. Instruction without corresponding education is a disintegrating[?] element. We must above all educate our youth (especially in a time of despair and hopelessness) toward a collectivist-national outlook on life inwardly, and toward correct, dignified conduct outwardly; for if unity has as its positive result the strengthening of our power of resistance, correct and tactful conduct outwardly has as its result the weakening of our enemies' power of attack. And we Jews in particular must devote more attention to the factor of social education, for all Israel are responsible for one another. Correct, non-provocative conduct in the street, in the café, on the train and the like — these are trifles among us to which, unfortunately, we pay no heed, but our enemies blow them up to all the winds and make a kind of "Protocols of the Elders of Zion" out of our smallest and most innocent misstep.
A little less arrogance in speech and in manners, a little less showing off[?] in public, a little less high-flown boasting out loud — a little more consideration for one's fellow man, all the more so when that fellow man is one of those who seek only new arguments to reinforce their slanderous accusations against us. Besides instruction, the Jew must [?] be educated to understand life and to adapt himself to it properly; the Jew should not be a mere label but also content, not merely a beard but also a Jew, also a human being. But unfortunately here again there is a "but": we do not have the educators, for the main education is the girsa de-yankuta — the education we receive in our childhood years — and the educators, or better said the women educators, are lacking. The education of our daughters is lacking, and their education as future educators in particular must be given more consideration by our pedagogical corps (if such a thing exists at all), for "the education of the sons depends on their mothers"; and for this purpose our Sages ordained the reading on Rosh Hashanah of "And the Lord remembered Sarah", as well as the haftarah of "Hannah", in order to draw attention to the absolute[?] necessity that the mother herself must take on the education of the child and not blindly entrust it to strangers. "For in Isaac shall seed be called to thee — the seed of Abraham must be educated like Isaac, who was brought up by Sarah and not by Hagar"; and thus too is praised the good upbringing of the prophet Samuel by his mother Hannah, who is mentioned so many times in the haftarah.
If we want to have a Yavneh that will cultivate our spirit and form an elite, and if we want to have educated women educators capable of raising a new type of person — a whole person, an ethical person, who will not judge everything in life from an individual point of view but from the general national standpoint — a person with a sense of responsibility; that is, when we have a unified, conscious leadership and a unified, conscious mass, our prestige in the Diaspora will be strengthened, our enemies' lust for attack will be weakened, and the framework for a future Jewish state will be created.
A Prayer.

[Poetry — Rosh Hashanah.] By Sh. Shaynboym [?].
In my heart a prayer wove itself:
hidden deep, like a dreaming spring,
it sprouted forth like a fresh green tuft,
warmed by a gentle ray of spring.
The doors of my heart burst open —
and sent out my prayer like a white dove;
upon my lips a praise hovered toward You,
but Your heavenly gate was shut. God!
I thought my pearl-tear
would roll to Your footsteps —
and like a new-born sun
my song would rise to You...
I hoped my heavy groan
would ring out like the sound of bells
and like a music full of magic
song would ascend to You...
Again I stand in submission before Your throne[?] —
my head is bowed, my heart barely stirs,
a white prayer surfaces trembling within me;
God! Reveal to me but one spark of Your holiness —
and I shall fall with a smile upon Your threshold,
and be swallowed up in Your eternity...
