No News on the Front

[Eretz Israel — correspondence.] (A correspondence from Eretz Israel.)
Matek H'mp'l [?].

That our government has committed, and is committing, a whole series of mistakes in its tactics during the present bloody events is already a well-known thing. The Yishuv drew the government's attention to its incorrect conduct and more than once pointed out "the dangers that could arise from the many mistakes, but unfortunately the hope of the Yishuv remained a voice crying in the wilderness: the government continues its method to this day, 5 months after the events, which have still not managed to free the authorities from their error.

One of these mistakes was the constant conferences with the Arab leaders, with whom the government began to negotiate right from the start, and presumably at our expense. True, the High Commissioner more than once spoke quite sharp words to the leaders of the murderers and called on them to liquidate the strike and the terror, stressing that the government would in no case yield to physical force and acts of violence and would suppress the uprising with all the forces at its disposal if they continued their cruel crimes. The "leaders", however, listened quite calmly to the High Commissioner's quite sharp words and did not fulfil his wish, and the High Commissioner in turn did not keep his own promise... The Arabs continued their terrible deeds with more courage and more cruelty, while the authorities, on the contrary, showed less energy and less strength.

The government cannot or "will not introduce order in the country; it cannot or will not put an end to the blood-game, and instead of a "strong hand" it turns even now — 150 days after the events — through various mediators to the "command" of the murderers, asking that it consent to grant peace to the country. Such negotiations have already taken place through the mediation of Emir Abdullah of Transjordan, but they produced no positive result because of the great differences of opinion that prevail among the Arab leaders. There are two camps among them: moderates and extremists. And the zealots, headed by the Mufti, hold sway over the camp. The Mufti's followers have cast terror upon their own people and declared: "Whoever is not with us — is against us", killing among themselves dozens of people — let the murdered "president" [mayor] of Hebron be mentioned — who were among those content with little, who walked the paths of settlements and compromises.

Now the negotiations have been renewed through the mediation of the Foreign Minister of Mesopotamia [Iraq], Nuri Pasha, who also met at first with difficulties, above all from the Mufti, who says that one must go on fighting until all the Arab postulates are fulfilled. Nuri Pasha declared that from lengthy talks with government circles it had become clear to him that if the present attempt at negotiations also fails, the High Commissioner will suppress the "putsch" with far harsher means than hitherto, and that within 7 days. One of the means will be: handing the country over to the authority of the military. At the same time the Arab delegation returned from London and advised the Mufti to give up the strike, because in London the bitterness against the Arabs is growing on account of the cruel acts of terror and the attacks on the military. The Mufti, having no choice, agreed to negotiations, which are indeed now being conducted with great vigilance [?].

The leaders grow more insolent from day to day, seeing the weakness of the government, and push forward ever more new demands. They are no longer content with the conditions they put forward immediately after the outbreak of the events: stopping immigration and restricting land purchase; rather they demand more and more: Arab independence, abandonment of the Mandate, a national Arab government, and declaring all the Jews who came into the country after the World War to be aliens, strangers... The government replied that it cannot consider all these demands, since the matters concerning Palestine policy in the future lie within the competence of the Royal Commission, and at present the government cannot adopt any decision on these questions.. The Arab mediator, too, has confined himself to the urgent demands only, putting off the others to another suitable hour, and is now occupied with the questions of closing immigration, dissolving the concentration camp at Sarafand and releasing the Arabs arrested during the events.

In these negotiations we Jews were bypassed, passed over in silence and not included. As though no Jewish Yishuv and no Jewish people existed. It is clear that the dealing is done at our expense and that we will be the victim of this diplomatic bargain. The dangers of stopping immigration, even if only a temporary suspension, hang over our heads. Stopping immigration is against the Mandate, against the Jewish people, and a reward for the murderers who have soiled their hands with our blood. The Yishuv warns the government at the last hour, before the fatal step is taken, that suspending immigration under the pressure of terror will entangle the authorities in a tangle of extreme Arab demands that the government will be unable to fulfil, all the more so within the framework of the Palestine Mandate. Does the government think that peace will come to the country when it stops immigration?! There will be no peace when the authorities close the gates of the country, when the authorities leave the weapons in the hands of the murderers, when the inciters can go on inciting and when the murderers can roam about freely, without trial and without punishment. At such a dear price, with such a dear payment, the government will not buy peace, which would be a "peace, peace, when there is no peace". The whole Jewish world must now concentrate around our leadership; all forces must be mobilised; we must set up a great protest movement; we must go over to the offensive, to a hard struggle, in order to repel the evil [?], the grave betrayal, believing in the victory of our great cause, for the Eternal One of Israel will not lie.

•

Strangely does our government act during the bloody months. On that cruel day when, in the colony of Kfar Saba neighbouring my own quarter, 4 Jewish workers were murdered as they returned from work, the authorities released 25 Arab inciters who had been under arrest in the concentration camp at Sarafand. It is said that this manifestation is connected with the "oy-garde" [?] and the negotiations I have already mentioned above. May this kindness the government has shown not, God grant, take its revenge on us, for we have already had time to feel its first fruit. A leading inciter from Jaffa, soon after his release, published an article full of enthusiasm for the fight against us. He writes: "Between us and the Jews there is no understanding whatsoever. The Jews must return to the sea that spat them out; the Jews are of evil character and are not worthy to live with a cultured people"... The government is silent. Comment — superfluous.

•

The authorities know where to look for weapons, and they know who is a danger to the country. Hear this [?]: Tel Aviv is a danger to the country, and among the inhabitants of Tel Aviv weapons are searched for... Almost every night there is shooting at the northern part of Tel Aviv, at the "Exhibition" [the Levant Fair grounds], at the houses of the streets bordering the Petah Tikva road; almost every night bombs are thrown at the quarters of the Jewish city — and weapons are searched for among Jews... The Arab press cries that the Jews provoke themselves (a well-known claim...) in order to blame the Arabs; that the Jews actually attack "peaceful" Arab passers-by, and that even the bomb that was thrown from the train in Herzl Street is a Jewish work... The authorities apparently believe all this, and to satisfy them, "round-ups" [obławy] are carried out in Tel Aviv in search of weapons. It is not enough that the government does not arm the Yishuv and does not legalise the Haganah — it robs us of the smallest possibility of resistance, protection and defence.

The authorities are consistent in their deeds. After the barbaric murder of the 2 Jewish nurses in Jaffa, the government extended the curfew ["state of war"] over that city of slaughter to a full 21 hours a day. The Yishuv was sure that the authorities were at last taking energetic steps against the murderers, but the very next day the District Commissioner of the Jaffa district lifted the intensified curfew from Jaffa and... imposed it on the Jewish quarters of Tel Aviv. The Yishuv was astonished: what happened? What has occurred? And the government replied: because of acts of terror on the part of the Jews against their Arab neighbours!

Not only the Tel Aviv quarters do the authorities place in one row with the murderers, but also a Jewish quarter in Haifa, "Ahuzat Herbert Samuel". In a lane of this quarter a dead Arab woman and two seriously wounded Arab men were found. The authorities are "sure" that the murder is a Jewish act of revenge, and conducted the investigation in that direction, and although there is no proof whatsoever, they fined the quarter 250 pounds. We presume that the Arab woman, a seller of "vegetables" and therefore a "strike-breaker", fell by an Arab bullet, for the events know many such facts. But the government hastened to announce that the murderers are Jews. Let us even accept the assumption that a Jew committed the murder — then he did it in his own name, on his own responsibility, and he was not sent by anyone, but driven by despair and pain, and in such a case one cannot blame an entire Jewish community and put it on one level with Arab villages and towns that have been stained with Jewish blood. All the facts cited serve the government: it wants "equilibrium", it wants to show the world that in Palestine a civil war is going on, mutual attacks, and that both sides, the Jews as well as the Arabs, are guilty of the spilt blood and murder. Where wars take place between religious communities it is hard to establish peace... Such libels does the government commit against us; thus it robs us of trust in its conscience [?], thus it undermines its own honour — and does England really want us to become altogether disillusioned with her?
The „Old One's“ Baggage

[Zagłębie — satirical feuilleton for the eve of Rosh Hashana; kehilla.] (An erev-Rosh-Hashana conversation). By Ben Amotz.

No sooner had I opened my eyes at dawn today than the old year was already standing there, dressed, wrapped in a fur, ready for the road, and around him — no end of packed suitcases.
— What's the matter with you, old fellow [„altitshker“]? Are you leaving us already? And what have you got in the suitcases? — I ask.
— In these suitcases I am carrying my baggage — he answers curtly.
— Your baggage? What are you talking about? God forbid, have you lost your mind already, heaven save us? You came to us poor[?] and naked, as your mother bore you, and the times we had with you — may they be said of all the enemies of Israel; surely you remember what we lived through in your time, which I needn't tell you about; we bathed in a sea of troubles, and in the end it turns out that you actually did not do badly in business — you are going off with such baggage, so many packed suitcases. May one know, old fellow, what is in the suitcases? Perhaps after all the troubles of last year?
— Troubles? — he gave a sarcastic smile — it is not troubles that are in the packs; these are the gifts you received from me during my stay with you. Well, would I be so tactless[?] as to take back the gifts I gave you?
— Then what on earth is in the suitcases? Perhaps the literature of the last kehilla elections in Sosnowiec and Dąbrowa? If so, be so kind as to unpack it right back, because we will need it for Będzin, for the coming kehilla elections.
— Don't talk nonsense — the old man interrupted me — you still have such sweet dreams in your head, that elections will take place in Będzin; first there must be rabbinical elections.
— But what do you have in your suitcases after all?
— You really want to know? — he had already become a bit nervous — go ahead[?] and open them.
With that he tossed me a bunch of keys, and I set to work.
I open one suitcase — the deficit of the Sosnowiec kehilla commissioner, in black and white.
— Old fellow — I turn to him — you want to take Fenger's[?] deficit with you? No, such a document must remain with us, because we are confident that he keeps on working his schemes; he will grab his way back onto the chairman's seat...
I open a second suitcase — the minutes concerning the investigating commission in the Będzin kehilla and concerning the „title“ that the kehilla chairman received from the chairman of the kehilla council..
— You old fool, have you gone out of your mind? You want to take such minutes away from us? We need them for history, as a memento of the democratic kehillas..
— Nonsense — he says with a smile — you'll soon have a „sond“ [sąd — a court case] about the events, so you'll have a fine memento...
I open a third suitcase — hush! Packed in it is a little piece of merchandise, an antique, I tell you: the name of the eighth parnas [kehilla board member], who out of „conviction“ voted for Shlomo Yitzchak Rinski...
— Leave that here — I plead with him — it will surely come in handy for the further votes that the Agudah wants to push through...
He did not answer me, only shook his head for „no“, and afterwards he said:
— The Agudah will push everything through with today's[?] „Kaiser“...
And so I opened one suitcase after another, came across quite a few „current“ articles, until I reached a big trunk.
— And here? — I ask.
— The tombstone of the Pogoń „martyr“ Rosenblum.
At this I lost my temper.
— Unpack the trunk at once! It's a mistake to take the tombstone along!
— They're not putting it up yet — he answered coolly — it will take long enough, because the lad is no party comrade whom one must hurry to immortalize...
I was left speechless and already wanted to take leave of him, but suddenly I remembered something.
— Old fellow! — I say — you have so many suitcases with you, take along one more; I'll give you a few Jewish informers to take along, so that the „ushandn“ [probably Polish urzędy — government offices] won't be so swamped with Jewish denunciations...
But instead of answering me, he heaved the baggage onto himself and vanished...

In Honour of Rosh Hashana.

[Humour section “Der Kokh-Lefl” — Rosh Hashana poem.] “Der Kokh-Lefl” [The Cooking Spoon] — humour and satire. Compiled by Amotslo.
Leonidas.
As a child plays with buttons,
counts them and strings them on a thread —
so sits and counts and tallies [?]
his years — the son of man.
White, black, red buttons —
“Here you are, Chaim, here you are, Berl!
Eleven — sixteen — ninety — thirty —
look — a whole ‘string of pearls’!”
Children sit — children of men —
with pensive old buttons
and pull the thin thread
and tally [?] the buttons.
And the children rejoice
with the little bones and the bits of tin
and they delight in the buttons
and even in the little holes...
Rejoice, rejoice, you big small fry,
it is only a game — this life.
Whether brass or gold, the plaything —
it was given only for play.
True, often a cause turns up:
something like a little magic sword
makes a “cut” into the thread —
and scatters [?] the “string of pearls”...
But this too is only a game
for the Creator and Founder.
Children play with buttons
and H e plays with the children...
Dear children, dear Jews,
a new year has come.
Pull up the new button —
may the game agree with you.
Play nicely and quietly and earnestly —
then Father will not spank you,
and the thin thread of life
will not [?] tear for a long time yet.
The Blowing of the Shofar.

[Humour section — Rosh Hashana; satire on the summer holiday.] The sound of the shofar reminds the wives of the signals that the train gave them at the dacha [summer cottage], announcing the bad tidings that Satan — the husband — is arriving.
Then it was:
Min ha-metzar [“from the straits”] — cramped and nasty,
because the husband had written:
Aleinu le-shabe’ach — I’ve already come to the spitting [allusion to the custom of spitting during Aleinu].
—o—
“Der Kokh-Lefl” Wishes
To all our sworn readers, men and women, to the dozors [kehilla board members], communal workers, elected and defeated parnassim — we wish a good “kibitzed” year [pun on “a good blessed year”].
The Modern Unetaneh Tokef.

[Humour section — parody of the Unetaneh Tokef prayer; commerce and kehilla.] How many shall pass away — many communal workers will crawl down [?] from their little seats this year.
And how many shall be created — and many “wreckers” will be created, who will take over their little seats.
Who shall live — who will make a living from other people’s money.
And who shall die — and whom the sequestrators [bailiffs], the wife and the creditors will do to death.
Who at his end — who has already made an end and handed in his trade licence to the “Uszagr” [?; apparently the tax office, Urząd Skarbowy].
And who not at his end — and who still struggles and cannot come to any end.
Who by water — who will have to suffer from watery lectures.
And who by fire — and who will be helped by a fire.
Who by earthquake [ra’ash, also “noise”] — who will be driven mad by his own household.
And who by plague — and who will suffer from a plague of protested bills of exchange.
Who shall become rich — who will become a new magnate.
And who shall become poor — and dark it will be for the poor man when he comes to such a magnate to ask a favour.
Who shall be brought low — which of the once-great firms will become canvassers [“propagandists”].
And who shall be raised up — and a lad, a nobody, will be raised up to a big firm...
Leib Stabinski.
Khatskele Klabonik Gives a Sermon about Rosh Hashana.

[Humour section — mock sermon in garbled folk (Galician-style) dialect; Rosh Hashana.] Dear congregation [“aklal”], here we already have Rosh Hashana, akhes [?], tsmaysn rekh [?], and on Rosh Hashana I have not given you any speech [?]. On Rosh Hashana it is the custom [?] to wish the rich “a good year” — such a man am I, that everyone sends me [?] roughly to his father’s father [= to the devil], but on Rosh Hashana I would [?] Samael [?].
But today [?] I cannot hold back [?], I mean to say something, congregation, comrades, fellows from the “Apromtshe” [?] and from the “Bikevige” [?], considering that tonight is Rosh Hashana.
Rosh Hashana is a holy festival. Everyone goes into the synagogue to pray for a good year, that you should not be insolent [?], that on Rosh Hashana you should not go for anybody and not loaf about [?] on the Old Market, but go into the synagogue, and you will hear the cantor with the choristers sing Unetaneh Tokef.
So [?], dear fellows, I wish you all “a shone toyve” [printed “ashune droybe”] for the new year; come all of you to pray, when the shofar is blown, and we will go to Tashlikh at Meshibikh’s [?] meadows.
Therefore [?] may we have a good year and may we be healthy.
The Old Mahzor According to a New Commentary

[Humour section — parody of the High Holiday prayers; taxes and commerce in Zagłębie, kehilla.] Benyele says that this refers to every present-day merchant whom the assessment commission has assessed and slapped with the real portion of turnover tax [“obrotowa”] — he is obliged to submit an appeal, which must be written “exactly” according to the following text:
Hineni he-ani “mamesh” [“here I am, the poor one”] — I have already become an ex-hatmaker [pun on “mi-ma’as”/“mamesh”], “really”, from the various rents [?] and taxes that they keep tearing from me.
Nir’ash ve-nifchad [“trembling and afraid”] — I am thrown into a fever when I see that the “One enthroned on praises”, and the chief culprit for the high assessments, is none other than Israel — one of our own, mi-shelanu...
Bati [“I have come”] — I have come with the appeal to the Urząd Skarbowy [tax office] to beg for mercy, that for my sake at least in instalments, asher shelachuni [“who sent me”] — the “nakaz” [payment order] that you sent me, because she-eini kedai [“I am unworthy”] — the kittel [?] is already worth nothing and I cannot even stand on my feet.
Yitgadal ve-yitkadash — it is getting close to the point where I shall have to say Kaddish de-Rabbanan after my shop.
Adam yesodo me-afar [“man’s origin is dust”] — this refers to Zagłębie commerce, which already lies nine ells deep in the earth.
U-khe-chalom ya’uf [“and like a dream it flies away”] — this refers to the promises of the new dozors [kehilla board members]; the voters may now boldly dream about them.
Lo yitamu [“they shall not end”] — this refers to the fair sex, who never become “older” — they keep getting younger.
The Silent Prayer of the Head of the Kehilla.

[Humour section — parody of the High Holiday Amidah; kehilla.] U-ve-khen ten pachdekha ve-eimatekha [“and so put Your fear and dread”] — upon the so-called investigation commission.
Ve-yira’ukha [“and they shall fear You”] — and let them be afraid to tell
about all the deeds that I have done.
Ve-tikva tova [“and good hope”] — there will be a hope that it will pass off peacefully.
Simcha... ve-sasson [“joy and gladness”] — only then will there be real joy.
U-tzmichat keren [“and the flourishing of the horn”, keren also “capital”] — and I will keep the capital and not have to hand over percentages [interest] from it.
Ve-khol ha-rish’a ke-ashan tikhle [“and all wickedness shall vanish like smoke”] — all the bad will go up in smoke.
Ta’avir memshelet zadon [“remove the rule of arrogance”] — and the Zionists, with “Tasn” [?] Liher at the head [?], will not have succeeded in removing me from power.
Ve-timlokh [“and You shall reign”] — only then will the “registering” [?] rule really get going.
Yimlokh le-olam [“He shall reign forever”] — and never again will anyone be able to overthrow him.
Ve-yeda kol pa’ul ki ata pe’alto [“and every creature shall know that You made it”] — despite the fact that it was known, and I gave the “wyjaśnienie” [explanation] to the “Burushes” [?].
Ki ata yetzarto [“for You formed it”] — that I created dates on the minutes [?].
Ki ata solchan [“for You are forgiving”] — our dear little Jews will forgive and everything will be forgotten.
With a Full Mouth.

Le-shana tova tikatev [“may you be inscribed for a good year”]. This is a tart [?] wish, short and sharp, but not from “the tip of the tongue” — rather with a full mouth.
• • •
Melekh elyon and melekh evyon [“supreme King” and “pauper king”] — many former “supreme kings”, people who stood at the highest rank, became “pauper kings”, great beggars, in the past year.
• • •

• • •

[Humour — "The Cooking Ladle"; for Rosh Hashana.]
The wisdom of a Będzin merchant.
A local partnership firm was in a tight spot. Sitting over the balance sheet, one partner asks the other:
— What do you reckon is best to do?
— I'll become a cantor? — the second partner replied.
— What does that mean?
— I'll call together the creditors, I'll wait until there is a minyan, then I'll stand facing them (like a real cantor) and begin to recite "Hineni he-ani". The only difference is that when a prayer leader [?] says "Hineni he-ani" it is heard only in the synagogue, and when I say "Hineni he-ani" it will be heard all over Zagłębie and in Łódź too.

From the Haftarah.
"And she was in bitterness of soul" [1 Samuel 1:10]. Hannah was grieved and lamenting, she had no children. Today's Hannahs weep and lament when they do have children.
Lejb Stobiński.
In the Tangle of Life.

[Serial novel — "In the Tangle of Life"; instalment 11, conclusion.]
(A novel with dramatic events in Kraków, Zawiercie and New York) (11
Some time passed and Thelma did not see Emma. Once Thelma talked it over with Arthur.
Arthur answered her:
— Emma loves me, she is no deceiver! She cannot spend time with you as before, knowing that she loves me.
— Are you drunk or out of your mind? — Thelma stared at him.
— That's how it is, Thelma, that's life! I love Emma and Emma loves me!
— But you are so much older than she is! You could have had a daughter like her!
— To Emma that makes no difference!
— And the fact that you are married to me? — Thelma could no longer hide her jealousy.
— I'm sorry — Arthur answered her — but we will not stay married long. I have long wanted to tell you: I have decided to go and live with Emma.
At these words Thelma fainted.
Arthur barely brought her round and put her to bed; Michael called a doctor, and it turned out that Thelma had fallen seriously ill; day by day she grew worse, until she suffered a paralytic stroke.
Arthur was badly shaken by the event; he kept justifying himself to Michael.
But more than anyone, Emma was shattered. She suffered terrible pangs of conscience; whole nights she could not sleep and kept thinking how to make amends to Thelma.
At last she made a decision: she would tell Thelma that her whole love for Arthur had been a mistake.
That very same day Emma came there and at once set to work — to nurse Thelma.
When Bernard heard the news, he went straight to the Sanders' house and found Emma at Thelma's sickbed.
This time, though, Emma received him better than ever, [—] told him she was happy that he had come.
When she had finished her tasks with the patient for a while, she went out with him into another room.
— You should know that I have left school; I am staying here with Thelma.
— As you see fit [?], Emma.
— But that is not all. I must talk to you about John.
— What is it with John again?
— He is bombarding me with letters, he threatens me that if I do not marry him he will commit suicide. Bernard, I want no more tragedies on my account! There have been tragedies enough, both with my parents and with me myself; what shall I do, Bernard?
— When he comes, I'll see [?] to do something.
— Good, Bernard, I know I can rely on you. I give myself into your hands for my whole life.
And tears appeared in Emma's eyes, tears of love and gratitude.
Bernard was happy; although he was in a house of illness and misfortune, it was already clear to him that he had finally won Emma.
Bernard now often came to Emma, who was at Thelma's house day and night. Several times he tried to speak seriously with Emma about a future together, but she kept putting him off.
— We have waited so long, let us wait a little longer.
And he waited patiently.
But once something quite extraordinary happened to him.
Bernard travelled to Montreal, Canada, on business, and there he met a pretty young girl named Hilda Schwartz.
Bernard liked the girl very much, and a few days later Hilda Schwartz came with him to New York.
Bernard took Hilda to a hotel, went to Emma, told her about Hilda and added:
— She is lonely here, she needs someone to go out with her; I'll introduce her to John. She is pretty, clever, cheerful — a girl with every virtue; perhaps he will fall in love with her.
It was not long before John came on his daily visit to Emma. This time she received him very nicely and invited him to drive with her and Bernard to meet Hilda; he gladly came along.
Hilda made a very good impression on John, and she liked him too.
At the beginning of June 1925 three — or, more precisely, three and a half — weddings took place: Bernard with Emma, John with Hilda, Sasha [?] with Michael (who had converted to Judaism and was now called Abraham), and a half-wedding of Arthur with Thelma.
Thus ended a stormy drama of two generations.
(The End).
First meeting of the newly elected councillors in Sosnowiec — an agreement between the camps of Rabbis Englard and Hager

[Sosnowiec — community.] As we have already reported, the first meeting of the newly elected councillors (parnasim) of the Sosnowiec kehilla took place in accordance with the election calendar.
The purpose of the meeting was to elect the electoral commission, which conducts the elections to the new kehilla board.
12 councillors took part in the meeting (Dr. Maladiecka [Mołodecki?] and Herman Kliner, who is in Rabka, did not come).
The kehilla commissioner, Mr. Stancer[?], opens the meeting and proceeds to the only item on the agenda — the election of an electoral commission.
The result of the vote came as a surprise to some of the councillors, who had not yet known about the “peace”[?] between the camps of Rabbis Hager and Englard. Five councillors were elected to the commission, 3 from Rabbi Englard’s list and 2 from the national[?] camp, namely: Yosel Meisels, Shlomo Dalisman, Chaim Rancziger[?], Yitzchak Steinfeld and Bernard Jasny. Mr. Yosef Meisels was elected chairman of the commission.
“The street” immediately snapped up the sensational news, and people wished one another “mazel tov” on the “peace” concluded between the two camps, which have been fighting for 7 years already.
The “peace” made a heavy impression in Agudah circles, where no one had believed that such a thing could happen. As we are told, on the Sabbath in the Ger[?] shtiblekh it was “cheimlikh”[?]; a protest meeting against the “peace” was to have been called, but for certain reasons the meeting did not take place.
The “official” circles deny the “peace.”
In connection with the rumours that peace is being concluded between the above-mentioned rabbis, we turned to the “official” persons, who explained to us that for the time being the peace rumours are still groundless — but what the future will bring, no one can yet know.
“And the agreement over the electoral commission?” we asked.
“That is merely a ‘coincidence’.”
The position of the Zionist Organisation.
On Sunday the committee (va’ad) of the local Zionist Organisation held a meeting at which the Organisation’s position toward the newly created situation in connection with the “peace” negotiations was discussed.
On this question the chairman of the Organisation, councillor Dr. S. Maladiecka, took the floor and stated that he is aware that negotiations are being conducted about it, but he is taking no part whatsoever in them.
After the discussion the line for the future was laid down, which envisages creating a kehilla majority that will conduct a normal and just kehilla administration in the spirit of the Zionist Organisation.
How Zagłębie yesterday welcomed the 23rd Regiment returning from manoeuvres

[Będzin — army and municipality.] Yesterday evening the 23rd Regiment returned to Będzin from the autumn manoeuvres. In this connection, on the initiative of the Będzin municipal administration, a reception committee was formed, which includes the municipal administrations of Będzin, Sosnowiec, Dąbrowa and Czeladź as well as various institutions and organisations; at the head of the committee stood the town president, Mr. Iwiórczyk[?].
The 23rd Regiment arrived in Czeladź yesterday at 6.30 in the evening, where the entire reception committee was assembled. At the Upper Silesia–Czeladź border the troops were greeted by the starosta, Mr. Baksa[?]; the orchestra of the “Saturn” [mine] played the national anthem.
A second reception took place at 8 o’clock on the Małobądz–Będzin road, where President Iwiórczyk gave the greeting.
Later a banquet was held in the officers’ casino.
Electric light will not be cut off during the holidays

[Będzin — municipality.] On the strength of the intervention of alderman (ławnik) Mr. Rubinlicht with the director of the municipal power station, we draw attention to the fact that the electric-light bills which are payable on the eve of Rosh Hashanah may be paid until Monday the 21st of this month. During the holidays the electric light will not be cut off.
Pledges from Rosh Hashanah until after Sukkot belong to the Sosnowiec free-loan fund

[Sosnowiec — charity.] There are institutions that rattle the collection box all year round, and there are those that come once a year with the cry — help!
To the latter belongs also the Gemilut Chassadim (free-loan) fund in Sosnowiec. Although its expenses have grown by nearly 2000 zł. a year because of the “revenge” of the kehilla commissioner, the board has not come to the public with a call to help through material efforts in order to keep the fund in existence.
Income is raised only now, through the pledge (nedarim) campaign proclaimed every year from Rosh Hashanah until the end of Tishrei.
Therefore everyone who is called up to the Torah during this time should bear in mind that the free-loan fund does not belong among the various little societies that one dismisses with “two morsels”[?]; rather, it is the only “Sosnowiec” institution that carries a heavy burden — the livelihoods of hundreds of merchants and craftsmen.
So pledge with a generous hand, and thereby fulfil the verse “And if thy brother be waxen poor… then thou shalt relieve him” [Lev. 25:35]...
“Beit Lechem” for the coming holidays

[Będzin — charity.] Despite the difficult financial situation of the “Beit Lechem” society in Będzin, food products will be given out to a large number of needy people for the coming holidays.
This, however, depends on the support of the Jewish population, which must support with a generous hand the traditional “Pidyon Nafshi” campaign of the “Beit Lechem” society.

Bronisława Chimczyk [?] of the village of Nierada, wishing to get rid of her first-born child, threw it to the dogs.

The head of the registration (residents' registry) department at the Będzin magistrate, Mr. Czałek [?], is retiring these days.

Mr. Makower, to whom the Sosnowiec kehilla owes a debt of nearly 2000 zł., has imposed a sequestration on 30 etat (kehilla tax) payers who owe larger etat sums.

A 14-Year-Old Girl as Leader of a Gang of Thieves.

Maria Kowińska [?], 14 years old, organised a gang (szajka) of thieves who engaged in stealing in shops. The division of the loot was carried out by the 14-year-old Kowińska.

League for Human Rights in Zagłębie Dissolved
[Sosnowiec — organisations.]
For quite a long time a branch of the League for Human Rights, with its seat in Sosnowiec, has existed in Zagłębie.
By order of the municipal starosta in Sosnowiec the League, and also the Freethinkers' [?] Society, are being dissolved.

A Horse Fell into a Well.
[Będzin — incident.]
In the yard of the Będzin mill on Kościuszki Street there is an old, disused well, which is covered with boards.

The French Minister's Visit to Zagłębie Called Off.

[Sosnowiec — economy.]
On Monday the French Minister of Commerce, Bastid, accompanied by Minister Roman, as well as senior officials of the French and Polish Ministries of Commerce, was to have been at a conference in the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec.

Spread Counterfeit 50-Złoty Banknotes.

[Sosnowiec — crime.]
The Sosnowiec police have detained a certain Franciszek Szymczyk [?], who engaged in spreading counterfeit 50-złoty banknotes in the Upper Silesian and Sosnowiec area.
The Owners of “Seats” in the Będzin Synagogue Must Come to Pray All Year Round...

[Będzin — synagogue.]
On Sunday the committee of the Będzin synagogue held a meeting, at which, among other questions, the question of the possession rights (chazaka) of the “seats” in the synagogue was dealt with.

Delegates to the International House-Owners' Congress.

A Parents' Meeting at Public School No. 2.

A "Subscribers' School" in Zagłębie

[Zagłębie — post and telephone.] In the coming days a "subscribers' school" will operate at the post offices, where everyone will be able to learn how to use the automatic telephone sets.
The lessons will be given at the post offices of Sosnowiec, Będzin and Dąbrowa.
She Wanted to Buy Shoes.

[Sosnowiec — crime.] An elegant lady came into the shoe shop of the "Delka" firm in Sosnowiec and asked the shop assistant for shoes.
In the meantime the "customer" stole socks and vanished.
These days she stood trial before the Sosnowiec district court, which sentenced her to 3 months' unconditional imprisonment.

In Honour of Rosh Hashana

Leonidas.
As a child plays with [—] [—], counts and [—][?] them up [—], rocks and counts and counts [—] few years — the [—][?], [black?] threshold of the [new?] year, [for] besides the [usual one?] — according to the calendar, we have [another?] time-reckoning: it is already half a year since the riots broke out in Eretz Israel, as dark forces of the desert rage and want to destroy our work of building.
In the last two decades the Yishuv in Eretz Israel has already withstood many bitter trials, but never in the course of that period was the attack against it so organised, so wild, so prolonged.
The Yishuv stands in the front line of the struggle, and the lower ranks of the people will have to come to its help. So that we do not come out defeated but, on the contrary, stronger, more steeled[?], more self-reliant, so that the enemy will no longer [be able to] raise a hand.
• • •
The bloody events have confirmed anew that the power of resistance does not depend on political factors alone, but depends also on our development in the country and on the roots we strike into the soil. The Yishuv understood this well, and therefore did not let its hands drop for a single day. Under hails of bullets and the crash of bombs, the building wo[rk] goes on [...]
Commission elected to conduct the elections to the kehilla board

A few days ago a meeting took place of the newly elected dozors (kehilla council members), at which an election commission was chosen to conduct the elections to the kehilla board.
The election commission consists of Messrs. Meir Eisenberg, Prez.[?] S. B. Nalman[?], S. Bekerman, Prez.[?] Sternfeld and S. Leichter.
Mr. Meir Eisenberg was elected chairman of the election commission.
Jewish jeweller refuses to buy stolen goods and hands the thief over to the police

[—][?] An unknown Jew came into the shop of the jeweller Nusberg[?] in Jędrzejów and offered Nusberg various gold and silver articles at ridiculously low prices. Nusberg, realising that the articles came from thefts, called the police, who detained the said "merchant".
It later turned out that the "merchant" is a known thief, his name is Moshe Braun[?] of Wodzisław, who had recently carried out a series of thefts, among them[?] he had also robbed the Worowicz[?] family in Wodzisław.
[—] the Threshold of the New Year.

[Palestine — Rosh Hashana article; Keren Kayemet and Keren Hayesod.] …[the building] work [goes on] feverishly. The exhibition in Tel Aviv; the aid for the 10,000 refugees from Jaffa — aid that consists not only in feeding them from day to day, but in rebuilding their lives, making useful people of them and putting them on their feet for their own good and for the good of the whole people; the organisation of guarding[?] and security; the arming of thousands of young Jews with official consent — all these are works that have been carried out, or are being carried out, in these present hard days when death lurks from every corner. The Yishuv knows now where its strength lies; the Yishuv knows with what to defend itself.
• • •
And one more thing: more than ever the Yishuv now realises what the national funds mean for the country. The work of the Keren Kayemet and the Keren Hayesod has gone on in recent months as it should. New settlement points have sprung up, and in the old points new people have been added, because of... the immigration, which in the first half-year alone brought in 16,257 immigrants, of whom a sizeable part went to the village, and also because the disturbances caused unemployment in some branches of work in the towns. On Keren Kayemet land in the Zebulun Valley hundreds of workers are working. In some places they are searching for water — and finding it too. In many points new houses are being built.
This is only a short survey. What the national funds are for the Yishuv, and how beloved they are by it, mute figures can perhaps testify. In the course of the first half of the year 5696 Palestine took third place in the list of Keren Kayemet revenues: first comes America, then England, and after England Palestine, with a sum of 21,667 pounds. Palestine comes even before British[?] South Africa. Palestine sees with its own eyes what the Keren Kayemet is for it, and therefore knows how to appreciate its work.
And therefore our answer must be: rapid work for the redemption of new tens of thousands of dunams, in order to create wide tracts of national land in the country. This is the greatest moral of the events of recent months. It must be done soon. There are still possibilities, and we must not put off until tomorrow what we can do today.
The whole people must now unite in this task. It is now for us a question of life. The Yishuv now stands in the firing line. It makes heavy sacrifices not only for itself but for the whole people, and its call to the people on the threshold of the new year is:
— Land! More and more land!
More land for the Yishuv, for immigration. More land in order to take root, to fortify ourselves and to prevail.
A. Beilin.

[Kielce — humour; a "piyyut" for Rosh Hashana.] A Mahzor for Kielce. A piyyut for Rosh Hashana.
Who says what:
The Chmielnik hasidim together with the Chęciny hasidim, in honour of the victory in the kehilla elections:
"And so the righteous shall rejoice..."
A defeated dozor [kehilla board member]:
"For I am a sinner and transgressor..."
Meirlekh[?] with "paks zganies"[?]:
"You know the secrets of the world..."
Shmuel Zelig with Yechiel Yeshaya:
"Man's origin is dust and his end is dust..."
The merchants, house-owners and the People's Bank:
"But a destitute 'king'..."
The kehilla officials:
"And You count and number, and decree the 'allotment' for all Your creatures..."
The sick, to the "Linas Hatzedek":
"Turn us not away empty-handed..."
Today's communal workers:
"I am unworthy in deeds and lacking in understanding.."
Insurance agents:
"Who by water and who by fire..."
A merchant about the Jewish "vitserp"[?] in the Treasury office:
"Trembling and afraid for fear of Him who dwells..."
Today's "city providers":
"Although I am not worthy and fit for this..."
Evicted tenants:
"[Lodging][?] in the shelter of the shade..."
The "plitshnikes"[?] to the creditors:
"Wound[?] and fracture..."
Dozor Leichter:
"May my prayer come before the 'Throne'..."
The leaders of the Merchants' and Small Traders' Association:
"Stop the mouths of our accusers and prosecutors..."
The Sokołów hasidim, who this Rosh Hashana will pray in the gmina premises:
"Holy congregations shall sanctify..."
Today's youth:
"To multiply[?] his seed like the dust of the earth and his offspring like the sand of the sea..."
A secretary in a well-known Jewish institution:
"I alone shall reign for ever and ever.."
Newly-risen war-rich men:
"And every mishap, and every quarrel, and all kinds of calamities..."
The writer of these lines:
"Today You shall bless us!..."
Mordechai.
Storm damage in the Kielce voivodeship amounts to five million złoty.

[Kielce — agriculture; storm damage.] The Kielce "Izba Rolnicza" (Chamber of Agriculture) has just established that the damage to the fields caused by the hurricanes and storms in the Kielce voivodeship amounts to about five million złoty. 23,791 peasants in 540 villages have suffered.
